title: MATREX VR manual
text: MATREX VR connects measured animal movement to controlled visual environments in Unity. Use this manual to operate an existing experiment, understand the path from a tracker packet to an LED viewport, interpret saved data, or extend the source. The manual describes the 0.3 software and the current source. Sections for modern native tracker decoding and the live browser bridge are explicitly marked as source updates after 0.3; those changes do not retroactively appear in the stable 0.3 downloads. The standalone application, this documentation website, external trackers and analysis tools have separate responsibilities. Documentation updates do not change an installed application or publish a new software release.

title: Follow one experiment through the system
text: Describe it. The system file assigns hardware, tracker endpoints and rig identities; a sequence selects scenes and experiment files. Configure it. The studio edits those same JSON documents. Opening a default or an unknown field does not rewrite the experiment. Run it. MainController loads the selected scene or advances a compatible scene in place. The scene controller applies stimuli and tracking behavior. Present it. ClosedLoop and manual/autopilot controls update rig poses. ViewportSetter maps the allowed camera faces to configured display rectangles. Retain it. Recordings preserve animal poses, supported virtual populations, the consumed configuration graph and generated sky provenance. Inspect it. Telemetry monitors the running process; replay reconstructs supported recorded evidence on a shared timeline. An animal is the real subject providing movement input. An agent is a virtual, mirrored or replayed individual. VR1, VR2, and other positive VRn names are routing identities, not animal names or species.

title: What is included
text: The compact desktop build includes ControlScene, Choice, Choice_desync, Choice_Selwyn, Swarm, Kannadi, Optomotor, TerrainCueLab, Rugosity_RS and ReplayScene. Optional forest/tree environments remain in source and must be enabled in a custom build. The scene guide distinguishes a controller family, a particular authored environment and its JSON recipe. Kannadi — ಕನ್ನಡಿ — means “mirror” in Kannada. It presents a matrix of mirrored animal poses across a hexagonal arrangement. The Kannadi section explains visibility and replication; it is more than an isolated animal model.

title: Coordinates, units and timing
text: Unity's world uses +X right/east, +Y up and +Z forward/north. Positive yaw turns +Z toward +X. Walking and rugosity scenes use centimetres; Selwyn/migration terrain uses metres. Keep scene scale, tracker input units and physical moth dimensions distinct. Presentation and rig logging follow rendered frames. They are not an independent hardware acquisition clock. The input contract identifies raw tracker units; the run's archived JSON records the actual gains and scale. Read data formats before converting recordings into physical quantities.

title: Evidence and limits
text: The site links the actual runtime source and saved validation reports. Synthetic captures show the software's rendering, not a live animal session. Accelerated repeated-load checks establish behavior in their recorded workload; they do not prove that a long physical acquisition session or the historical Unity crash is resolved. Hardware checks and lifecycle evidence describe those boundaries. For a citation, use the software citation. For ready-to-run applications, use the existing OS downloads.

title: Getting started
text: Choose an operating-system ZIP from GitHub Releases, or use the download website. Extract the whole ZIP to a writable location. Keep its application, data folder, Unity libraries and START-HERE.txt together. Players run without Unity Editor or Python.

title: Launch and configure
text: Windows: open the .exe. Its adjacent _Data directory and DLLs are required. macOS: open the .app (universal Apple silicon/Intel package). Releases are ad hoc signed but not notarized; use Finder's Open action and the corresponding Privacy & Security option if macOS requests it. Linux: open the .x86_64 player in a graphical desktop with a compatible graphics driver. If extraction loses the executable permission, restore it in file properties or with chmod +x. The bundled HejjéTrac binary requires glibc 2.39 or newer; use an independently verified compatible external tracker on older distributions. Read the version's included START-HERE.txt. 0.1 starts on the historical metadata form, with a manual-start Choice_Selwyn sequence. 0.2 retains the Config UI Test branch's automatic seven-condition TerrainCueLab sequence, 30 seconds per condition. Press Escape to return to Control, or launch with -configure to enter setup immediately. These version defaults are preserved for provenance. For example: # Linux (replace the filename with the downloaded player's name) "./MATREX VR.x86_64" -configure # macOS (replace the path) open "/path/to/MATREX VR.app" --args -configure 0.3 opens setup by default for a fresh profile (autoStart: false). 0.4 opens its hardware-free demo/configuration home for a fresh profile. Existing user sequence flags remain authoritative. The 0.4 release section records publication status and known limits. In the studio, System config describes hardware, Sequence config arranges experiment blocks, and Experiment configs edits each referenced stimulus. Session cards describe the real animals; VR1, VR2, etc. remain hardware routing identifiers. Set tracker endpoint/mode, sphere diameter and display layout for your actual apparatus. A supplied public system template opens the application; it does not calibrate an LED array. Choose closedLoopMode: "Kinefly" for the historical flight yaw-rate input. FicTrac walking uses its separate cumulative-displacement contract. System examples and input/data documentation describe the difference. A tracking publisher is needed for closed-loop motion, not for browsing setup or using configured manual controls. Use Initialize tracking to open the independent tracker and inspect input/calibration while setup remains open. This does not start an experiment or create its pose recording. Then use Save setup and Start experiment. Review Save tracker video before initializing the tracker; a recorder started with video enabled can already be recording during preflight. Auto start controls the next launch. Escape returns from a run to Control; Escape from Control exits the standalone player. Each studio-started experiment gets a separate recording directory.

title: Configuration and data locations
text: 0.4 keeps editable configuration in a writable user profile and recordings beside each installed player. The application seeds missing files into Config on first launch; updating the application never overwrites existing files. The recording library shows the actual recording root and lists its completed sessions. Environment Configuration Recordings Editor Assets/StreamingAssets Assets/RunData 0.4 standalone, writable player directory Application.persistentDataPath/Config MATREX VR RunData beside the app/executable 0.4 standalone, protected installation Application.persistentDataPath/Config Application.persistentDataPath/Installations/<installation-id>/RunData Archived 0.3 standalone Application.persistentDataPath/Config Application.persistentDataPath/RunData 0.1 / 0.2 Windows/Linux <application>_Data/StreamingAssets <application>_Data/RunData 0.1 / 0.2 macOS <application>.app/Contents/Resources/Data/StreamingAssets <application>.app/Contents/RunData Unity's profile root normally lives under %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\<Company>\<Product> on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/<Company>/<Product> on macOS, or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/unity3d/<Company>/<Product> on Linux (usually ~/.config/unity3d/...). Company/product names come from the build's Player Settings. The application can also use explicit absolute roots: "./MATREX VR.x86_64" -configure --config-dir "/path/to/my-config" --data-dir "/path/to/my-runs" system_config.json is the hardware file; sequenceConfig.json contains ordered blocks. Each block's parameters.configFile identifies its experiment relative to the configuration root; parameters.design identifies a Dynamic Choice design. Preserve referenced subdirectories and data files. Templates and examples provide complete files. Back up existing editable configs and run folders before switching versions. To retain 0.1/0.2 configuration, copy its complete tree to a chosen writable directory and use --config-dir. Use --data-dir to continue a previous recording root, or Browse… in the replay library to inspect old shared application-support recordings. The application does not move earlier runs or silently replace their files.

title: Controls
text: Focus Game/the player. Metadata text entry suppresses experiment hotkeys. Keys / gesture Action R Reset tracked rigs to the active experiment initial pose. P / O Toggle tracked translation / yaw. Arrows / gamepad left stick Manual translation, if enabled. A / D; gamepad right stick Positive / negative yaw. Ctrl+Space Toggle active experiment forward autopilot; steering and reverse remain available. Shift+Up/Down Adjust manual translation speed by 1 per press. Shift+W/S Adjust manual turn speed by 1 degree/s per press. C / Z Vertical motion if allowVerticalTranslation is enabled. W / S; E / Q Pitch; roll, if allowPitchAndRoll is enabled. Escape, on release Return to Control; from Control, quit the standalone player. Tab, 0.2 onward Show/hide runtime dashboard. In setup, normal field navigation. Right / middle drag inside overview Orbit / pan the operator camera. Wheel inside overview Zoom. Replay: Space Play/pause. Replay: Left / Right Seek 1 second; hold Shift for 10 seconds. Replay: N / M Previous / next recorded step. Kinefly/Bogong retains +/− yaw gain, Ctrl+Y yaw-rate mode, 1–9 selection for matching rig IDs, 0 or Next animal to cycle all configured IDs (including VR10), and held [/] DC offset. Dashboard trim controls affect the current sequence row. Optomotor owns its stimulus movement, disables autopilot, and pauses with Space/backslash. See the full Input System map for gamepad and secondary controls. For 0.4 replay, choose Replay recordings in setup to see this player’s runs. Choose Browse… for an external saved folder, or enter its path. Windows/macOS and the Editor use their system folder dialogs; Linux uses zenity/kdialog when available, otherwise the path input remains available. Standalone OS-level folder drag/drop is not implemented. See replay.

title: Save the evidence
text: Retain the complete run directory, not only a rig CSV. New recordings include original system/sequence/experiment inputs, immutable snapshot versions and hashes, loaded external data, animal metadata, rig and population logs, runtime_trace.log, and generated Skyboxes with their manifests. Writers drain on clean exit; the original directory remains if ZIP creation fails. Rig CSVs use wall-clock timestamps. TerrainChoice/rugosity and walking scenes use centimetres; Selwyn terrain/migration scenes use metres; raw Kinefly yaw input uses radians. Interpret the exact scene and saved scale settings. Data formats, run snapshots, and replay explain interpretation and reconstruction limits.

title: Terrain recipes and current limits
text: Load one of the four Examples/Rugosity/sequence-treatment-*.json sequences for matched terrain, visible terrain with flat navigation, flat appearance with terrain navigation, or both flat. Each sequence runs the four shared TerrainChoice layouts for 30 seconds each and uses terrain-treatment.json for common settings. The two placeholder trees are equally distant from the start. The recipe uses real tracked motion, 1 cm clearance and texture scale 4; initialize tracking before starting. Both-flat trials intentionally have identical surfaces. See the four treatment files. Choice blocks expose Edit config → Available objects & materials. Under Stimulus → Objects, Type and Material controls offer names registered in that scene, preserving exact JSON values and existing custom names. Video recording currently follows the independently launched tracker, rather than acknowledged per-experiment Start/Stop commands. Finish the tracker normally and collect completed footage for replay. The linked external recorded-trajectory viewer is supported only by the reviewed Mac arm64 dashboard bundle; Unity’s internal pose/video replay remains independent. Older pinned strict flight-camera paths on other architectures remain blocked. Evenly paced 60 FPS is still under investigation. Latest standalone mouse/drag acceptance was blocked by the native automation tool; keyboard, rendering and separate Unity GUI-event checks have their recorded scope. Windows/Linux builds are cross-built and have not received native execution walkthroughs. These limits and physical calibration requirements are recorded in release verification.

title: Source and tracker setup
text: Clone the repository, add it to Unity Hub and open it using Unity 6000.3.16f1, as pinned in ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt. Let Package Manager restore the pinned dependencies. Start at Assets/Scenes/ControlScene.unity. Restart an already open Editor after pulling Input System/backend changes. FicTrac is an optional external acquisition component for walking experiments. The project's FicTrac fork includes install_ubuntu.sh for Linux setup. Follow that repository's installation instructions and confirm the publisher's units and endpoint against the ZMQ contract. Kinefly and Tirbala use their own input paths. Custom experiments require Unity scene/asset/controller authoring. Add them to the build scene list and rebuild; the packaged studio configures the experiments the build contains. Experiment workflow covers that extension path.

title: Native capability gallery
text: These previews come from genuine Unity rendering of the named source scenes and configurations. Captions distinguish software fixtures, authored environments and the compact standalone scene set. They are not photographs of an animal session or invented renderings. Choice_Forrest

title: Choice_Forrest + Landscape prefab
text: Actual Choice_Forrest rendering with the bundled Assets/Prefabs/Landscape.prefab instantiated by the capture fixture to supply ground and forest. This is a source customization, not the default scene or a compact-player preset. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Choice_Selwyn

text: Authored terrain and an automatically generated astronomical sky. The sky manifest identifies its observer location and represented time. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Choice_Selwyn

title: Terrain and a panoramic background
text: Homing-style visual context combines authored terrain with an explicit panorama. A panorama background does not define navigable geometry. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Choice

title: Choice bars
text: Configured bar stimuli in the existing Choice controller family; positions and appearance belong to the experiment JSON. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Optomotor

title: Optomotor drum
text: The rotating grating/drum path owns stimulus motion and records its stimulus parameters. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Choice

title: Stripe fixation recipe
text: A stripe/fixation configuration uses the existing controller and registered visual assets rather than requiring a separate scene per parameter. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Choice

title: Objects and landmarks
text: A configured set of object stimuli with explicit pose/appearance and the active tracking/reset choices. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Swarm

title: Locust swarm
text: Virtual agent populations rendered around an animal-controlled rig, with independent agent motion and per-rig visibility. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Kannadi

title: Kannadi — the mirror matrix
text: ಕನ್ನಡಿ means mirror in Kannada. The scene replicates tracked animal poses across a hexagonal matrix with configured self/peer viewing. Experiment JSON · Capture provenance Capture provenance identifies the native fixture, scene and configuration. Image/config hashes identify the actual files. The manifest retains an Editor startup SearchDatabase exception separately; the gallery failure field is null. No hardware collection is represented.

title: What a preview establishes
text: A capture establishes what that scene/configuration rendered in the documented software fixture. It does not establish physical LED scanout, tracker latency, photometric calibration or the perceptual response of an animal. The source/configuration/provenance links travel with each preview. The forest preview is Choice_Forrest with the bundled Landscape prefab instantiated by the native capture fixture. The additional prefab is recorded in provenance; it is not a claim that the authored scene already contains that ground/forest or that this setup ships in the compact player. Optional forest/tree environments remain available from source and require their scenes in a custom build. The current 0.4 compact application contains the fourteen documented scenes, including the four shared-world TerrainChoice variants; the gallery does not silently add a scene to an existing release. For the generated sky's sample time, location, source map and image hash, inspect its archived manifest. For terrain geometry, use the measured rugosity conditions, not a visual estimate from a screenshot.

title: Runtime architecture
text: The application has one operator/sequence layer, scene-owned experiment controllers and per-animal rigs. Tracking, presentation, monitoring and recording communicate through explicit state; they do not all run on the same worker or share a single ZMQ port. Schematic of ownership and channel direction, not a timing trace or hardware wiring diagram.

title: Ownership at a glance
text: Owner Responsibility Lifetime MainController System config, sequence order, trial/step clocks, scene transition, tracking registration, saved heading references Persistent across normal scene changes MasterDataLogger Session directories, exact consumed inputs, trace, writer-drain/archive boundary Persistent; starts a fresh session from configured setup ConfigWorkbench Session form, system/sequence/experiment editing, validation and Start Control/setup only; its panel is destroyed for an experiment Scene controller Choice objects/design, Swarm, Kannadi, Optomotor or terrain-specific stimulus application Current scene; compatible controllers can reconfigure in place Rig components Input reception, measured movement, manual movement, camera mapping and animal pose logging One configured rig in the experiment scene Night-sky controller Generated/explicit sky, activation provenance, resource cleanup Managed stimulus context Telemetry/status UI Bounded sampled diagnostics, live operator state and errors Independent of the setup panel and overview ReplayController Saved-run timeline, evidence resolution, replay views and supported environment/population reconstruction ReplayScene

title: Startup and setup
text: RuntimePaths selects the configuration and recording roots. In a player it copies missing bundled configuration files into the writable profile. Existing user files are not replaced. In the Editor, defaults remain StreamingAssets and Assets/RunData. MainController establishes its singleton, ensures that MasterDataLogger exists, reads the system/sequence configuration and registers scene-load handling. The default 0.3 sequence has autoStart: false, so a fresh profile enters the studio. -configure also forces setup. An existing user file can intentionally retain auto-start. MasterDataLogger captures the system and sequence graph before experiment loggers begin. The studio may then rotate into a fresh configured session when Start is pressed. It saves the selected documents, records their exact sources and metadata, and hands execution to the existing runner.

title: Scene transition boundary
text: MainController selects the next execution-order entry. A real scene load runs the new scene's controller, configures its rigs and applies the experiment. RuntimeRigRegistry reconciles the configured VRn identities with the authored rig template before their tracker Start callbacks open inputs. For a compatible same scene with reloadScene: false, the runner calls IInSceneSequencer.AdvanceStep(parameters). This avoids loading the scene again while still rebuilding/reapplying the condition. It does not mean that all prior trial resources may remain allocated. Population/material cleanup remains the controller's responsibility. A change of scene or an explicit reloadScene: true follows the full-load path. The scene lifecycle guide explains owned resources and the crash investigation's actual evidence.

title: Frame-side work and workers
text: Execution context Work Unity frame thread Scene/rig transforms, stimulus configuration, rendered cameras, immutable snapshot capture and most Unity object creation/destruction Tracker receive worker SUB socket, payload validation and a locked latest-sample handoff; the worker owns socket disposal Telemetry publisher worker JSON encoding and outbound PUB operations using the latest bounded pending snapshot Swarm recording worker Buffered population formatting, gzip and file writes; clean shutdown drains before ZIP creation Replay loading/indexing Saved evidence parsing/indexing; Unity object application remains in the replay's frame-side flow Do not call Unity rendering APIs from an arbitrary socket or file worker. Do not let a network subscriber back-pressure the experiment frame loop. Telemetry can drop snapshots; recordings and their dropped-frame diagnostics have their own contract.

title: Motion and experimental phases
text: ClosedLoop consumes the newest complete tracker sample and applies the selected walking or flight interpretation. Keyboard adds permitted operator/autopilot movement. Optional RugosityRig owns height/normal alignment after horizontal movement; MigrationMotion retains its specific wind/AGL role and yields where rugosity owns the pose. ExperimentPhases manages enabled preStimulus, stimulus and postStimulus conditions in one scene. Phase clocks begin after their configuration/sky setup completes. Heading windows are bounded to the scene or phase duration rather than lengthening the condition. Heading observations use the animal's virtual yaw; raw flight control input is not the measured heading.

title: Trace one failure
text: Configuration validation can stop Start before a presentation begins. A missing consumed snapshot makes the archive incomplete. Scene/phase application exceptions enter the runner's error state and report through the status overlay and trace. Telemetry bind/send failures are monitoring failures and do not certify that stimulus execution recovered. Use runtime_trace.log together with the current phase, config manifest and Unity Player log. A visible error panel records a failure; it is not an automatic experimental validity decision.

title: Scenes and capabilities
text: A scene supplies authored geometry, rig templates and a compatible controller. An experiment file supplies its stimulus/motion parameters. A sequence chooses scene/file combinations and timing. Reusing an environment with a different JSON file is usually preferable to duplicating a whole scene for a parameter change.

title: Choice objects, bars and fixation
text: ChoiceController reads complete experiment JSON and uses its registered prefab/material resources. Trials can place objects at specified positions or angular arrangements, change their appearance, and select tracking/autopilot/reset behavior. Empty or omitted object lists support sky-only terrain conditions where the parser permits them. Bars and stripe fixation are visual task recipes inside these controller families; they are not a claim of a separate dedicated scene for every stimulus. Dynamic Choice designs can sequence changes within one environment and trigger steps by their configured time/area rules. Keep per-animal step labels in the recording when asynchronous animals advance independently.

title: Swarm populations
text: Generated agents use preferred agentCount, agentSpeed and agentSpeedStdDev names while old number/speed aliases remain readable. Direction/concentration/elevation, spawn volume, wrapping, density and visual dimensions define the presented population. A generated population and a recorded trajectory file have different timing controls; playback.speed does not mean generated agent speed. The modern Bogong visual supports dot/angular modes and a physical moth representation with GPU wing motion. Recorded tracks can be anchored to each animal's world position and continued according to their recipe. See generated swarm and recorded swarm.

title: Kannadi: the mirror matrix
text: ಕನ್ನಡಿ (Kannadi) means “mirror” in Kannada. Kannadi replicates the tracked animal's pose across a configurable hexagonal matrix. The replicas are virtual agents, derived from real animal motion rather than independently measured animals. numberOfRings, hexRadius (legacy spacing) and the selected kannadiTilePrefab determine the arrangement. Per-animal vrConfigs can set initial pose and watchIndex. A specified watch index chooses a configured animal population; without it the view contains the other animal layers. Self-view handling skips the overlapping centre where appropriate. Camera masks retain shared floor/world geometry while replacing animal-layer visibility. The full matrix is a stimulus arrangement, not a second physical tracking array. A recorded Kannadi clone row identifies a visible-model root; a root can contain a mirrored band rather than one biological animal. The data reference explains the schema, and integration history retains the original validation context.

title: Night sky, terrain and panoramas
text: Choice_Selwyn and other supported Choice/Swarm/Kannadi experiments can use nightSky to orient the bundled stars/Milky Way to location and time. This is a generated texture stimulus. It does not add atmosphere, planets, the Sun or the Moon. skyboxPath supplies an explicit panorama instead. Generated sky and explicit image precedence are documented per parser. A panorama background does not define collision or navigable terrain; a terrain mesh and its scale remain separate. Homing-style environments can combine authored terrain, configured landmarks and a panoramic background without making them one file format. TerrainCueLab separates what is rendered from what controls navigation. The four TerrainChoice scenes share one prefab; four treatment sequence recipes choose matching or mismatching visual/navigation roles across all four spatial patterns. Their default treatment uses 1 cm eye clearance and texture scale 4. Matching, mismatching and height/tilt isolation conditions apply explicit surfaces; “rough” is a geometry condition, not an asserted perceptual result. Rugosity documents actual mesh samples and precedence.

title: Optomotor
text: The drum/grating path owns stimulus motion and disables general forward autopilot. Its config describes frequency, contrast, duty cycle, speed, axis/direction and tracked loop switches. Stimulus/drum transforms must not be interpreted as the real animal pose. Generated mesh/material/texture ownership matters when repeatedly rebuilding the scene.

title: Scene extension boundary
text: The studio configures experiments that the build knows how to render. New environments require Unity authoring, controller/prefab registration and build-list changes. There is no general level editor. Follow the extension workflow when the desired condition cannot be expressed by existing parameters.

title: Rigs and viewports
text: A rig is the virtual observation pose controlled by one animal. It normally contains ClosedLoop, a tracker listener, manual controls, a ViewportSetter, stimulus cameras and compatible recording components. VRn is the routing identity that connects the rig to one system configuration entry.

title: Configured rig count
text: RuntimeRigRegistry reconciles positive, unique VRn identities with the scene's authored templates. It disables omitted rigs and clones a template for additional configured identities before those rigs start tracking. Sparse IDs such as VR10 are valid; VR1 must not accidentally match VR10. Each independent stimulus population requires an isolated Unity user layer. The authored first four populations have named layers; extra populations use available unnamed layers. Capacity is finite and depends on the build's layer layout. An exhausted layout produces a configuration error rather than silently sharing a population. JSON configuration does not provision another computer, tracker or LED panel.

title: Camera-face allow-list
text: ViewportSetter is authoritative for its own stimulus cameras. It starts by disabling them, then enables only named faces listed in the rig's system displayOrder. Valid letters are D, R, B, L, F, U: down, right, back, left, front, up. Normalization uppercases, removes unknown letters and deduplicates while preserving valid order. A camera must match Main Camera <letter>. A camera absent from the normalized order stays disabled even if its prefab checkbox was enabled. A rig absent from system config renders none of its stimulus views. This protects against old serialized camera state exposing the wrong view.

title: Pixel-to-viewport mapping
text: ledPanelWidth/ledPanelHeight are pixel dimensions of one face. startCol and startRow locate its first slot on the selected display; rows count from the top. horizontal chooses whether successive camera slots advance across columns or down rows. For display width W and height H: w = ledPanelWidth / W h = ledPanelHeight / H x = (startCol + (horizontal ? slot : 0)) * w y = 1 - (startRow + 1 + (horizontal ? 0 : slot)) * h viewport = (x, y, w, h) These are normalized Unity camera rectangles, not a physical LED wiring map. Configure the actual display dimensions and verify the result on the apparatus. The camera field of view is set to 90°. Up/Down faces inherit the matching front camera's population mask, position and clipping planes so vertical faces do not accidentally expose another rig's population.

title: Physical display selection
text: System targetDisplay selects the zero-based Unity display and is applied to each rig. An invalid/missing display or nonpositive panel size leaves cameras disabled. Secondary displays are activated when needed. ViewportSetter uses Screen dimensions for display 0 and the secondary display's rendering dimensions for other displays; resolution changes trigger a layout refresh. A small desktop window can therefore produce a very small or displaced face strip if the system file still describes a full LED canvas. Use a desktop layout intentionally for inspection rather than assuming a monitor view is a calibrated arena.

title: Shared geometry and isolated animals
text: Camera culling masks combine shared environment geometry with selected agent layers. Runtime rig provisioning remaps additional-rig stimulus masks. Kannadi changes self/peer population visibility. Operator marker layers remain excluded from stimulus cameras. A layer mask is not a physical display index. watchIndex, vrId, targetDisplay and displayOrder describe different relationships; do not reuse one number for another without an explicit mapping.

title: Operator overview
text: The overhead view is an analysis/operator camera with numbered heading arrows and fading animal trails. Right drag orbits, middle drag pans and the wheel zooms inside the image. Hiding it stops its rendering/tracking work and releases its render target; it does not turn off stimulus cameras or telemetry. The independent FPS/status display can target another display. Replay's animal-view cameras are also analysis views; they do not reconstruct a hardware-calibrated LED layout merely by loading a recorded system file.

title: Source and full reference
text: ViewportSetter, RuntimeRigRegistry, six-camera reference, hardware checklist.

title: ClosedLoop and motion
text: ClosedLoop converts a complete tracker sample into movement of the animal's virtual rig. Its interpretation depends on the active walking/flight controller path, not only on the spelling of one field in the system file. Check the dashboard's effective input mode and the recorded tracking implementation.

title: Walking displacement and orientation
text: The walking path consumes cumulative ball displacement. It swaps the incoming planar axes into Unity's horizontal frame, differences successive samples and applies the reset/manual orientation reference. Multiplication by sphereDiameter / 2 converts angular ball displacement to a linear distance when the publisher uses the documented radians contract. At walking position gain 1, no extra multiplier is inserted. At orientation gain 1, one measured yaw degree produces one world degree. Wrapped angular differences use the shortest delta around 0/360. Rotation is not multiplied by deltaTime and is not smoothed toward an absolute heading by a turn-speed cap. Walking waits for a pose and freezes tracking contribution when the sample is stale. A held/stale pose is still present in historic rows; its presence alone is not proof of fresh acquisition.

title: Kinefly flight yaw-rate compatibility
text: The historical flight path preserves raw signed radians rather than round-tripping through a Unity quaternion. In yaw-rate mode, the applied virtual yaw increment is: yaw increment (degrees) = yawGain * (rawYawRadians - yawDCOffsetRadians) * Rad2Deg * deltaTime The latest value continues to integrate between packets, including the historical held-input behavior during a disconnect. That differs from the walking freshness freeze. The dashboard and telemetry expose state; they do not silently change the compatibility arithmetic. Negative yaw gains remain supported in this historical path. DC offsets persist across configured trials in the current sequence process. Use flight gain compatibility when comparing an older acquisition build.

title: Tirbala force/torque path
text: Tirbala selects the retained force/torque branch. Its channels are control quantities, not ordinary measured Euler angles. Do not label those raw rotation channels as degrees merely because the wire object calls them pitch/yaw/roll. Read the effective mode and its units in telemetry and the experiment's saved config.

title: Reset, toggles and references
text: R applies the current experiment's initial pose and restarts tracking initialization. It works without a fresh tracker. It does not change the operator's selected P/O tracking switches. P toggles measured translation; O toggles measured orientation. Re-enabling tracking rebases the appropriate reference rather than replaying accumulated disabled movement. Manual yaw also updates the displacement reference so later tracker motion remains consistent with the visible heading. Experiment pose reset flags and operator tracking toggles are separate controls. A phase/row can deliberately retain motion continuity with resetPositionOnStart and resetRotationOnStart disabled.

title: Manual motion and autopilot
text: Keyboard uses the shared Input System actions, respects the system's manualControls, and suppresses movement while the operator types into metadata. Forward autopilot uses the active experiment's autopilotSpeed; lateral, reverse and yaw input remain available. Ctrl+Space toggles the mode. It does not synthesize a tracker packet. Walking scenes use cm/s while metre-scale flight scenes use m/s. Manual operator speed, generated agentSpeed and the real animal's measured speed are different quantities. Optomotor disables forward autopilot to retain ownership of stimulus motion.

title: Terrain pose ownership
text: When RugosityRig controls the pose, horizontal motion is applied in a level yaw frame; the terrain follower supplies height/normal alignment. This prevents pitch/roll from accidentally shortening horizontal speed or adding steering. Migration wind can remain active while yielding the overlapping altitude role.

title: Flight gating and auto trim
text: KineflyAutoTrim observes distinct, fresh input samples, qualifies flight and applies the configured iterative centering only in its supported flight/yaw mode. The measured flight state, a bypass switch and trim enablement are independent. See auto trim for variance thresholds, median/uncertainty windows, current-row scope and recorded diagnostics.

title: Source and related contracts
text: ClosedLoop, Keyboard, input contract, data columns, operator controls.

title: Input contracts
text: Each configured animal rig has a ZMQ SUB input. The tracker or adapter publishes; Unity connects to the configured zmqAddress and zmqPort. The separate experiment telemetry endpoint is a Unity PUB output. Matching port numbers without matching the direction and wire contract does not make two tools interoperable.

title: Stable 0.3 JSON frame shapes
text: ZmqListener accepts a single UTF-8 JSON frame, or two UTF-8 frames containing topic then JSON. The listener subscribes to any topic. The pose object uses finite numeric channels: {"x": 0.0, "y": 0.0, "z": 0.0, "roll": 0.0, "pitch": 0.0, "yaw": 0.0} The six names identify channel positions, not universal units. The selected tracker/motion path determines the meaning. The historical Kinefly bridge sends one JSON frame; do not add a mandatory topic frame to an existing publisher simply because outbound telemetry has one.

title: Walking contract
text: Legacy walking JSON uses cumulative ball angular displacement for planar motion, in radians before sphere-radius conversion. Its yaw is interpreted as degrees through the historical Unity quaternion path. Sensor y maps to Unity X; sensor x maps to Unity Z. The configured sphere diameter is in centimetres for centimetre-scale walking scenes. Do not publish an already converted linear position or a velocity into that cumulative angular-displacement contract. The same JSON shape with the wrong meaning will produce plausible but incorrectly scaled motion. Verify a known ball movement before collecting data.

title: Flight contract
text: Kinefly-compatible flight uses signed raw yaw radians for the historical yaw-rate calculation. Unity retains raw rotations as well as a display quaternion; telemetry version 2 converts angular reporting to degrees while raw CSV compatibility fields remain distinguishable. Rekkefly is the modern flight-tracking project in this toolchain. Use its documented Unity-compatible fanout output rather than guessing that every monitoring socket has the same frame shape. Integration guide links the verified repository and launch contract.

title: Current-source native FT rows
text: Source updates after 0.3 add Hejjetrac and Rekkefly backend names while preserving serialized FicTrac=0, Kinefly=1, Tirbala=2; the new enum values are Hejjetrac=3 and Rekkefly=4. Legacy JSON is not silently rewritten. Modern flight naming normalizes to the flight calculation; modern walking selects the walking contract. HejjéTrac's native payload is one UTF-8 frame: FT, followed by exactly 25 numeric CSV fields. Counting the numeric columns from 1 after FT, forward sphere displacement is column 15, east displacement column 16, and heading column 17; these quantities are radians. The current decoder maps east to Unity X, forward to Unity Z, converts heading for the walking orientation representation, and applies sphere radius for linear displacement. This differs from the old JSON yaw-degrees representation even though both reach the walking controller. The format decoder and the native ZeroMQ transport connection are separate checks. The native source integration report received 791 input frames: 300 actual HejjéTrac FT rows, 100 mixed legacy JSON messages and 391 actual Rekkefly messages. The Rekkefly fixture processed 400 synthetic source frames; Unity and an independent libzmq subscriber each received 391 after normal PUB startup subscription delay. This is not a claim that all 400 were delivered. The report also covers 150 listener shutdown cycles with worker count returning to zero and 25 telemetry publisher teardown cycles with thread count returning to baseline. The source bundle uses NetMQ 4.0.1.13, AsyncIO 0.1.69 and NaCl.Net 0.1.13; the transport manifest records exact artifacts. This macOS no-graphics probe is not a physical camera or other-OS execution claim. The immutable 0.3 application should use its established JSON adapter rather than assuming it includes this post-release FT decoder.

title: Latest-sample handoff
text: The receive worker validates a complete message and updates position, raw rotation, converted rotation, receive UTC and a sequence counter under one lock. ClosedLoop sees one atomic sample; it cannot mix channels from two partially received packets. Samples are consumed at rendered-frame cadence. Multiple frames can consume the same input sample; multiple packets can arrive between renders. input.latest and input.consumed in telemetry distinguish reception from the sample most recently read by motion processing. They are not a lossless log of every camera frame or tracker pulse.

title: Freshness and disconnects
text: The listener records receipt age. Walking freezes its tracking contribution when stale; historical Kinefly yaw-rate integration holds the latest value. The dashboard reports source, endpoint, wire format and freshness. Operator movement/reset can still work with a stale input. When a listener component is disabled/destroyed, it requests worker shutdown; its worker owns socket disposal. A timed-out stopping worker must not be overwritten by a second live socket thread. This ownership is part of scene lifecycle validation.

title: A useful bench sequence
text: Connect a test publisher to one configured VR input and confirm endpoint and packet sequence in the dashboard. Send a stationary reference and verify no unintended world movement under the chosen gain/DC offset. Apply one known translation/yaw increment and compare actual world displacement/heading to the contract. Stop publishing and observe the mode-specific stale behavior. Re-enable P/O and reset; verify that accumulated disabled motion is not replayed. This checks the software connection. Physical camera calibration, ball slip, north alignment and LED timing require the actual apparatus.

title: Source and reference
text: ZmqListener, ClosedLoop, recorded units, external trackers.

title: Unity 6 input and movement
text: The project uses Unity 6000.3.16f1 with com.unity.inputsystem 1.20.0. Unity recommends the Input System package for new input work; 1.20.0 supports Unity 6000.3. This replaces the project-owned runtime calls to legacy UnityEngine.Input. It does not replace FicTrac with a physics character controller: the Swarm/Kannadi walking path uses measured displacement. Bogong/Kinefly uses the restored historical yaw-rate calculation; see gain compatibility. After pulling, let Package Manager resolve the pinned package and restart the Unity Editor if it was already open when Active Input Handling changed. Open ControlScene and focus its Game view. Entering text in a Unity UI or TMP input field suppresses experiment hotkeys, so typing names/comments cannot move animals or trigger reset. Assets/Resources/ExperimentControls.inputactions is the editable action map. ExperimentInput loads one shared enabled copy, so all rig components observe the same input frame. Default keyboard and gamepad bindings work together, without PlayerInput auto-pairing stealing the keyboard when a gamepad connects. Operator movement affects each rig whose manualControls.enabled is true. This is an operator console, not four gamepad-assigned players. Action Keyboard/mouse Gamepad Effect Reset R Select / View Reset all tracked rigs to current experiment initial position and rotation, even if tracking is absent/stale. Also resets an optomotor drum. TogglePosition P West face button Toggle tracked translation; not a position-only reset. ToggleOrientation O North face button Toggle tracked yaw; resuming rebases to current visible heading. Move Arrow keys Left stick Local X/Z translation. Diagonal keyboard motion is normalized. Yaw A positive, D negative Right stick horizontal Historical A/D polarity is preserved: A turns +Z toward +X. Remap in the action asset if desired. Autopilot Ctrl+Space — Toggle constant forward motion at the active individual config's autopilotSpeed; lateral, reverse and yaw input remain available for steering. Vertical C up, Z down — Requires allowVerticalTranslation. Pitch W positive, S negative — Requires allowPitchAndRoll. Roll E positive, Q negative — Requires allowPitchAndRoll. SpeedModifier Either Shift — With Up/Down: change translation speed by 1 cm/s per press. With W/S: change turn speed by 1 degree/s per press. No movement during adjustment. Cancel Escape, on release Start / Menu, on release MainController stops sequence and returns to Control. From Control, quits the standalone player. Unity Editor Application.Quit does not exit Play mode. Orbit / Pan Right / middle drag in overview — Move overview camera only. Scroll Wheel inside overview — Overview zoom. Pause Space South face button Replay play/pause or optomotor pause. Backslash also pauses optomotor. Back / Forward Left / Right D-pad left / right Replay seek by 1 second, or 10 with Shift. PreviousStep / NextStep N / M Left / right shoulder Replay jump to adjacent step marker. Debug D — Optomotor debug state in Console. Also retains D yaw when manual movement is enabled. Reset does not change P/O's selected tracking mode. Re-enabling tracking does not replay accumulated disabled motion. A manual heading change updates the displacement reference. Tracked yaw deltas add to the visible heading; they do not pull it toward an absolute target. Missing/stale sensor poses freeze the walking path but do not prevent operator controls. The historical Bogong/Kinefly path continues integrating the last yaw value. In that path, +/- adjusts yaw gain by 1 per press, Ctrl+Y toggles yaw-rate mode, number keys 1–9 select matching configured rig IDs; 0 or the HUD’s Next animal button cycles every configured rig, including sparse IDs such as VR10. Held brackets adjust that rig's DC offset by 0.5 rad/s. Offsets persist across trials and scene reloads. Negative gains remain allowed as before. Each individual experiment config file can use the Mario Kart-style autopilot. Set autopilotEnabled and autopilotSpeed in the file referenced by the sequence step’s parameters.configFile. The runtime shortcut Ctrl+Space toggles the mode. Optomotor scenes explicitly disable autopilot so the stimulus controller remains the sole source of scene motion. Scroll uses Unity 6's uniform cross-platform wheel units: one tick maps to 0.1 legacy zoom units (20 world units with the default zoomSpeed=200). Fractional trackpad motion stays proportional. UI EventSystems are upgraded at scene load from StandaloneInputModule to InputSystemUIInputModule; newly created overview UI uses the new module directly. Project Active Input Handling is Both for compatibility with unmodified third-party demo scripts (TMP examples, ant demo, free-flight texture demo). The experiment code and active UI use the new backend; Both is not double-reading operator actions. Switching to Input System Only would additionally require migrating or disabling any legacy vendor demos you choose to run.

title: Validation and bench checks
text: Assets/Editor/KannadiValidation.cs runs on a disposable project copy with a KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY sentinel. It tests queued keyboard, mouse, and gamepad events; real reset handling with no tracker; rig motion actions; UI module replacement; all current scene regressions; Optomotor startup; wind/AGL; and transitions back to normal Choice. The batch harness forces game input routing only while synthesizing events and restores the editor settings afterwards. The final run passed 918 checks with zero runtime failures; the report separately records an existing Unity Editor SearchDatabase cache exception. The report is kannadi-validation-results.json. Tests do not certify LED scanout timing, live FicTrac latency, a particular physical gamepad, or monitor mapping. For a bench check, focus Game, press R/P/O, move with arrows and a connected controller, edit a metadata field to confirm hotkeys are suppressed, hide/show the overview, and press Escape to return to Control. Compare sensor-driven displacement against the measured 2.6 cm ball before collecting experimental data.

title: Status panel and build errors
text: Tab toggles the persistent bottom-right status panel (the historical shortcut). Focus Game; it is ignored while typing in an input field. The dashboard is visible by default, refreshes every 0.5 seconds, and reports trial, scene, per-rig loop switches/gain/DC offset, Kinefly flight/trim status, input freshness, heading assessment and telemetry state. Its Auto Trim button toggles the running sequence row; see auto trim. A new error/exception automatically shows it again, even in standalone builds. Full details remain in runtime_trace.log and the outbound telemetry stream. Configure statusOverlay.visible and statusOverlay.targetDisplay in system_config.json.

title: Unity experiment studio
text: The Config UI Test integration provides a working runtime UI Toolkit experiment studio to ControlScene. Experiment execution remains inside the Unity player; Python plotting and analysis remain optional. A desktop Unity release includes the UI and its JSON schemas without a Python installation, uv, browser server, or second application.

title: Try it
text: In Unity 6000.3.16f1, choose Tools → Experiment setup → Open setup screen (Play). This opens ControlScene and bypasses auto-start for this preview without editing any configuration file. Leave Play mode to end the preview. Normal players honor the sequence's existing autoStart setting. Ship autoStart: false for a release that opens setup on double-click. -configure overrides auto-start when launching an existing player; -no-configuration-ui disables the studio for legacy validation workflows. An unconfigured apparatus opens a clearly labelled Night sky flying demo; press Start demo without hardware. Configure holds species, walking/flying mode, VR/display counts, LED dimensions, face order and tracker endpoints. Its face net and display map share the runtime pixel geometry. Save with Use this configuration; subsequent sessions put the sequence and block parameters first, retaining hardware settings separately. Initialize tracking opens the independent native tracker windows while setup stays open. Check input and calibration before Start experiment; initializing does not start the experiment or allocate a run directory. A native tracker's own video option still governs its independent recorder. Use Tab / Shift+Tab to move between controls, F1 for shortcut help, Ctrl/Cmd+S to save, and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+J to open the current JSON. Alt+1–5 selects Start, Sequence, Experiment settings, Recordings and Apparatus. Tab stays inside an open dialog. Escape closes dialogs or returns to Start; an unapplied JSON draft stays visible for applying or discarding. Session cards hold experiment name, experimenter, comments and each animal's arbitrary text ID. Species is read from system speciesName and changed in Configure, then copied to metadata SpeciesName. Sex starts at Unspecified, and an empty age remains unspecified. Each subject has its own comments, with starvation details behind the subject settings icon. These values are saved in AnimalMetadata.json with the run and reloaded when returning to setup; a transitional FlyMetaData.json copy supports old analysis. Hardware rig IDs remain the system's routing keys; the animal's Animal ID is its free-text label. Existing metadata extension properties are retained. Auto start, Loop and Randomize are direct icon buttons with explicit ON/OFF indicators. They edit the original sequence flags and are also visible in the sequence editor. Auto start controls the next launch; the current setup session starts with Start experiment. A clickable system strip shows tracking modes, panel count/resolution/order, tracking input addresses and telemetry output. A compact virtualized Coming up list shows the current sequence, effective block timing and a stimulus summary. Longer plans scroll within that list. The header opens Sequence config, System config or Experiment configs. The last lists only referenced files in the current sequence, with the number of blocks using each. Session returns to the simple screen while retaining unsaved labels, notes and config edits. Detailed editors expose full settings; More → All parameters / Edit JSON provides the complete document tools without putting them on the landing screen. In Sequence config, blocks are virtualized cards showing their config path, environment, exact effective timing and stimulus/movement summary. Use the native drag handles to reorder, the copy icon to duplicate, or the bin icon to remove a block. Click a card for its environment, outer duration, gain, auto-trim and reload controls. Gain sliders span 0–50; exact text entry also accepts negative or larger values without slider clamping. A phased config owns its timeline, so the retained outer duration is visibly disabled in the builder; it remains editable under All block settings or JSON. Add experiment block opens a searchable file library. Filter by paradigm, inspect timing/effects and phase states, then add the selected complete config in one action. Current configs, templates, examples and custom JSON are listed. The Archive category loads historical files on demand. A custom relative or absolute JSON path can be loaded from the same dialog. System and sequence files are excluded from individual block selection. The environment is suggested from the file and remains selectable from the compatible scene family. Replacing a block changes its scene/reference while retaining existing gain, duration, reload/trim flags and extension fields. Edit config opens the referenced document directly. Essentials exposes common controls; Motion, Stimulus, Sky and Tuning group the rest on the same page. Pre/stimulus/post phase tabs show their on/off state and duration. Missing optional phases are displayed without adding JSON; the explicit Add action creates them. Enabling a phase with an omitted duration inserts its displayed 10-second authoring default so it can run. Disabled phases keep their values. Native vector icons, illuminated ON/OFF switches, XYZ controls, color swatches and sliders make values visible. All parameters, All fields, and JSON retain access to every stored and schema-defined setting, including extension keys. Number entries retain their exact JSON text. Sliders are convenience ranges and never clamp a value simply by displaying it. Numbers outside a slider's range remain editable and visibly marked. Explicit slider changes use a documented step and synchronize the exact entry. Pending slider positions flush before navigation, undo, save and Start. Ports, IDs and values without meaningful slider ranges retain number entries. The run overview shows exact total timing, heading-assessment time, loop/order state and effective config effects. Sky summaries follow uniform-color/panorama/procedural precedence and distinguish live from fixed sky. Disabled or absent phases are marked inactive. System overview shows input modes, frame synchronization, display, configured camera faces, telemetry and overview state. Configs shared by multiple blocks are explicitly labelled. Make an independent copy on a selected sequence block creates a complete variation file and relinks only that block. Undo restores the original reference; the newly created file remains on disk. Save a variation in the sidebar copies the current document. Existing files are never overwritten by these creation actions. Absolute paths are supported; relative experiment/data references resolve against RuntimePaths.ConfigRoot (Editor: StreamingAssets; standalone: writable profile), matching the runtime loaders. Open a file loads a different primary system/sequence or standalone config. Edit JSON exposes the complete document. Apply a draft to synchronize the form, or discard it. An unapplied draft blocks navigation, save and start. Save setup writes changed loaded documents and a metadata draft under RunData/Backup, leaving completed-run metadata intact. Start experiment validates the active file graph, saves changes, archives a fresh session using the selected system and sequence paths, copies metadata into that new run folder, and starts the existing runner. Session metadata includes every configured VR even when subject details were not edited. Non-looping runs started here return to session setup; Escape also returns from a running experiment. The next run gets a separate data folder.

title: JSON parity
text: The editable source of truth is a Newtonsoft JToken tree, rather than a deserialized C# config object. Unknown properties and arrays remain editable. Exact number lexemes are retained, including long integers, scientific notation and decimal values beyond floating-point precision. Numeric controls use delayed text commits to avoid float-widget coercion. Missing, null, false and zero are distinct values. Removing a property restores omission; the ∅ button sets an explicit null. Missing settings show their declared runtime defaults immediately. Invalid known values show default controls with a Check JSON marker while validation continues to block starting. More → Effective JSON & defaults shows a read-only resolved document and can copy it or explicitly make those defaults part of the editable draft. Merely viewing defaults never writes them into a source file. Optional phases are not created by this view. A whitespace-only file opens with inherited defaults and becomes valid {} JSON when explicitly saved. Malformed JSON keeps its exact source for repair in Edit JSON, while the form remains available for inspecting defaults. It cannot be saved or run until an explicit JSON repair is applied. The normal .bak retains the previous malformed input after repair. A save with no value changes preserves the original bytes, including BOM, indentation, whitespace and line endings. Edited files use pretty-printed UTF-8 JSON with the original property order and preserved untouched numeric lexemes. Whitespace is not preserved after an actual edit. Duplicate property names and nesting deeper than 128 levels are rejected explicitly rather than silently losing data. Known parameters must fit their runtime types before starting; arbitrary extension numbers are preserved without being interpreted as experiment settings. External changes are checked once per second while setup is active. Clean documents reload into the form. A changed file with an unsaved local edit produces a conflict and cannot be overwritten. Copy the draft from the JSON view before using Reload disk. Each file is replaced atomically with a .bak of its previous version. Saves across multiple files are not a filesystem-wide transaction. Undo/redo keeps the latest 32 editing transactions. A block reorder is one transaction and moves the complete JSON object, including unknown fields.

title: Schema and extension points
text: Assets/Resources/ConfigurationUI/schemas.json contains JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 documents for system, sequence, Choice, Swarm, Kannadi, Optomotor and Dynamic Choice. ConfigurationSchemaBuilder generates definitions from the Newtonsoft serialization contracts used by the runtime loaders, including inherited fields, converter unions, private Dynamic Choice types, and shared phase/auto-trim fields. It regenerates before a player build; use Tools → Experiment setup → Regenerate JSON schemas after changing config types. The runtime validator implements the keywords emitted by the generator: type, enum, required, properties, items, minItems, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, and permissive additional properties. It also runs the existing production validators for cross-field rules. It is not a general-purpose validator for arbitrary third-party JSON Schemas. The generator's x-ui annotations define conditional visibility, enablement, help text, units and soft slider ranges. Compound enable rules cover pose reset plus random-heading conditions. Per-rig poses do not inherit nonexistent sibling flags. Current examples include: Kinefly/FicTrac input and flight terrain fields; walking ball diameter hides in Kinefly mode. Disabled phases, manual controls, telemetry, overview and sky blocks grey their dependent controls while retaining their enable switch and saved values. Autopilot and animation dependent settings; software FPS cap under vSync. 2D/3D swarm elevation, scene/Bogong visuals, dot/moth dimensions, world/angular sizing, recorded playback, and continuation controls. Auto-trim and flight-check tuning; time/area Dynamic Choice triggers. Inline Swarm/Kannadi sequence overrides use their scene's field definitions and conditional rules. Autopilot and heading settings stay owned by the experiment file, as required by the current loaders. Changing modes hides controls without deleting values. Disabled contents remain accessible in JSON. To add an ordinary parameter, add it to the relevant runtime config type and regenerate schemas. Existing scalar/container renderers handle it automatically. Add optional annotations in ConfigurationSchemaBuilder.Annotate for mode-specific rules or units. For a new scene/parser, register its schema type and extend ConfigSchema.ForScene; keep loading and validation aligned with that parser.

title: Performance and scope
text: The sequence board, landing-screen plan and file library use fixed-height virtualized ListView cards. The board supports native reordering. The full-field editor also mounts only visible rows. Nested objects/arrays render when opened. There is no workbench Update method. At start the UIDocument is disabled immediately and its scene-owned host and PanelSettings are destroyed; there is no configuration form, polling, or binding during the run. Setup is recreated only on return to ControlScene. Operator graphics suspend while setup is open. Tab retains setup field navigation and hides/restores runtime status, FPS, overview, desktop controls and replay controls together during a run. Calibrated LED rectangles are reserved against status/FPS/overview placement; a panel is omitted when no free area fits. Diagnostics and optional telemetry keep their separate runtime lifecycle. The UI and JSON arrays support configurable rig/sequence counts. Current source provisions configured rigs from authored scene templates before their tracking components start, and disables absent rigs. Each isolated population consumes a Unity rendering layer; exceeding the available layer capacity produces a configuration error. Hardware IDs remain VR followed by a positive integer. See the 0.3 release verification for tested scene/count combinations. Versions 0.1/0.2 retain the authored VR1–VR4 engine limit. Current desktop source uses RuntimePaths.ConfigRoot and RunDataRoot: a writable user-profile Config directory, and a recording library beside each installed player (MATREX VR RunData beside the Mac app). Read-only installations use a stable per-installation profile fallback. The Editor uses StreamingAssets and Assets/RunData. Seeding copies missing files and never overwrites a user config. --config-dir and --data-dir choose explicit roots. Versions 0.1/0.2 retain application-relative storage. WebGL/mobile storage, hardware display calibration and physical tracker timing remain outside this workflow. File selection uses an in-app path field/catalog rather than a native OS file dialog.

title: Validation
text: ConfigurationUIValidation.Run requires a disposable project with KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY at its root. Run graphics-enabled Unity with -batchmode -projectPath <copy> -executeMethod ConfigurationUIValidation.Run -logFile <log> without -quit; the runner exits after its asynchronous checks. The suite checks every leaf of all current templates/examples, byte-identical no-op saves, raw/form round trips, numeric precision, external conflicts, conditional controls, 10,000 sequence rows, actual UI callbacks and rendering, selected non-default paths, metadata capture, and two complete experiment transitions. The base validation report covers the full-field and archive checks. The studio validation report also records session defaults, icon button state, navigation persistence, metadata extensions, dashboard suppression and actual Input System Tab presses, alongside library insertion/custom paths, native drag events, duplicate/remove/replace/variation/undo, numeric controls, absent phases, 10,000 block cards and repeated run teardown. Session preview, sequence preview, settings preview, system preview, and library preview are rendered by the actual runtime panel using synthetic validation sequences. ConfigurationStudioValidation.Run uses the same disposable-copy marker and invocation pattern. Unity's existing editor search-indexing exception is excluded by its specific stack trace; runtime UI/experiment errors fail the suite. The config-template checker and run-archive regression suite are also run. Runtime UI Toolkit input integration follows Unity's runtime event-system guidance.

title: 0.3 native GUI verification
text: 2,946 native checks passed with no errors. Fresh Full HD captures show the current animal/species Session screen, sequence/system/settings panels, raw JSON, all fields and replay launcher. See the 0.3 GUI report, capture manifest, Session, raw JSON and replay launcher. These are actual graphics-enabled runtime UI Toolkit captures with synthetic validation animals, not live collection data.

title: Current-source ecosystem UI after 0.3
text: The ecosystem GUI report passed 2,970 checks with no runtime errors, including modern backend labels, explicit optional tracker launch controls, metadata/JSON/Undo/navigation and readable full-width selectors. Fresh current-source Session and capture provenance use synthetic animals, not camera acquisition. These additions are separate from the immutable 0.3 player. See native tracker integration.

title: Configuration GUI and operator HUD
text: The Config UI Test work is preserved in the 0.2 baseline and carried into current source. Older Bogong-only builds retain their historical interface. Open ControlScene and press Play, or use Tools → Experiment setup → Open setup screen (Play). No GUI changes are pushed to the Bogong branch by this work. The dashboard is designed first for 1920 × 1080. Session, Sequence config, System config and Experiment configs always occupy the same left navigation rail, with a selected-page highlight. The header carries page context, setup state and live FPS/frame time; the independent FPS canvas is suspended while setup is open and restored for the run. The footer owns Save and Start. Experiment controls stay in the workspace, and the secondary overview gives run context. Smaller windows retain the navigation and use vertical scrolling where necessary; horizontal scrollbars are hidden and controls are checked for overflow. Motion uses the community terms Closed loop orientation and Closed loop position. The first controls measured yaw, and the second controls measured translation; autopilot and starting-pose resets are separate groups. Compact switches, short numeric entries and expandable feature headers avoid stretching a simple value across the screen. Hover over a field, switch or label for its behavior, units, JSON path and omitted default. Help is rendered by the setup panel in both Play mode and standalone builds: Unity's built-in tooltip property only displays in Editor UI. Descriptions are shared through Resources/ConfigurationUI/field-help.json, with schema-specific help for overloaded fields such as optomotor angular speed and playback time scale. Omitted fields with defined defaults are shown automatically and marked Inherited. Monitoring defaults are explicit previews: telemetry ON, localhost port 9880 at 20 Hz; status overlay ON on display 0. The schema is generated from runtime configuration classes, including initialized objects and vectors. Opening an inherited object, expanding it or navigating never writes defaults into the user's JSON. Editing an inherited child writes only the selected path; Undo restores the original omission. Explicit null remains distinct from an omitted default. All parameters → Show unset optional fields exposes additional null/unspecified entries. The editor uses compact numeric spin controls with exact text entry. Click the up/down arrows, press Up/Down while editing, or use the wheel over a focused number. Shift multiplies the step by ten; Alt divides fractional steps by ten. Counts and ports step as integers. Sliders appear for continuous adjustments such as speed, gain, contrast, exposure and directional concentration. Gain sliders cover 0–50; exact entry retains negative and larger values. A value outside the slider's range remains visible and unchanged until explicitly edited. Spin arithmetic preserves decimal digits beyond double precision. Colors use Unity's native UnityEditor.UIElements.ColorField in Editor Play mode, including its color picker and eyedropper. Standalone builds use a compact hex/RGB/alpha dialog, because the editor picker is not available in a player. Missing alpha keys are not inserted; extension keys inside a color object are retained. Unity ColorField documentation. Forms adapt to the actual window width. Smaller windows hide the secondary overview so controls retain usable space; short numeric values occupy compact input boxes rather than stretching across a column. Vector components stay together. The metadata form, sequence builder, main settings, optional fields, raw JSON and unknown parameters remain accessible. Add parameter… accepts a new key and an arbitrary JSON value. Viewing controls does not change a file. Edits, JSON mode, Save, Undo and Redo use the same lossless document model, including unusual numeric precision and future extension fields.

title: Scene duration takes precedence
text: Heading observation no longer extends a scene. Flat experiments use the sequence row's duration; phased experiments use the configured phase durationSeconds. The effective window is: min(requested windowSeconds, scene/phase duration − startOffsetSeconds) The GUI shows a small amber warning when a window is shortened. The original windowSeconds remains in the JSON and archived config; the heading result logs both requestedWindowSeconds and effective windowSeconds. Observation still measures the animal's actual virtual yaw and completes before the next condition uses the saved mean. An offset at or after the scene end is a configuration error, because no observation interval exists. The legacy measureDuringPresentation key is retained for file compatibility. It no longer adds an assessment period to the scene clock. Its false value can still cause legacy spawners to reapply the completed reference. Use separate pre-stimulus and stimulus phases when a dedicated assessment condition is required.

title: Flight HUD and hiding
text: Each active rig leads with its flight state: Flying, Not flying, or Acquiring while the flight detector lacks a qualified window. DC, gains, tracking modes and basic trim information use smaller, quieter information tiers. More details expands the full sample/window statistics, input endpoints and telemetry; Less details returns to the compact view. Cool gray is neutral, green indicates flying/active, amber indicates operator bypasses or warnings, and errors remain distinct. Tab works during experiments, including when an old metadata input retained focus. Action callbacks and a frame-state fallback are debounced so one press cannot toggle twice. In setup, Tab retains form navigation. During a run, it hides/restores status, FPS, overview, desktop controls and replay controls together. The status/FPS/overview allocator keeps their panels outside calibrated LED rectangles, omitting any panel that cannot fit. Panel contents are clipped to their reserved bounds. A one-frame washout clears retained operator pixels before stimulus cameras render, so hiding leaves LED output intact. Error capture and telemetry continue while graphics are hidden.

title: Verification
text: The current overlay report adds 172 native framebuffer assertions across seven 1920×1080 LED layouts, including real Tab input, first-frame washout and restore, plus 6,428 actual-source geometry/visibility assertions across 24 LED configurations and 1,500 random obstacle layouts. Native screenshots include the unchanged ScreenSpaceOverlay canvases; camera-only targets were not used as proof of UI compositing. The validation report records 5,987 studio checks, 40 focused UX checks, 4,422 phase/heading checks, standalone macOS script compilation, 66 current configs and 10 Python tests. The studio regression tests cover lossless no-op saves, edits to config leaves, arbitrary extensions, exact numbers, undo/redo, native input and virtualized sequences. ConfigurationUXValidation adds rendered layouts at 1024×720, 1440×900 and 1920×1080; native color callbacks; precise mouse/keyboard spin controls; future parameter addition; an actual 30-second request capped to a 0.7-second flight condition; real Tab input; black pixel output and one-render camera shutdown. Rendering tests use a disposable project and synthetic inputs, not a live animal session. See configuration-ux-validation-results.json and the images under docs/images/ux/ for the recorded checks and native captures. Player script compilation checks the standalone path without the Editor-only color picker. The dashboard revision adds 2,773 native checks for fixed navigation, Full HD geometry, subject clipping, FPS ownership, runtime hover events, descriptions for every schema property, and default edits/Undo. The existing studio suite passes 5,987 checks; the interaction/HUD suite passes 40 checks at 1024, 1440 and 1920 pixels. Standalone macOS player scripts compile. The config validator passes all 66 templates/examples, and all 10 Python tests pass. See dashboard validation summary and detailed results. Captures use example configs and synthetic metadata in a disposable Unity project. Native captures:

title: Configuration reference
text: For 0.3 species/animal IDs, agentCount/agentSpeed aliases, rig counts and reversible editing, see animal/agent compatibility. The tables retain older accepted JSON names so existing experiments remain interpretable. Current standalone paths use a writable profile; see getting started. For recorded swarm input, the standalone converter and batched 3D moth, see swarm-playback.md. The recorded-swarm example centres each recorded birth on the current animal and continues its terminal direction at the configured 6m/s until 100m away (playback.continueAfterTrack: true, periodicBoundary: false, continuationSpeedMetresPerSecond: 6; nested under swarm for Choice terrain experiments). playback.preRollSeconds defaults to 0; that example flies the observer at 5 m/s with zero incoming lead-in, matching Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-flight-observer.example.json. The optional Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-passive-observer.example.json disables observer autopilot and uses five seconds of incoming extrapolation for a stationary visibility check. These settings belong to the individual experiment, with defaults and units in that guide. Terrain/migration distances are metres; older walking distances are centimetres. worldUnitsPerMetre resolves this explicitly without changing existing movement-controller units. This reference describes the experiment configuration code, tested with Unity 6000.3.16f1. Start with the complete JSON files in StreamingAssets/Templates. They contain editable example values; the tables below distinguish these from values used when a field is omitted. JSON does not allow comments. Keep notes in a separate text file; do not invent JSON keys, because most loaders silently ignore unknown keys.

title: Files, precedence, and running an experiment
text: Use the complete Templates/system_config.template.json, Templates/experiment.template.json and Templates/sequence.template.json as a matched Kinefly flight starting set. Set actual hardware addresses and displays. The local system_config.json is Git-ignored and is not replaced by cleanup. For other paradigms, choose a complete file from Templates; use Examples for variations. Relative references resolve from RuntimePaths.ConfigRoot (Editor: StreamingAssets; current standalone: writable profile Config). Dynamic Choice uses parameters.design; other experiment controllers use parameters.configFile. Open Assets/Scenes/ControlScene.unity, enter Play, enter metadata, and start the sequence. Sex is visible for each animal, with Unspecified as the fresh default. Saved Female/Male values are restored on reload. Focus Game for hotkeys. The prior Selwyn sequence and all files in Kannadi/ are preserved; current source defaults to the TerrainCueLab demonstration. The old collection is under Archive/Legacy/, with original bytes and a checksum manifest. If an experiment reference is missing at its current path, the loader checks that archive, so unchanged Kannadi sequences can still resolve their old Choice dependency. System config owns physical camera layout and sphere calibration. Sequence config owns scene order and duration. Experiment configs own stimuli and tracked motion. Kannadi/Swarm merge inline parameters over configFile (arrays replace, rather than append), while autopilot remains owned by the referenced file. Choice/Optomotor read their referenced file without merging inline stimulus fields. Dynamic Choice uses parameters.design, not configFile. The recovered historical Adaminaby image/config can also run through the current six-camera Choice scene: use Examples/Sequences/adaminaby-historical.example.json. See its provenance and run instructions, including the original screenshot's projection limitations. Autopilot is controlled by the individual experiment file referenced by parameters.configFile, so the sequence selects a complete movement configuration without duplicating its fields. A default in a C# class is not necessarily a scene default: serialized prefab values override inspector defaults, and omitted fields on an in-scene step can retain state. Use explicit values for reproducibility. Current source provisions configured rigs from an authored scene template within the available Unity layer capacity. JSON does not create new scenes/assets or physical hardware.

title: Units and coordinate system
text: Unity coordinates are left-handed: +X right/east, +Y up, +Z forward/north. Walking experiments use one world unit = one centimeter; migration/Selwyn terrain uses one world unit = one metre. Distances and translation speeds use world units and world units/second (cm and cm/s for walking, m and m/s for terrain). Enter scene-native values in configs. Recorded-swarm input is in metres and is mapped using worldUnitsPerMetre; moth body/wing dimensions and near clip use physical metres independently. Euler angles are degrees: X pitch, Y yaw, Z roll.
