University of Konstanz visitor address.

title: Validation
text: Run the static repository checks, then use Unity 6000.3.16f1 with graphics enabled on a disposable project copy containing KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY: Unity -batchmode -projectPath <copy> -executeMethod NightSkyValidation.Run -logFile <log> Do not add -quit or -nographics. This tests clock/offset/now/DST handling, coordinate conventions, GPU filtering/output, checksums, explicit-image precedence, restart/update/freeze behavior, camera restoration and CSV attribution. KannadiValidation.Run separately covers the existing experiment stack. Physical north alignment and LED acquisition timing still need a bench check. Use NightSkyValidation.RunControlPreview on a disposable copy with the preserved Adaminaby preview sequence to test the real Control-scene launch, current-time export, actual aligned Bogong movement and flicker-free visibility, simulated next half-hour image/load record, and Escape behavior. The general Kannadi suite installs the saved pre-preview sequence into the disposable copy before running. Use ChoiceNightSkyValidation.Run on a disposable copy for the Choice sky-only regression: omitted/null objects, generated-to-legacy image transitions, camera overrides, current-time panorama export, 30-minute refresh and cleanup. RunSelwyn additionally tests the local Choice_Selwyn terrain scene and Kannadi/selwyn-night-sky.json when those assets are present. Both runners install a temporary sequence and six-camera system config in the disposable copy.

title: Generated physical Bogong swarm
text: The full-duration reference runs the four-block Selwyn Milky Way/swarm cycle: one-time 360 s setup followed by repeating 240/240/240 s conditions, 7 m/s observer, 150 moths per rig and corrected approximately 99% directional order. It measures each animal's mean during the Milky Way-only block and reuses it in both swarm blocks. This document describes the separate original Examples/Swarm/generated-bogong-speed-distribution.example.json recipe and rendering/recording tests for its 64-moth population. That recipe and your existing heading-aligned/recorded playback files remain available. The individual experiment's stimulus.swarm creates 64 generated moths per configured rig, with no CSV input. The moth remains 3 cm long, 1 cm thick, with a 6 cm coupled wing pair, matching your physical playback settings. sizeMode: "World" retains perspective; GPU flapping runs at 30 Hz and subpixel contrast fades with projected area. The sky remains your 0.12 uniform gray during presentation. The near plane is 1 mm, allowing a 1 cm approach. Heading 0 is relative to the frozen animal baseline; kappa is 1000 for yaw and elevation. Existing direction sampling is retained. Parameter under stimulus.swarm Recipe Meaning trajectoryFile empty Generate agents; no replay or inherited recorded trajectories. numberOfLocusts 64 Count per rig; four rigs give 256 independent moths. The legacy field name also controls moth populations. density null Optional density used only when count is omitted. In this metre-scale volume, agents/m³. locustSpeed 6.17 Mean generated speed in m/s here; world units/s generally. locustSpeedStdDev 1.24 Standard deviation, not variance, in m/s here. Each moth samples once and keeps its speed through wrapping. Negative normal draws are redrawn; at this mean/SD the truncation is negligible. Omitted/zero preserves legacy constant speed and RNG. volumeHalfExtentMetres 2 Cube from -2 to +2 m relative to the observer on each axis. This physical parameter overrides the configured spawn/boundary sizes, converting to the scene's units. Null preserves older dimensions. preserveBoundaryOvershoot true Periodic wrapping preserves excess travel instead of snapping to an edge. Large time steps and observer teleports remain within the cube. Omitted/false retains the original wrapper. spawnRelativeToAnimal, followAnimalPosition true Start and retain the volume around the current observer. Individual moths move at their own world velocity; they are not dragged by observer motion. spawnCenter 0,0,0 No vertical/forward offset from the animal. wrapY true Wrap all three axes in 3D. worldUnitsPerMetre 1 Terrain/migration world scale. A centimetre scene uses 100 and scene-native speed values such as mean 617, SD 124 cm/s. The observer uses experiment-level autopilotSpeed: 6.17, outside the swarm object, during both phases. Matching forward speeds preserve relative separation; speed differences and direction scatter produce overtakes. The boundary follows current position after observer/AGL movement but does not steer existing moths with subsequent yaw. The count stays constant across periodic crossings. This is a synthetic steady population, not an estimate reconstructed from the CSV. At 64 moths in 64 m³, nominal density is 1/m³ and volume-per-animal spacing is 1 m; this is not a nearest-neighbour guarantee.

title: Contrast and encounters
text: GeneratedSwarmValidation.Run measures the actual 64×64, 90° rendered pixels against the 0.12-gray background. Full contrast means the difference between background and the configured moth RGB; half contrast means the strongest affected pixel carries at least 50% of that difference. It samples front/broadside views, wing phases and subpixel offsets. The configured half extent is the greater of 2 m and the sampled half-contrast distance. Results are in validation results. In the native test, the furthest sampled distance meeting half contrast is 1 m; the sampled poses at 1.5 m are below it. The recipe therefore uses the requested minimum 2 m half extent. At 2 m the maximum residual is four 8-bit gray levels out of the full 28-level contrast. The front view can be much fainter than a broadside wing view. These measurements use the physical size and RGB values above, with no contrast boost. Recalibrate if changing dimensions or panel resolution. At 2 m, some orientations can still leave a faint gray pixel. There is no hard invisibility threshold or artificial pixel/opacity floor. A cube with 2 m half extent has corners 3.46 m away. This pixel test does not calibrate night-level animal acuity or physical panel luminance. At 10 cm, the actual wing geometry changes visibly between up/down phases. Adequate temporal resolution matters: 30 Hz flapping can alias at 30 FPS; 120 FPS supplies four samples per cycle. Hardware frame timing remains in system config and is not changed by this experiment. The deterministic ten-minute encounter test uses the same unforced random population and co-moving observer. Its counts demonstrate naturally occurring close passes, not an event schedule. Count and volume jointly control density; increasing count raises encounter likelihood. No moth is deliberately steered toward the animal or enlarged for a close pass. With seed 703 and a co-moving 6.17 m/s observer, that realization has 19 entries within 10 cm, 203 within 25 cm and a nearest approach of 2.36 cm, sampled every 50 ms. It averages 4.35 moths within 1 m. The 100,000-sample speed check measures mean 6.167 m/s and SD 1.236 m/s. Native up/down views of the one coupled wing pair at 10 cm: Head-on views previously lost both zero-thickness wing sheets. The same two patches now use a thin projected blur edge, equivalent to 5% of body diameter (0.5 mm for this moth), with opacity scaled by its actual pixel coverage. This is a simple blur approximation, not full wing anatomy. It introduces no extra wing pair, minimum opacity or body-size increase. The far proxy uses area-weighted wing/body centroid motion, avoiding the previous body-only wobble when wings were edge-on.

title: Recording and performance
text: Both standalone Swarm and embedded Choice/Selwyn swarms save all presented positions with the existing pooled asynchronous gzip writer. Generated movement runs after observer motion; capture runs after movement, and CSV formatting/compression/disk writes run on workers. There is one shared motion component and one batched renderer per rig, GPU flapping and no per-moth Animator. Steady movement does not resample speeds, recreate objects, read configs or hash files. The new controls live in the individual experiment JSON files; the original ControlScene metadata form remains. Tests start the generated recipe through that original Save/Start button and check camera allow-lists, physical scale in both metre/centimetre worlds, world-relative motion, exact wrapping and complete coordinate recording. See data formats for the unchanged nine data columns and world units. Headers now include the speed SD. Archived system/sequence/experiment versions remain in each run's config bundle. The isolated benchmark compares logging off/on for four 64-agent populations and 24 native cameras, verifies zero dropped frames and exact final saved coordinates, and measures main-thread allocation after warm-up. Its CPU submission timings exclude terrain, physical displays and tracker processing; they are not a promise of workstation FPS. On Apple M2 Pro / Unity 6000.3.16f1, median motion/upload/camera submission is 2.29 ms without recording and 2.45 ms with it; recording capture itself takes 0.104 ms median for all four swarms. Recording-on p95 is 5.27 ms. All 71,680 submitted coordinate rows are present, without drops or worker errors, and final saved positions match every agent. Warmed movement/upload/capture allocates zero managed bytes per frame on the main thread. Your 120 FPS target and hardware layout remain unchanged. Existing recorded playback and five-scene phase suites also pass on the original controllers. The transferred heading-aligned.example.json removes only the accidental duplicate enabled heading assessment inside stimulus; its existing preStimulus assessment and other edited settings remain. All current templates/examples validate without an exclusion: python3 tools/validate_config_templates.py The non-GUI simulation, rendering, configuration and recording updates are on codex/bogong-night-sky.

title: Bogong moths and recorded swarm playback
text: The active sequence uses the four-block Selwyn Milky Way/swarm cycle, with generated physical Bogong moths and no CSV input. The recorded CSV recipes below remain separate and unchanged; select their sequence to replay the measured data. The current sequence selects the generated heading-aligned experiment, described in experiment phases. To run this recorded-data recipe, set the Swarm sequence row's parameters.configFile to Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-playback.example.json, retain duration 1200, then open Assets/Scenes/ControlScene.unity and press Play. The supplied CSV recipe starts Swarm immediately for 1200 seconds, with a uniform 0.1-gray sky, the recorded swarm's aggregate direction set to north (0°), and each animal starting at yaw 0°, height 5 m. This standalone experiment explicitly uses metres, an observer flying north at 5 m/s (autopilotEnabled: true, autopilotSpeed: 5) and gain 1. Moths spawn at their first recorded sample with zero incoming lead-in, follow their unchanged recorded samples, then continue at 6 m/s until 100 m away. Auto-trim is off for this direct playback recipe. The 599.46-second recording repeats its schedule while previously spawned moths keep flying. Set autoStart: false to restore the manual Start button. The individual experiment is Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-playback.example.json; edit its playback and bogongVisual settings. uniformSkyColor uses normalized RGB, 0–1: 0.5 is gray and 1 is white. A value of 15 is invalid and causes the phase to be rejected; use 15/255 (approximately 0.058824) only if you intend the 8-bit code value 15. These values do not specify physical luminance. The committed CSV example sky is 0.1; local edits may differ. The unlit bogongVisual.color is a direct rendered RGB value, not a reflectance multiplied by lighting: the old 0.12 moth nearly matched or exceeded that sky. The committed CSV example moth uses 0.012 to give a dark silhouette. These explicit values are a stimulus choice, not a calibrated photometric model. The terrain alternative Examples/Sequences/selwyn-trajectory-playback.example.json uses Choice_Selwyn and an embedded swarm object, with southeast presentation. Templates/swarm-playback.template.json has a blank data path and produces a generated swarm until one is supplied. Hardware settings remain in your existing system_config.json; these edits preserve camera order and tracker endpoints. The CSV observer settings match Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-flight-observer.example.json: autopilot at 5 m/s and preRollSeconds: 0; visual/sky settings can differ. The optional Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-passive-observer.example.json uses a stationary observer and five-second incoming lead-in. To select the stationary diagnostic, change the sequence row's parameters.configFile to that passive example. Flight templates keep autopilot enabled by default. Ctrl+Space toggles autopilot during a run.

title: Coordinates and units
text: The source uses millimetres: +X north, +Y west, +Z down, with Z=0 at 5 m AGL (confirmed October 12, 2026). Converted positions are metres, in Unity axes (+X east, +Y up, +Z north): X = -source Y / 1000 Y = 5 - source Z / 1000 Z = source X / 1000 time = TimeExact - earliest TimeExact (seconds) Naive timestamps are Australia/Sydney local time (UTC+11 on October 7, 2026). The shared relative clock preserves gaps between sightings. The converted file retains all 14,429 rows and 430 IDs, local 19:44:35.283–19:54:34.743. The raw source is untouched. Finite outliers are reported in bounds and retained. Positive source Z lowers Unity height. Earlier conversions incorrectly used +Z up; the corrected file reflects height about 5 m, without changing horizontal positions, distances, speeds, IDs or timing. With the stated axes, aggregate heading is 225.64° (southwest). The canonical file preserves those axes. The active standalone Swarm recipe uses playback.yawOffsetDegrees: -225.64127709737375 to present its aggregate displacement at 0° (north). The terrain/flight examples use -90 for 135.64° (southeast). Generated motion uses mu; recorded motion uses this explicit yaw offset, preserving each measured trajectory and its spread. Set 0 to retain the measured cardinal direction. Flight direction cannot independently establish geographical calibration. Positive yaw is clockwise from above: N=0°, E=90°, S=180°, W=270°. Terrain/migration uses metres (worldUnitsPerMetre: 1); older walking scenes use centimetres (100). Omitted scale defaults to 1 in a scene with active Terrain, otherwise 100. Prefer explicit values. playback.dataUnitsPerMetre describes CSV units, default 1. Positions are multiplied by worldUnitsPerMetre / dataUnitsPerMetre. Boundary sizes, offsets, generated swarm speed and autopilot speed remain in existing scene units. For terrain, speed 5 means 5 m/s. Moth dimensions and near clip are physical metres, so the body stays one inch long in either scale. The camera's original near plane is restored when the swarm is cleared. Centering removes the absolute dataset position/height during presentation. For original georeferenced positions, disable both centerOnAnimal and periodicBoundary.

title: Standalone converter
text: Python 3.9+ with timezone data is sufficient; no third-party dependencies or Unity are needed: python3 tools/convert_swarm_trajectories.py /path/to/long-format.csv Assets/StreamingAssets/SwarmData/new-unity.csv Input columns are Frame, ID, X, Y, Z, TimeExact. Output is exactly ID,X,Y,Z,time, sorted by time/ID. IDs stay text. Frame is validated and its range retained in metadata. The sidecar records local start, timezone, units, source hash, bounds, rejected rows and transform choices. Empty IDs, invalid frames/timestamps and nonfinite positions are rejected and reported. Duplicate ID/time pairs raise an error; --duplicates first|last explicitly changes that policy. Finite position outliers are retained. Options: --source-units mm|cm|m (mm), --source-z down|up (down; use up only for an explicitly upward source dataset), --output-units m|cm (m), --height-origin-m 5, --timezone Australia/Sydney, --yaw-degrees 0. Keep converter yaw 0 when using playback yaw to avoid rotating twice.

title: Playback settings
text: Field Default Meaning trajectoryFile empty StreamingAssets-relative or absolute CSV path. Blank preserves generated motion. Supplied missing/malformed files raise errors. worldUnitsPerMetre scene-dependent Physical scene scale: 1 terrain or 100 walking. nearClipMetres 0.001 for Moth 1 mm near plane; permits seeing a moth 1 cm ahead. Applied to stimulus cameras, preserving system camera allow-lists. playback.dataUnitsPerMetre 1 CSV distance scale. playback.loop true Repeat until the outer experiment/phase ends. playback.speed 1 Positive time multiplier. playback.startTimeSeconds 0 Shared clock offset. playback.maxGapSeconds 0.1 Interpolate across gaps no longer than this; longer missing intervals are invisible. playback.yawOffsetDegrees 0 Clockwise presentation yaw independent of steering. playback.centerOnAnimal true Align the full dataset's sample centroid with the animal at each track appearance. playback.periodicBoundary true Recycle positions through the moving 3D boundary with overshoot preserved. playback.continueAfterTrack false; true in Selwyn examples Continue each uninterrupted recorded segment at its terminal velocity. Requires periodicBoundary: false. playback.despawnDistanceMetres 100 In continuation mode, retire a moth when its 3D distance from the current animal exceeds this many physical metres. Scaled correctly in centimetre scenes. playback.terminalVelocityWindowSeconds 0.1 Estimate outgoing velocity from approximately the final 0.1 s of each uninterrupted segment, and incoming velocity from its first 0.1 s. Short segments use available samples; zero uses the endpoint pair. Does not smooth or alter recorded positions. playback.continuationSpeedMetresPerSecond null Physical speed override for extrapolated incoming/outgoing lines; positive m/s, independent of CSV/scene units. Null retains each measured endpoint velocity. Active recorded examples use 6. Recorded positions/times are unchanged. A singleton or zero-velocity endpoint stays stationary. playback.preRollSeconds 0 Seconds of straight-line incoming extrapolation before a segment's first sample. Requires continueAfterTrack: true. The passive Selwyn example uses 5 (about 30 m at 6 m/s); active/flying examples use 0. Preserve 0 for historical first-sample spawns. No prior recording cycle is invented at startup. spawnCenter zero in examples World-unit presentation offset. spawnVolumeSize dataset bounds in playback Explicit positive X/Y/Z periodic volume if supplied; does not rescale or retime tracks. With continueAfterTrack: false, IDs are pooled at startup and visible only during their recorded lifetimes, retaining the earlier playback behavior. Position is interpolated, heading follows trajectory velocity/elevation, and constant-speed movers are disabled. Data is parsed once and shared across rigs. Tracks receive world anchors at appearance, loop, or gap reappearance. Existing agents do not translate with the animal or rotate with steering; only an enabled periodic boundary recycles crossings. Each rig retains its stimulus layer.

title: Spawn-centred continuation (active Selwyn recipe)
text: The animal is at the full recording's sample centroid of the new spawn volume, not necessarily at the centroid of the moths currently visible. The measured centroid is (-0.2697495303, 4.2748470732, 0.1078053752) metres before presentation yaw. At each birth: anchor = animalPositionAtSpawn + spawnCenter - yaw * (recordingCentroid * unitsScale) worldPosition(t) = anchor + yaw * (recordedPosition(t) * unitsScale) after the final sample: recordedPosition(t) = lastPosition + finalVelocity * (t - lastTime) before the first sample: recordedPosition(t) = firstPosition + initialVelocity * (t - firstTime) This is a translation of the recorded volume, with an explicit presentation yaw (north in the active recipe, southeast in the terrain examples); it does not rescale, randomize or retime measured observations. The anchor is frozen at spawn. Turning or moving the animal later changes its view of that moth but cannot drag or steer the moth. New births centre a new copy of the same sampled volume on the animal's current position. The old births then fly outside the small mocap volume without any teleportation or periodic wrapping. Following the same direction and speed can keep a moth alongside the animal beyond the original track's endpoint. It is retired only when it exceeds the 100m distance cutoff or the experiment stops. Matched velocities can retain moths across multiple recording loops; the pool grows only when all existing slots are busy, preserves wing phases and continues to use one batch renderer per rig. First-sample times, entry positions, recorded trajectories and inter-arrival intervals are measured; incoming and outgoing lines are extrapolated, so continuation does not establish unmeasured motion or density beyond the capture volume. Lead-ins instantiate earlier than first samples. A CSV interval without observations can therefore still contain incoming moths and existing tails. The median recorded track length is 0.15 seconds (range 0.02–1.83 seconds). Seven gaps exceed 0.1 seconds; they split into separate recorded segments, each with its own birth and continuation, rather than drawing a false connecting trajectory. A segment with only one sample has no measured velocity and remains stationary until the animal leaves the cutoff. Backward seeking clears tails and initializes recorded/incoming segments present at the seek time, since the animal's past movement is unavailable. Forward frame steps emit every crossed instantiation event, anchoring them at the current frame's animal position. The active recipe sets continuationSpeedMetresPerSecond: 6. This retains each measured endpoint direction and normalizes speed on the incoming/outgoing extrapolation only. The short recorded portion still uses its measured velocity (median 4.10 m/s); the original measured terminal-speed median is 5.02 m/s. Set this override to null to reproduce the earlier measured-speed continuation. locustSpeed controls generated motion only, and playback.speed changes the entire data clock including arrival rate; neither controls only extrapolated physical speed. The recording's row-weighted centroid centres its sampled cloud. It is not a survey of the geometric mocap boundary or an instantaneous population centre. With zero spawnCenter, SwarmTrajectoryPlayback.SpawnVolumeCentroid tracks the animal; the world centroid of existing moths is free to move away. With centerOnAnimal: false, canonical absolute data is retained, without the spawn-centred translation.

title: Moth visual
text: Set agentVisual: "Bogong", bogongVisual.shape: "Moth". Dot is still the old default. Assets/Resources/Bogong/Moth.prefab is the reusable metre-scale asset. Unity's GameObject → Experiments → Bogong moth (metres) creates another editable BogongMoth root. Geometry regenerates on enable; edit physical dimensions on the component. Swarms use a shared renderer directly, avoiding one renderer per prefab instance. bogongVisual field Default Meaning shape Dot Moth selects a 3D cigar body and two GPU wing patches. bodyLengthMetres 0.0254 Length along local +Z. bodyDiameterMetres 0.01 Body thickness. wingSpanMetres 0.04 Total two-wing width. flapFrequencyHz 30 Flap cycles/s; zero gives a static pose. wingOpacity 0.25 Faint wing blur opacity, 0–1. subpixelVisibility true Soft proxy below a few pixels, with opacity proportional to projected body area plus faint wings; retains subpixel flap motion. sizeMode World Physical distance scaling, or Angular for constant apparent nominal body length. angularSizeDegrees 1 Dot diameter, or nominal moth body length, in Angular mode; orientation still changes the projected shape. size 0.5 world units Legacy dot diameter; Moth uses physical dimensions. color RGBA .12,.12,.12,1 Dark gray unlit albedo with cheap body shading. Body alpha stays opaque; use wing opacity for blur. metallic, smoothness 0, .25 Legacy compatibility; unlit visual ignores PBR lighting. flickerFrequencyHz 0 Whole-agent flicker separate from flap. Zero disables. flickerDutyCycle .5 Visible fraction, 0–1. Each moth has exactly one coupled left/right wing pair: two quads sharing a single 30 Hz flap phase. There is no additional forewing/hindwing pair. The subpixel proxy replaces the body and wings when selected; it is not drawn as an extra wing pair. Near animals use actual low-poly bodies and rudimentary wings. Far animals use an area-weighted bilinear point footprint, fading toward the background rather than failing subpixel triangle rasterization. It distributes the true projected area over one to four pixels, preserving total subpixel contrast as the point crosses pixel boundaries. The previous Gaussian spread this contrast across roughly eight pixels, making individual pixels unnecessarily faint. There is no artificial minimum opacity or increase in physical size. Extreme distances still reach finite 8-bit display precision. No Animator runs per insect. For 30 Hz flapping, 120 FPS is preferable; 60 FPS shows two phases, and 30 FPS can alias. Panel refresh limits available temporal detail. The same pair now has a coverage-weighted thin blur edge when viewed head-on, so its flap does not disappear at a close pass. The subpixel centroid is weighted by actual body/wing area instead of shifting an edge-on body as though broad wings were visible. The body dimensions, vertex/draw counts and recorded trajectories are unchanged. See generated swarm validation for native front/broadside captures and performance checks. Flight AGL is settled before the first CSV birth is anchored, preventing first-frame moths from being left behind at the terrain scene’s authored height. The moth shader uses separate RGB/alpha blending so composited camera textures remain opaque over an opaque background. This preserves the intended faint RGB contrast when exported or displayed in a UI instead of applying transparency a second time. The RGB stimulus rendering is unchanged by the alpha fix. Existing pooled asynchronous gzip logging is retained. Swarm-scene logs identify agents by _ID_<source ID> names and record presented world positions; repeated births add _C<recording-cycle>_S<segment> so simultaneous instances are distinguishable. Pool reuse refreshes logger identity caches. Terrain Choice retains its rig logging. Loading a CSV adds no duplicate raw-data writes. Converted data and metadata retain provenance.

title: Arrival rate and visibility audit
text: The supplied recording has 430 IDs over 599.46 seconds: 43.04 unique arrivals/minute, or 1.39 seconds per arrival on average. Arrival times are bursty: 26–71 IDs per minute, with a longest gap of 12.67 seconds. The 430 allocated root objects are a pool, not 430 simultaneous visible animals. Seven missing-data gaps produce 437 uninterrupted segments, as already documented above. When multiple IDs have the same recorded timestamp, their median nearest-neighbour distance is 2.16 m; only four IDs are simultaneously recorded at most. This conditional sample is not a complete census of the surrounding population and does not establish sub-1m spacing. Playback retains the original metre coordinates and spacings. It does not compress the volume or add extra births to create a denser synthetic stimulus. Density audit separates measured speeds/spacing from the explicit 6m/s continuation. For a northward observer at 5m/s, an exact-time geometric calculation predicts about 6.2 passes/minute within 1m, 24.4 within 2m and 40.9 within 3m. An arrival is not necessarily a close pass. The earlier 5 m/s flying-observer 0.5-gray scene audit sees every source ID, 49 births in the first minute, and about 31 live moths on average with 100m retirement. With the corrected point footprint, 42 first-minute births within 3m produce at least three bytes of gray contrast in native 128px panels; 35 do at 64px. Wing phases can change these sampled counts between runs. These are numerical detection counts in 5×5 patches, sampled at 0.1s, not a biological visibility threshold. Overlapping moths can contribute to the same patch. Gray sky, body dimensions, source positions and birth times are retained. The low-poly body's diameter now reaches the specified 1cm instead of 0.87cm. Reproduce the data audit without Unity: python3 tools/audit_swarm_playback.py Assets/StreamingAssets/SwarmData/selwyn-oct7-unity.csv --config Assets/StreamingAssets/Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-playback.example.json --observer-speed 5 --report /tmp/swarm-audit.json With zero pre-roll, SwarmTrajectoryPlayback.TotalBirths reports first-sample spawns since the last stream reset/seek; ActiveCount reports live moths. SwarmStartupValidation.Run tests ControlScene and runs the complete ten-minute scene audit in a disposable project.

title: Stationary observer and incoming extension
text: Passive-observer audit measures each path's closest 3D approach to the centered, stationary animal. Before incoming extension, seven paths pass within 25 cm over ten minutes (0.70/min), 20 within 50 cm (2.00/min), and 78 within 1 m (7.81/min). The nearest is 17.70 cm; none reaches 10 cm. Frequent source arrivals therefore do not imply frequent large images. A 2.54 cm body at the nearest distance spans about 4.6 pixels broadside near the center of a 64px, 90° face, or 9.2 at 128px. Orientation and position within the cube face change the projection; most arrivals remain much smaller. Five seconds of incoming extrapolation raises the predicted counts to 28 within 50 cm and 94 within 1 m, while the seven within 25 cm remain unchanged. These extra path sections are predictions, not additional CSV observations. They extend the same paths and do not compress space, enlarge moths, or add source IDs. Adding still more distant trajectory history mostly adds distant, faint moths. The first sub-25cm pass is ID 158 at 268.496 s (4:28.5), also the closest overall. The remaining ones occur around 285.83, 323.45, 429.00, 523.71, 527.87 and 550.87 seconds. There are none in the first four minutes. With the corrected +Z-down conversion, ID 158's closest image is on the upward face; a system omitting that camera cannot display that closest moment. Camera allow-lists remain authoritative. Looping a stationary replay repeats these same encounters rather than generating new random close passes. For a quick stationary close-pass check, first select Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-passive-observer.example.json in the sequence row, then set playback.startTimeSeconds: 268.35; ID 158 passes close about 0.15 seconds after Play. Temporarily set playback.speed: 0.25 for a labelled diagnostic at quarter speed (about 0.59 seconds until the pass), then restore speed 1 and start time 0 for the normal experiment. This slows the trajectory clock and arrival rate; it does not enlarge the moth or change the shader's real-time 30 Hz wing frequency. The upward camera must be present in system config to show the closest moment. Instantiate at firstTime - preRollSeconds, or at startup for lead-ins already in progress. The complete recorded volume is centered on the animal at that earlier instantiation, and its anchor remains fixed through approach, recording and departure. It is not recentered at the first measured sample. Later movement of the observer changes its relative encounters. In particular, a five-second lead-in combined with 5 m/s northward autopilot moves the sampled volume behind the animal; the active and separate flight examples consequently keep pre-roll at zero. Incoming paths initially beyond 100 m remain pending without rendering until they enter the cutoff. Backward seeking clears existing tails and starts current recorded/incoming segments with fresh anchors, since the observer's previous path is unavailable. Source first-sample times are unchanged, but instantiations happen earlier. The stationary Unity audit emits all 437 uninterrupted segments and sees all 430 IDs. In the first minute it instantiates 54 moths, including five whose first samples occur in the following five seconds; the CSV itself still has 49 first-minute ID starts. At native panel sizes, 43 instances produce at least three bytes of contrast at 64px and 48 at 128px within 3 m. Mean live population is about 15.8, with a maximum of 37. Those contrast counts are numerical detectability, not a human or moth threshold at a given light level. Rendering alone cannot establish night-level visibility without panel luminance and visual-threshold measurements. TotalBirths counts instantiations, including lead-ins; it resets on seek. ActiveCount excludes pending incoming instances outside the cutoff. The default zero lead-in retains previous counter timing. Reproduce the passive audit using the command above with --observer-speed 0 and --config Assets/StreamingAssets/Examples/Swarm/selwyn-trajectory-passive-observer.example.json.

title: Resolution and corrected vertical calibration
text: Resolution audit compares unchanged world positions and wing phases at 64×64 and 1024×1024, including a stationary observer with five-second incoming extension and the active 5 m/s observer with zero extension. Six 90° faces cover the full sphere, including behind/above/below. The high-resolution camera is a rendering diagnostic, not a calibrated human acuity model. Images are saved locally under Builds/BogongSwarm-resolution; they use the visual parameters and sky color captured in the report. At the center of a 90° face, one 64px pixel spans about 1.79°. A 3cm broadside body at 1m spans about 0.96 pixels; at 3m it spans 0.32. A 6cm wingspan at 3m spans 0.64 pixels before foreshortening. One 1024px pixel spans about 0.112°, so the same body at 3m spans about 5.12 pixels. Pixel angles vary across the face. These geometric values do not establish perceptual thresholds or screen luminance. Distant moths remain in the world and can appear on the back face, but their projected contrast falls with area, approximately as inverse distance squared. Many retained tails are far beyond the few metres where they are detectable in an 8-bit 64px panel. Keeping a moth alive to 100m does not guarantee a visible pixel to 100m. The supplied tracks are arrivals through a small recorded volume, not a simultaneous census of a dense 100m volume. Correcting source +Z from up to down reflects vertical placement. After centering, all 3D distances and closest-pass times remain the same, but above/below faces and vertical motion reverse. Historical captures and validation reports before October 12 use the old vertical sign; the resolution audit and current source verification use the corrected file. No extra source IDs, spatial compression or artificial opacity floor are introduced. The current 0.1-sky/0.012-moth recipe retains the locally edited 3cm body, 1cm thickness, 6cm span and 0.75 wing opacity. The four-horizontal-face startup audit detects at least three levels of contrast for 26 of 49 first-minute births at 64px and 41 at 128px; one-level counts are 41 and 42. Phase and overlap affect these numerical counts. All 430 IDs and 437 uninterrupted segments become active. Mean population is 30.68 for the flying observer, but only 0.82 moths on average are within 3m; for the stationary diagnostic the corresponding means are 15.77 and 0.64. Retained tails include moths behind the observer. The current local hardware file specifies 64×64. Historical comparisons rendered 64px explicitly alongside the then-selected 128px setup. If the physical panels are 64×64, use ledPanelWidth: 64 and ledPanelHeight: 64 in each corresponding system rig to avoid an additional resolution conversion. Hardware settings are not changed by these diagnostics. The comparison uses a mid-gray control for legibility, without boosting image contrast. The first row is a stationary snapshot at 30 seconds: 26 live moths, nearest 9.22m. The lower row is the recorded ID 158 close pass at 268.496 seconds, 17.70cm away, on the corrected upward face. The 1024px output is shown at half size; native renders remain in the local capture directory. SwarmResolutionValidation.Run reproduces the full-sphere retention checks and captures in a disposable Unity copy marked KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY. The player never creates these diagnostic cameras or performs readbacks.

title: Playback rendering cost
text: Moth rendering compacts live agents into the start of a shared mesh. It uploads only their centers, rotations and phases; static body/wing/proxy geometry stays in a separate GPU buffer. The draw range contains only live agents. Empty populations disable the renderer and skip uploads. Wing phase follows the pooled agent rather than its temporary draw slot. There is one renderer/material per rig, GPU flapping, no per-moth Animator, and no managed allocation in steady-state pose updates. The playback birth scheduler also uses a sorted event cursor instead of scanning all 437 segments every frame. Asynchronous recording remains in place. Performance comparison, Unity 6000.3.16f1 on Apple M2 Pro: four pools of 430 slots, 35 live per rig, 24 cameras at 64px. Median CPU pose refresh falls from 1.410 ms to 0.088 ms (about 16×); refresh plus camera/render submission falls from 4.286 ms to 3.392 ms. The refresh allocation measurement is zero bytes/frame before and after. At 70 live per rig, refresh is 0.149 ms; at all 430 live, 0.650 ms. These are CPU submission measurements, excluding end-to-end GPU execution, physical displays, tracker processing and the full experiment frame. They establish the eliminated pool overhead, not a guaranteed workstation FPS. The eight raster comparisons retain exact pixels against the previous full-slot mesh at near and subpixel distances, including hosts under translated, rotated and scaled rigs. Partial buffer updates use Unity's mesh upload API. Incoming/playback validation records the earlier stationary five-second recipe, playback, rendering, configuration and source checks. Flying-observer validation records the earlier 0.5-gray flying recipe. Current corrected-data/contrast validation records 242 Unity checks, six Python tests, 58 configs and the rebuilt macOS app. Earlier visibility/speed validation records the preceding rendering, arrival and config checks. Earlier continuation validation records 61 playback/render/pooling checks, 30 real four-rig terrain checks, 4,833 config/UI checks, 46 ControlScene → Swarm startup checks and 7,866 legacy dot checks passing. Source verification independently compares every ID, position and relative TimeExact value against the supplied raw CSV: all 14,429 rows match. Reproduce that audit with python3 tools/verify_swarm_source.py /path/to/Selwyn_Oct_7_2026_LongFormat.csv Assets/StreamingAssets/SwarmData/selwyn-oct7-unity.csv. The local 18-second preview at Builds/BogongSwarm-preview/swarm-playback-and-close-pass.mp4 is captured from Unity Play Mode at deterministic 120fps. It shows the asset at real time and 0.25x, six recorded-swarm camera faces, then ID 158's measured 17.7cm close pass and its extrapolated tail. Slow motion and the direction-following diagnostic camera are labelled. An 8×8 centre crop enlarges pixels without changing contrast; MP4 decoding was checked to retain the faint 248/255 and 254/255 pixels. Capture background/observer settings are diagnostic only; the video uses the earlier southeast presentation. The active main experiment now uses a gray standalone Swarm sky, north presentation, observer autopilot at 5 m/s and zero incoming lead-in. Converter tests: python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_convert_swarm_trajectories.py. SwarmTrajectoryValidation.Run on a disposable Unity copy checks 64×64 renders, 1 cm visibility, subpixel fading, flap poses, interpolation, lifetimes, world anchors, loops and metre/centimetre scale. Existing BogongDotValidation.Run and SelwynSwarmValidation.Run retain reference raster/timing checks. Timing results describe the test machine, not guaranteed LED workstation FPS. Saved results: 39 render/playback/prefab checks, 30 real Selwyn sequence checks, 4,743 strict catalog/UI checks, and 798,525 generated-swarm/reference checks passed in Unity 6000.3.16f1. The four-rig test verifies metre dimensions, 5 m/s autopilot, 5 m AGL, per-rig visibility, disabled camera letters and near-plane restoration. The isolated 1,024-agent test across 24 cameras at 64×64 measured median CPU times of 2.27 ms for dots and 2.89 ms for moths on an M2 Pro; these measurements exclude real display hardware and the full experiment frame.

title: Selwyn Milky Way / ordered swarm cycle
text: The full-duration reference Assets/StreamingAssets/Examples/Swarm/selwyn-milky-way-swarm-cycle.sequence.json runs the protocol below in Choice_Selwyn. Your active Assets/StreamingAssets/sequenceConfig.json retains the quick-test edits made during implementation: the first two blocks and heading window are 3 seconds, with gain 2.5 on those rows. The later swarm blocks are 240 seconds each. To run the full protocol, copy the reference sequence over Assets/StreamingAssets/sequenceConfig.json before Play. Open Assets/Scenes/ControlScene.unity, press Play, fill the original metadata form, then press Save/Start. Automatic start is off. Your system config, tracking addresses, camera order, resolution and FPS settings are retained. Block Seconds Sky Conspecifics Auto-trim 1: Setup 360 Current Selwyn Milky Way None On 2: Milky Way measurement 240 Current Selwyn Milky Way None Off 3: Milky Way + swarm 240 Current Selwyn Milky Way 150 Bogong moths per rig Off 4: Swarm only 240 Uniform gray RGB 0.12 150 Bogong moths per rig Off Setup runs once. The first pass lasts 18 minutes; subsequently blocks 2–4 repeat every 12 minutes, with auto-trim staying off. loopStartIndex: 1 (zero-based) returns to the Milky Way-only block. Index 1 means the second sequence row. Randomization is off because blocks 3 and 4 depend on block 2. reloadScene: false retains the same rigs across these blocks. Setup resets their positions/headings to (0,100,0) / north; later blocks retain pose. The calibrated yaw DC offset persists, including when auto-trim turns off. Flight variance gating and tuning are copied from the existing auto-trim calibration example. The dashboard can still control the current row. All four experiments enable autopilot at 7 m/s, with animal steering enabled and tracked translation disabled. Wind is zero and AGL is 100 m. Terrain scenes use metre world units: Unity +Z is north/forward, +X east, +Y up; positive yaw turns clockwise from north. This generated experiment does not read the recorded CSV or change its conversion. The three stellar blocks use latitude −35.894409, longitude 148.453948, Australia/Sydney, date: null, localTime: "now", and north yaw zero. UTC offset is resolved from that timezone, including daylight saving. The sky is regenerated on block entry and held between the configured 30-minute image updates. Exposure 0.1 and faint-detail cutoff 0.05 retain the existing generated moth recipe's settings. Block 4 replaces the Milky Way with an archived uniform gray image; the scene's authored terrain remains.

title: Config files and hierarchy
text: The full-duration sequence contains timing, order, loop start index, scene name, yaw gain 1, reload flag, auto-trim enable flag and each experiment file reference. All flight, sky, measurement and swarm parameters live in the individual experiment files: Examples/Swarm/selwyn-cycle-01-setup-full.example.json Examples/Swarm/selwyn-cycle-02-milky-way-full.example.json Examples/Swarm/selwyn-cycle-03-milky-way-swarm.example.json Examples/Swarm/selwyn-cycle-04-swarm-only.example.json The full-duration sequence is Examples/Swarm/selwyn-milky-way-swarm-cycle.sequence.json. These are complete flat Choice experiment configs, editable as JSON. The active quick-test sequence retains the original selwyn-cycle-01-setup.example.json and selwyn-cycle-02-milky-way.example.json names and your edits; their full-duration counterparts set the heading window to 240 seconds. Hardware remains in system_config.json. Existing generated and CSV examples remain available as separate recipes.

title: Heading measured during block 2
text: The measurement block contains: "headingReference": { "enabled": true, "windowSeconds": 240, "startOffsetSeconds": 0, "measureDuringPresentation": true, "saveAs": "milky-way-baseline" } Each rig samples its own virtual world yaw after movement once per frame, and computes the circular mean over that 240-second window. A 359°/1° pair averages north, rather than 180°. This is a mean of unit heading vectors, not a straight average of angles or a displacement-weighted direction. Resultant length and sample count are recorded; low resultant length does not extend or reject a trial. measureDuringPresentation: true runs observation and the sequence timer together. Block 2 therefore lasts 240 seconds, rather than an observation period followed by an additional 240-second presentation. The final observation completes before the sequence advances. On the experimental GUI branch, scene duration now takes precedence for both values of this retained flag; long observation windows are shortened at runtime without rewriting the JSON. In phased files, measurement remains in preStimulus, under the phase runner's timer. Both swarm blocks contain: "useHeadingReference": true, "headingReferenceId": "milky-way-baseline", "mu": 0 Thus each rig's swarm mean is that animal's saved mean from block 2 plus zero degrees. It is frozen in the world through both swarm blocks, even while the animal steers. This does not continuously steer the swarm toward the animal or recompute the mean in block 3. References are held by the session controller, separately by rig and name; they survive in-place block changes and scene reloads. They are cleared at start, stop and each sequence loop, so a previous cycle cannot supply the next baseline. Each repeat starts a fresh 240-second Milky Way measurement, without returning to trimming. Missing named references fail explicitly. Core validation rejects shuffled or reordered sequences that present a named swarm before measuring it. headingReference.jsonl records each rig's mean, resultant, sample count, observation times, trial/step, saved name and concurrent-measurement flag. Each swarm log header records its resolved world Mu, yaw/elevation kappa and sampler. The exact system, sequence and all four experiments are archived with the run; generated sky images and metadata are also saved.

title: Ordered motion with independent speeds and wing phases
text: Nested swarm parameter Active value Meaning numberOfLocusts 150 Moth count per rig; four rigs give 600 total. Legacy field name retained. trajectoryFile empty Generated distribution; no recorded data input. locustSpeed 6.17 Mean speed, m/s in this terrain scene. locustSpeedStdDev 1.24 Speed standard deviation, m/s; not variance. directionDistribution VonMises Corrected normalized circular sampler. kappa 1000 in block 3; 100 in block 4 Yaw concentration around the frozen baseline; retains your later tuning. muElevation 0 Mean horizontal motion; positive Unity pitch points downward. kappaElevation 100 Elevation concentration. Combined order is about 99.45% with yaw kappa 1000, or 99% with yaw kappa 100. volumeHalfExtentMetres 2 Moving cube ±2 m on all axes, side 4 m, volume 64 m³. spawnRelativeToAnimal, followAnimalPosition true Cube centered on the current animal; mean direction stays frozen. preserveBoundaryOvershoot, wrapY true Exact periodic wrapping on all three cube axes. agentVisual, bogongVisual.shape Bogong, Moth Physical cigar body and one coupled wing pair. bodyLengthMetres, bodyDiameterMetres, wingSpanMetres 0.03, 0.01, 0.06 Perspective body and wing dimensions. flapFrequencyHz 30 GPU wing motion with independently randomized phases. sizeMode, subpixelVisibility World, true Physical perspective; contrast attenuation below pixel resolution. Speeds are independent nonnegative normal samples taken once per agent; a rare negative draw is resampled. Headings/elevations are independently sampled once at spawn. Steady motion retains those directions and speeds. Periodic boundaries recirculate the finite population; no per-frame random direction changes or synchronized spawning/flapping are imposed. Observer motion is subtracted naturally by world-relative geometry: a moth at the observer's speed/direction remains near it, and faster/slower moths pass. The historical direction sampler has a broad tail: kappa 1000 does not give its mathematically expected high concentration, while kappa ≥10000 forces exactly parallel motion. It is preserved for old configs using omitted/default directionDistribution: "Legacy". The new cycle opts into "VonMises", using the normalized rejection sampler. Your current block 3 tuning raises yaw kappa to 1000 (about 1.81° yaw SD); block 4 retains yaw kappa 100. Yaw kappa 100 has about 5.74° SD and resultant 0.995; adding independent elevation kappa 100 gives about 0.990 3D directional order. This is an order parameter, not a guarantee that 99% of individuals have identical headings. Higher kappa narrows the spread without the legacy point-mass cutoff.

title: Visible population and contrast
text: Six square 90° views cover directions around the animal; for a uniform cube centered on it, each face receives about one sixth of the population. 150 agents → about 25 geometric moth positions per view. It is editable in both swarm block files. Density is 2.344 agents/m³. Natural counts fluctuate; the implementation does not insert/remove moths to clamp each view to a count or force near passes. Turning changes which moths are visible, while the cube stays centered. In the deterministic two-minute test at observer speed 7 m/s, the six view means ranged 24.1–25.8. About 77.5% of camera frames contained 20–30 positions. A natural closest approach was 2.74 cm. These are one realization's statistics, not guaranteed rates. Geometric view counts do not mean 25 equally clear silhouettes on a 64×64 panel. Far moths still fade with projected coverage, and visibility depends on body orientation, pixel placement and sky contrast. The earlier native physical-moth test reached half full contrast between sampled distances 1 and 1.5 m; the cube retains the requested minimum 2 m half extent. There is no hard radial cutoff at 2 m; cube corners are 3.46 m away. Close 10 cm wing views and far fading use the existing rendering fixes, without enlarging moths or adding wing pairs. See generated moth rendering.

title: Validation and performance
text: Assets/Editor/SelwynSwarmCycleValidation.cs runs in the marked disposable validation project. It validates the full-duration reference files and tests the original ControlScene Save/Start button, in-place transitions, auto-trim flags, retained rigs/DC offsets, circular per-rig means, frozen reuse after steering, sky modes, cycle reset, misordered/shuffled references, exact coordinate recording and population statistics. The observation window is shortened only in the disposable copy; sequence durations and runtime assertions use the full-duration reference values, without modifying the main checkout's active quick-test configuration. This is an accelerated transition test, not a complete live hardware run. The normalized distribution test samples 100,000 independent yaw/elevation pairs. The recording benchmark exercises four 150-agent swarms and 24 actual 64×64 cameras, including pooled capture and asynchronous gzip output. It verifies every final coordinate against its presented transform and requires no dropped frames, pending backlog or steady main-thread managed allocation. Results and machine details are in selwyn-swarm-cycle-validation-results.json. Timings cover CPU movement/upload/capture/render submission; they exclude terrain rendering, GPU completion, tracking and physical panels, so they do not guarantee live 120 FPS. The existing system target remains 120 FPS. These features are on codex/bogong-night-sky, using the original metadata form and existing status overlay. The experimental configuration GUI stays on its separate UI branch. On the tested non-GUI branch, the 600-moth/24-camera recording benchmark submitted 170,400 rows without drops. Median CPU movement/upload/capture/render submission was 3.01 ms; pooled coordinate capture was 0.158 ms. Native renderer tests passed 100,319 checks; the legacy five-scene phase suite passed 85,479, and recorded trajectory/continuation passed 99.

title: Terrain cue lab: separate visual and navigation rugosity
text: Use the four TerrainChoice spatial layouts and the treatment sequences below for the choice experiment. Scene identity, spatial terrain pattern, and experimental condition are separate concepts. Each new scene is a thin instance of the same shared environment prefab; trees, material, mesh references, controller and standard configured camera rig are edited once. Existing RS/navrug scenes are not renamed or repurposed. The earlier Assets/Scenes/Rugosity_RS.unity, its GUID, meshes and six choice files remain unchanged and runnable with Examples/Rugosity/sequence-legacy-rugosity.json. The sixteen-case visual audit verifies the actual camera renders and mesh/navigation assignments, including exact 128×128 frames. It also documents that the photographic texture masks the small geometric relief: correct routing is not a claim of strong perceptual visual contrast. The four both-flat controls intentionally remain identical. New surface IDs paired with the stock legacy Rugosity_RS scene now produce a pre-start configuration error. The Bogong night-sky improvements were already inherited on this branch. The terrain work adds optional behavior; scenes without an enabled RugosityWorld keep their original movement behavior.

title: The four primary conditions
text: Vector schematic. The figure uses actual Unity mesh samples and rig poses, exported by RugosityValidation, rather than a separate idealized drawing. Blue is rendered terrain; dashed orange is navigation/collision terrain; purple arrows show eye position and the forward direction as the agent moves from left to right. The vertical scale is exaggerated. The clearance is vertical, not measured along the normal. Condition / choice file Visual surface Navigation surface Agent behavior matched-flat.json Flat Flat Fixed height, level orientation matched-terrain.json RoughSmooth RoughSmooth Follows terrain height and normal: the canonical ant walk visual-terrain_navigation-flat.json RoughSmooth Flat Sees bumps, moves horizontally with level orientation visual-flat_navigation-terrain.json Flat RoughSmooth Sees a plane, rises/falls and tilts with hidden terrain All four use AboveGround height, SurfaceNormal orientation, 1 cm clearance, and no spatial or temporal normal smoothing. A flat navigation surface naturally has a constant normal; the same controller can therefore be used for all four conditions. The last two change only the geometry assignments. Pitch moves a flat horizon vertically and roll tilts it; these are distinct from irregularities in a visible terrain silhouette. “Looks rough / feels smooth” is shorthand for the third condition. Here navigation rugosity means the movement of the camera rig; perceived roughness remains an experimental outcome.

title: Spatial pattern is independent of the condition
text: Registered surface IDs spell out left-to-right spatial structure. They do not encode visual/navigation pairings: Surface ID Negative X region Positive X region RoughSmooth Rough Smooth SmoothRough Smooth Rough RoughRough Rough Rough SmoothSmooth Smooth Smooth Flat Exactly planar Exactly planar The mixed patterns transition continuously from X = −5 to +5 cm. Smooth is low rugosity, not an atomically flat plane. The new demonstration uses maximum rough extrusion 0.8 cm and smooth extrusion 0.025 cm, so all four conditions stay above the visible ground at 1 cm clearance. The earlier 4 cm bumps could intersect a 1 cm flat camera path; the previous lab and examples retain their original geometry for compatibility. Select any pattern independently for visual and navigation surfaces. To reverse the spatial pattern in a sequence without changing scene names: { "sceneName": "TerrainCueLab", "duration": 30, "reloadScene": false, "parameters": { "configFile": "Examples/Rugosity/matched-terrain.json", "rugosity": { "visualSurface": "SmoothRough", "collisionSurface": "SmoothRough" } } } Examples/Rugosity/sequence-spatial-patterns.json demonstrates all four non-flat spatial patterns. Each assignment is a surface ID registered on this scene's RugosityWorld, not an asset filename or a global object-name search.

title: Load one treatment and run all four spatial patterns
text: The four ready-to-load treatment sequences below each run RoughSmooth → SmoothRough → SmoothSmooth → RoughRough, for 30 seconds each. They all use the same terrain-treatment.json base configuration. The four named scenes are thin instances of Assets/TerrainCueLab/TerrainChoiceWorld.prefab, so there are no duplicated environment contents or navigation meshes to maintain. Choose one sequence file in the app, then press Start experiment; loading it does not start automatically. Each sequence stops after the fourth trial. Scene Left half (negative X) Right half (positive X) TerrainChoice_RoughLeft_SmoothRight Rough Smooth TerrainChoice_SmoothLeft_RoughRight Smooth Rough TerrainChoice_BothSmooth Smooth Smooth TerrainChoice_BothRough Rough Rough The animal starts at the center, facing +Z, with two identical placeholder trees at X = −40/+40 cm and Z = +60 cm. Their distance from the start is equal (about 72.1 cm), and they sit on opposite sides of the rough/smooth boundary. Edit their shared appearance once in Assets/TerrainCueLab/TerrainChoiceTarget.prefab; edit shared positions or geometry once in TerrainChoiceWorld.prefab. The named scene instances override only the authored default surface pattern. Sequence JSON independently assigns the actual visible and navigation surfaces, including the flat alternative, so four scenes cover all sixteen combinations. Sequence file under Examples/Rugosity/ Visible surface Navigation/collision surface sequence-treatment-matched-terrain.json Current spatial pattern Current spatial pattern sequence-treatment-visual-terrain_navigation-flat.json Current spatial pattern Flat sequence-treatment-visual-flat_navigation-terrain.json Flat Current spatial pattern sequence-treatment-matched-flat.json Flat Flat The first three treatments retain all four meaningful spatial patterns. In the both-flat treatment, the four trials intentionally have identical geometry: the spatial pattern is a counterbalancing label, preserved in each row's _comment in the recorded sequence snapshot. This does not silently add invisible bumps to a flat-navigation condition. Change shared motion, clearance, orientation, or stimulus defaults once in terrain-treatment.json. Each sequence overrides only the two surface assignments; empty heightSurface and normalSurface inherit the selected collision surface. Change a trial's duration in its sequence as needed. The treatment presets use real tracking by default: closedLoopPosition and closedLoopOrientation are enabled and autopilotEnabled is disabled. Initialize and verify the tracker before starting. For a hardware-free walkthrough, temporarily enable autopilot and disable both closed-loop flags in that shared file, or use the older sequence-spatial-patterns.json bench example.

title: Press Play or tune in the Editor
text: For the older linear walkthrough, choose Examples/Rugosity/sequence.json through ControlScene. It runs the four main conditions followed by three isolation controls, 30 seconds each, looping. Each condition starts at X = −60, Z = 0, facing +X, and moves at 5 cm/s. This crosses the rough/smooth boundary automatically. Arrow keys and A/D allow movement and steering; Ctrl+Space toggles autopilot. Turning or reverse input changes the route. Files under Assets/StreamingAssets/Examples/Rugosity/: sequence.json: seven walkthrough conditions. sequence-four-conditions.json: only the four primary mesh combinations. sequence-spatial-patterns.json: matched visual/navigation geometry with four spatial patterns. sequence-legacy-rugosity.json: the earlier six conditions in the unchanged Rugosity_RS scene. The previous Selwyn sequence remains at Examples/Sequences/selwyn-before-rugosity.json. For direct authoring, use Tools → Rugosity → Open terrain cue lab, or open Assets/Scenes/TerrainCueLab.unity. Select Terrain cues — select to tune: Press Play and edit the surface dropdowns, height/orientation modes, clearance and normal response. Changes apply live without restarting. If running a sequence, choose InspectorOnly to prevent the next trial from replacing your tuning. Builds always honor JSON. Keep current settings in scene after Stop captures the current snapshot and restores it after Play ends. Save the scene afterward. Click again if you change more settings before stopping. Copy effective rugosity JSON copies the settings. Save rugosity into choice JSON… preserves the other choice fields; phased documents receive stimulus.rugosity. The lab's authored scene pose remains the canonical linear walkthrough. Its cameras now use the standard configured rig: start through ControlScene so a MainController supplies the apparatus layout. A directly opened scene without a loaded system configuration keeps stimulus cameras disabled, matching other configured scenes. In Edit mode, changing the Inspector updates visibility/collider roles; Preview pose at current rig positions applies height and orientation and supports Undo. Existing RS scenes do not acquire this component automatically.

title: Apparatus routing and recordings
text: The earlier lab used a hand-created fullscreen camera with no ViewportSetter and no DataLogger. That bypassed configured LED face order, pixel dimensions, display offsets and rig duplication, and could produce a run with no playable pose rows. TerrainCueLab and the four new scenes now share the ordinary VR1 prefab, including ViewportSetter, ClosedLoop and DataLogger. RuntimeRigRegistry creates the configured number of animals; every clone is discovered by the terrain controller. Each rig therefore uses the system JSON's camera allow-list, display routing and panel rectangles. Desktop preview uses its configured single front view. The runtime test TerrainChoiceRuntimeValidation.Run checks real MainController transitions for all sixteen treatment/pattern combinations using one LED rig, four horizontal LED rigs, four vertical LED rigs, and one desktop rig. It reports the batch editor’s actual Game view extent and verifies normalized camera rectangles, contained panel pixel sizes, face order and target displays, shared target placement, terrain following, per-animal CSV pose rows, saved scene/surface context and replay reconstruction. It uses explicitly generated stationary input; it does not establish physical camera accuracy or animal-tracking calibration. The validator writes results into its disposable project's terrain-choice-runtime-validation folder. Because a batch Game view may be shorter than the real monitor, full-panel physical pixel coverage is checked separately in the native Mac player; offscreen editor panels are counted explicitly rather than claimed as a Full HD pass. Verified 27 October 2026: runtime validation results passed 3,193 checks across 64 actual sequence trials, with 22,485 playable pose rows across the ten configured animal tracks. Every track contains all sixteen scene/treatment contexts; recorded height and orientation agree with the selected navigation mesh, and saved replay configuration restores the inline surface overrides. The run also passed 384 contained-panel pixel checks and explicitly deferred 320 offscreen batch-editor checks to native-player validation. Sixteen actual camera renders were inspected locally, including matched, visual-only, navigation-only and flat controls. The shared ground material now uses the original 4096 × 4096 forest-floor albedo recovered from the packed images in ~/Downloads/nav_rug_rr.blend. The JPEG bytes are preserved in Assets/TerrainCueLab/ForestFloorAlbedo.jpg; provenance and checksums are in terrain-texture-provenance.json. The packed normal map is deliberately unused so it cannot add apparent normal-map bumps to a flat visual condition. The earlier checker texture remains available as GroundPattern.asset, and legacy Rugosity_RS materials are unchanged. A rendered surround extends the visible ground to 1 km so a nearby square boundary does not produce a false kink in a flat horizon. This surround has no collider and does not extend the 200 × 200 cm navigation footprint.

title: Configuration and isolation controls
text: Navigation normally uses collisionSurface for both height and orientation. Keep heightSurface and normalSurface empty for the four primary conditions: { "objects": [], "closedLoopPosition": false, "closedLoopOrientation": false, "initialPosition": { "x": -60, "y": 1, "z": 0 }, "initialRotation": { "x": 0, "y": 90, "z": 0 }, "resetPositionOnStart": true, "resetRotationOnStart": true, "autopilotEnabled": true, "autopilotSpeed": 5, "rugosity": { "enabled": true, "visualSurface": "RoughSmooth", "collisionSurface": "Flat", "heightSurface": "", "normalSurface": "", "heightMode": "AboveGround", "orientationMode": "SurfaceNormal", "centimetersPerUnit": 1, "clearanceCm": 1, "normalRadiusCm": 0, "normalSamples": 5, "tiltResponse": 0 } } Optional overrides separate the camera's height and orientation effects: Choice file Height Orientation Purpose control-height-only.json AGL over RoughSmooth, despite Flat collision WorldUp Up/down movement without pitch/roll control-tilt-only.json Absolute world Y = 1 RoughSmooth normal Tilt without vertical movement; Flat visual surface control-fixed-pose.json Absolute world Y = 1 WorldUp Visible RoughSmooth geometry with fixed height and level orientation The old visual-rs-level-agl.json is the earlier height-only experiment, not a pure flat-navigation condition: it deliberately follows the visible RS terrain for height despite Flat collision. It remains supported with that explicit meaning. Precedence at every trial/phase boundary is authored scene settings → choice/phase patch → sequence patch. Omitted or null fields preserve the authored baseline; an empty height/normal ID means “inherit collision.” A new trial starts from the authored baseline, so previous overrides do not leak. Config is not reapplied every frame; Inspector changes remain until the next boundary. enabled: false restores authored renderer/collider states and releases pose control. Disabling the component also releases control without changing other scenes. Setting Meaning visualSurface Rendered geometry collisionSurface Physical collider set and default navigation reference heightSurface / normalSurface Optional independent references for isolation controls heightMode AboveGround adds clearance to the reference; Absolute uses fixed world Y orientationMode SurfaceNormal follows the reference normal; WorldUp removes pitch/roll clearanceCm Vertical clearance, in centimeters centimetersPerUnit 1 for centimeter scenes; 100 for meter scenes absoluteHeight Fixed world Y in scene units normalRadiusCm Spatial averaging radius; 0 samples the center alone normalSamples Additional ring samples, 1–32 tiltResponse 0 is exact; positive values smooth the up vector, in inverse seconds Heading is preserved even while orientation is smoothed. Keyboard/autopilot and tracking translation use a horizontal movement frame while the terrain controller owns the pose. Terrain-induced pitch/roll therefore does not reduce horizontal speed or introduce steering. Legacy delayed pose resets are skipped for explicitly enabled rugosity trials. MigrationMotion retains its wind but yields height correction while rugosity is active.

title: Use existing terrain assets
text: A RugositySurface explicitly registers Terrain components, MeshFilters for sampling, Renderers for appearance and Colliders for physical roles. Register alternatives on a RugosityWorld; assign rig targets or let it find this scene's ClosedLoop rigs. Keep GameObjects active so visibility and collision remain independent. Do not include unrelated trees, animals or scenery in these arrays. Sampling reads the assigned geometry even when hidden or when its colliders are disabled. This is a kinematic ground follower, not a Rigidbody locomotion or wall/cave solver. Meshes need Read/Write enabled. TerrainData supports holes and boundaries and must remain world-up. Mesh sampling supports transforms/nonuniform scale; call InvalidateGeometry() after modifying vertex data in place. The highest vertical ground intersection is selected. Missing ground or walking outside the navigation footprint retains the last valid position. Custom geometry can intersect a requested camera path. There is no automatic visual-ground avoidance, since that would change the experimental condition. Choose heights and clearances deliberately; the supplied new profiles avoid that intersection at the default 1 cm clearance. Hidden navigation geometry is not baked into or substituted for the visible source mesh. Effective config and Inspector changes are recorded as RUGOSITY_STATE messages and, with a MasterDataLogger, appended to rugosity_states.jsonl with UTC time and frame number. The normal config archive preserves the input files.

title: Reproducible checks
text: Use a disposable project copy containing the KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY marker. The runners may rewrite test sequence/system configs there. Do not run them against the authoring project. Unity -batchmode -projectPath /path/to/disposable-copy \ -executeMethod RugosityValidation.Run -logFile /tmp/terrain-cues.log Unity -batchmode -projectPath /path/to/disposable-copy \ -executeMethod RugosityValidation.RunLegacy -logFile /tmp/terrain-cues-legacy.log Unity -batchmode -projectPath /path/to/disposable-copy \ -executeMethod TerrainCueSequenceValidation.Run -logFile /tmp/terrain-cues-sequence.log Do not add -quit; the runners exit after Play/Edit checks. Restore the active sequence from the example before testing the full sequence runner, because it shortens durations in its disposable copy. The new checks compare sampled heights to independent Unity MeshCollider ray intersections, verify the four spatial profiles, clearance above visible geometry, renderer/collider selection, heading under smoothing, centimeter conversion, transformed meshes, hidden TerrainData, bounds, Inspector/config precedence and retention after Stop. Autopilot traversal goes through actual Keyboard movement and LateUpdate. A separate run starts ControlScene and advances all seven trials through the real MainController. The unchanged older scene is tested with its original six files. Results and native camera renders are kept beside this guide. terrain-cue-cross-sections.json records the sampled geometry and poses used by tools/draw_terrain_cues.py to regenerate the PNG/SVG schematic. Hardware timing and live tracking are outside these checks.

title: Verified on 25 October 2026
text: Unity 6000.3.16f1: 4,570 new-lab checks passed, including independent collider intersections, synthetic tracking displacement, analytic normal checks, 60 traversal frames per condition, and keeping Inspector settings after Stop. Original Rugosity_RS scene: 2,391 checks passed with its six unchanged configs. Actual ControlScene auto-start: 43 checks passed across all seven conditions, using shortened durations only in the disposable copy. Inherited Choice/night-sky regression: 70 checks passed. Static validation: 84 JSON templates/examples, 88 scene/catalog dependency files, unique GUIDs, preserved archive hashes and build registration passed. On the measured new-lab traversal, matched terrain and hidden terrain both moved from approximately 1.002 to 1.799 cm in world Y with up to 9.53° tilt. Flat navigation stayed at 1 cm with 0° tilt despite the visible bumps. The height-only and tilt-only controls isolate those effects as intended.

title: Historical Adaminaby sky preset
text: The Adaminaby experiment was added on BogongAustralia in commit ef8a68b2ad2ff690e803007511666296a31eda5a (also present as d9f9810bb5eb9da31392dc2017ce82f5692b2bb5). That commit contains an image and a Choice configuration, not a separate Adaminaby Unity scene. Both files are restored here: Assets/StreamingAssets/Photosphere/adaminaby.png: original image bytes, Git blob 92d7a4e0d0cfcd3bd297bf56d62905aee59aa3d3. The image's metadata GUID is restored from f36f318c88186f646f61e8fdb9bbea9fd03ab0f8. Assets/StreamingAssets/choice__SM_adaminaby.json: original settings, with the trailing comma removed for valid JSON. It has no spawned objects, enables closed-loop orientation and position, starts at (0, 10.7, 0), and randomizes the initial yaw.

title: Run from ControlScene
text: Save your current Assets/StreamingAssets/sequenceConfig.json if you want to return to it later. Copy Assets/StreamingAssets/Examples/Sequences/adaminaby-historical.example.json over Assets/StreamingAssets/sequenceConfig.json. Use the local system configuration for your rig. To enable Front, Back, Left, Right, Up and Down, use the six-camera setup. Open Assets/Scenes/ControlScene.unity and press Play. The template automatically starts the current Choice scene for one hour. Escape returns to ControlScene. Edit duration or set autoStart to false as needed. The new sequence is an adaptation for the current scene and loader. It does not depend on the old Choice_Bogong terrain scene and its missing terrain assets. Adding this preset does not change the active automatic Bogong preview sequence. Choice applies the selected skybox to every rig face, including Up cameras with legacy local skybox overrides. Clearing the skybox or destroying the Choice controller restores the previous camera clear flags, local overrides and scene material. Loading an image does not change which faces the system config enables.

title: Source image limitations
text: The historical image is a 3024 × 1890 Stellarium screenshot, including its toolbar and status text. The status text says Canberra, 2025-12-08 23:30:28 UTC+11:00, and 180° FOV. Its filename is Adaminaby, but it is not a calibrated Adaminaby panorama or a 2:1 equirectangular export. The existing Choice loader maps the whole screenshot onto Unity's panoramic skybox, so the UI and projection distortion remain visible. This is a fixed historical image: it does not follow the current date, time or location, regenerate every 30 minutes, or create the astronomical skybox archive. For the current Adaminaby sky, exported panoramas and load-time records, use the Bogong astronomical skybox setup.

title: Validation
text: Run AdaminabyValidation.Run through Unity 6000.3.16f1 with graphics enabled on a disposable project copy containing the marker file KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY. The check installs this sequence and the six-camera system template into that copy, starts ControlScene in Play mode, verifies the loaded image pixels, renders all 24 camera views, and checks restoration after repeated loads, an empty skybox and controller destruction. It also covers an inactive face and a camera with a solid-color background. Results and a six-face contact sheet are written to the copy's project root. The restoration passed 78 checks with all 24 views rendered; see validation results.

title: Recording pipeline
text: A session is a bundle of evidence. Animal pose CSVs alone cannot identify all presented stimuli, gains, original inputs or sky orientation. Preserve the whole directory or complete ZIP together with the software version.

title: Before the experiment starts
text: MasterDataLogger establishes a unique timestamped session folder, adding a numeric suffix when a directory or ZIP already exists. RunConfigArchive captures the system and sequence and recursively follows the referenced config/input graph. The studio starts a fresh configured session from the selected system/sequence documents rather than appending new metadata to an old completed run. The archive retains readable first copies and immutable content-addressed snapshots. If a file changes between actual loads, both versions remain; the manifest distinguishes captured files from the exact versions consumed and records scene/load attribution. It never overwrites the earlier bytes as if the new version had always been the experiment.

title: The saved layout
text: RunData/<session>/ AnimalMetadata.json FlyMetaData.json transitional equivalent metadata system_config.json sequenceConfig.json config_manifest.json Configs/ Files/... readable first copies Snapshots/<SHA-256>.* exact immutable versions Skyboxes/ <skyboxId>.png <skyboxId>.json usage.jsonl loads.csv ... animal / population CSV and gzip logs runtime_trace.log Resource catalog names for built prefabs/materials are not external files. Referenced experiment/design JSON, trajectory files with metadata sidecars and explicit sky images are captured as files where supported. Generated sky images have their own activation provenance.

title: During the run
text: Animal/world loggers sample the rendered rig pose with scene, trial, sequence/inner-step and experiment-phase context. Optional sensor columns retain the receiver's input representation. Position is the virtual rig's world pose, which can contain autopilot, wind or terrain effects as well as measured tracking. Swarm recording captures population snapshots in LateUpdate and sends immutable pooled data to a bounded worker. That worker formats, gzips and writes. Pending queue overflow/dropped frames are diagnostic evidence; sampling a transform every rendered frame does not establish an independent fixed-frequency acquisition clock. Kannadi, band and Optomotor loggers add their own stimulus context. Do not interpret a drum transform or one replicated model root as another measured animal. Headers and data-column counts differ by format and historical version.

title: Phase and stimulus attribution
text: Rows retain experimentPhase where supported. Heading-reference and phase-onset JSONL records describe actual transitions and frozen references. Managed sky IDs join animal/population rows to the exact archived panorama and manifest. Rugosity state records document effective pose/geometry choices and Inspector changes in source workflows. The configuration manifest records load boundaries; it is not a per-frame world-state recorder. Playback cannot recover an unlogged random state or an exact historical pixel merely from a current file with the same basename.

title: Shutdown and ZIP creation
text: The archive boundary closes ordinary loggers, drains asynchronous population writers and completes gzip trailers before ZIP creation. The original session folder remains if zipping fails. Stopping the process uncleanly can still lose buffered/in-flight work, so retain the trace and original directory when investigating an interrupted session.

title: Interpretation rules
text: Use column names and the actual header rather than assuming one fixed row width across versions. Use timestamp differences, inspect gaps/duplicates, and retain the workstation's timezone context for historical local wall-clock rows.
