Distinguish raw tracker units, converted sensor display values and virtual world units. Preserve resets/wraps as discontinuities before estimating speed or paths. Read canonical Animals once; transitional metadata aliases describe the same animals and must not be counted again.

title: Source and detailed schema
text: MasterDataLogger, RunConfigArchive, data formats, run snapshots, replay.

title: Recorded data and units
text: Recorded swarm input uses ID,X,Y,Z,time with Unity axes (+X east, +Y up, +Z north), metres, and relative seconds. See swarm-playback.md. Presented/logged positions use the scene's world units: metres on terrain/migration, centimetres in walking scenes. The input CSV scale and physical moth scale are configured independently. MasterDataLogger creates Assets/RunData/yyyyMMdd_HHmmss/ in the Editor (current standalone source uses RuntimePaths.RunDataRoot, default <player directory>/MATREX VR RunData beside the app or executable; a protected installation uses Application.persistentDataPath/Installations/<installation-id>/RunData. --data-dir overrides either location. Earlier standalone builds used the shared Application.persistentDataPath/RunData; 0.1/0.2 retain Application.dataPath/RunData). A numeric suffix is added if that timestamp already has a folder or ZIP. It snapshots the system, sequence and referenced experiment files before the sequence starts, and retains exact versions consumed on later loads. A session ZIP is attempted after writers drain; the original folder remains available if ZIP creation fails. See run configuration snapshots for the layout, manifest and historical audit. Keep this bundle alongside exported data: it defines gains, stimulus conditions, camera layout and physical scale. Sampling is once per rendered Update, not a fixed Hz acquisition clock. Disk buffering flushes about every 0.5 seconds; clean scene exit flushes remaining rows. Wall-clock timestamps are local machine time and contain milliseconds, without a timezone offset. Record the workstation timezone and synchronize machines for cross-device analysis. Do not assume rows are evenly spaced or use row number as elapsed time. Swarm position snapshots are captured in LateUpdate after generated movement; CSV formatting, gzip and disk writes run on a worker. They retain sample-time metadata and drain on clean exit. The dashboard reports queue overflow/dropped frames. Embedded Choice/Selwyn swarms also record all presented agent positions in one gzip file per rig/population.

title: Rig CSV (*_VRn_.csv)
text: DataLogger emits a header and comma-separated rows. The rig's transform is the world pose, not raw tracker coordinates. Column Meaning / units Current Time Local yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff. VR Rig object name. Scene Actual loaded Unity scene. CurrentSequenceScene Configured outer sequence scene. ConfigFile Experiment file referenced by configFile; blank for a design-only dynamic step. CurrentTrial Outer sequence trial counter. CurrentStep Zero-based execution-order position, not necessarily index in the original randomized list. GameObjectPosX/Y/Z World units (cm for the current walking scenes). X right, Y up, Z forward. GameObjectRotX/Y/Z Euler degrees, wrapped 0–360. Y is yaw; positive yaw turns +Z toward +X. SensPosX/Y/Z Raw position values received over ZMQ, before sphere scaling or X/Y remapping. Not already world centimeters. SensRotX/Y/Z Euler degrees obtained from the received pose quaternion: pitch, yaw, roll respectively. stepIndex, stepName Inner dynamic step index/name; index starts at -1 when unused. loopIndex, cumulativeStep Inner loop and cumulative-step counters. swapElapsedSec Seconds since dynamic step start when a color swap was recorded; event field, otherwise blank. swapWallClock Local wall time of that swap. grayAtTrialStart Normalized starting gray intensity for adaptive trials. blackSideAtTrialStart Adaptive trial side label. skyboxId SHA-256 ID of the active managed Swarm/Kannadi sky. Join to Skyboxes/<id>.json and .png; otherwise blank. skyboxSampleUtc Astronomical sample time as ISO-8601 UTC; blank for an explicit image or no managed sky. yawDCOffsetDegrees, yawDCCompensationDegPerSecond DC angle in degrees and its gain-scaled term subtracted from untrimmed yaw in deg/s; raw DC columns remain for compatibility. autoTrimMeanDegPerSecond, autoTrimUncertaintyDegPerSecond, autoTrimMeasurementSeconds Latest evaluated mean under the applied offset, approximate two-standard-error uncertainty, and active qualified window length. Blank before a full initial window. autoTrimEnabled, autoTrimState Kinefly automatic centering flag/state. Blank for unsupported tracking modes. flightDetected, flightVarianceRadiansSquared Flight decision and population variance of raw L−R before gain/offset; blank until the flight window is ready. autoTrimMedianDegPerSecond, autoTrimPasses Last evaluated effective median under the applied offset, and correction count in the current row/configuration. Median is blank while no complete qualified window is available. flightCheckEnabled, flightThresholdRadiansSquared, flightSamples Actual flight gate flag, entry threshold in rad² and distinct samples in the rolling flight window; measured flight remains independent of a bypass. experimentPhase Experiment state at row sampling: preStimulus, stimulus, or postStimulus. Flat experiments use stimulus; legacy flat heading observation uses assessment. Outside a running experiment: idle; failed experiment: error. experimentPhase is appended after the existing rig columns, including on Optomotor/other loggers using the base schema. It is recorded on every row, before disk buffering, so no event-log join is needed. Existing CurrentStep, stepIndex, stepName and band VisibilityPhase retain their original meanings. For example: import pandas as pd rows = pd.read_csv("your_VR1_.csv") pre = rows[rows["experimentPhase"] == "preStimulus"] stim = rows[rows["experimentPhase"] == "stimulus"] post = rows[rows["experimentPhase"] == "postStimulus"] The value uses the same state source as live telemetry's system.phase. It describes the state at the logger's sampling callback; phase transitions occur in LateUpdate. Historical CSVs collected before this column was added remain unchanged. Sensor columns are present only when includeZmqData is enabled on the logger. A stale packet holds the last pose, and the CSV does not currently include a freshness/validity column. A stationary logged pose alone cannot distinguish stationary behavior from packet loss; use runtime_trace.log and the original tracker stream.

title: ZMQ input contract
text: ZmqListener subscribes to a TCP publisher using two frames: a topic frame followed by JSON with x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw. The receiver preserves the raw wire rotation values alongside the existing walking Pose. The walking path interprets those values as degrees; the restored Bogong/Kinefly path reads signed raw radians, without quaternion conversion or wrapping. ClosedLoop takes sensor y as Unity X displacement and sensor x as Unity Z displacement, rotates this by the reset heading offset, then scales by sphereDiameter/2 and the optional locust position gain. For FicTrac ball calibration to yield centimeters, the displacement stream must contain cumulative ball angular displacement in radians, not an already converted cm position or a velocity. Confirm the publisher's convention before connecting another tracker. Sensor Z is logged but not used for walking translation. Orientation uses Unity Y/yaw; the Swarm/Kannadi walking path applies wrapped yaw deltas at unit gain unless a Swarm/Kannadi numeric gain explicitly overrides it. Rotation is not rate-limited or multiplied by frame duration. The migration wind/AGL adjustment is visible in the world transform columns but does not alter sensor columns. Kinefly instead integrates gain * (rawYawRadians - yawDCOffsetRadians) * Rad2Deg * deltaTime, matching BogongAustralia. A held value keeps turning between packets, including after a disconnect, as in that implementation. For Kinefly, SensRotX/Y/Z again contain Euler display angles calculated from the raw radians, and SensRotXRad/YRad/ZRad preserve the raw radians, matching the historical logger. The walking sensor columns keep their previous values. Use the added trackingImplementation, trackingMode, trackingInputUnits, wireYaw, yawGain, yawDCOffsetRadians, and yawOutputDegPerSecond columns to identify the calculation used. wireYaw is the untouched received value; its unit is given by trackingInputUnits. Kinefly rate output is blank outside yaw mode.

title: Kannadi clone logs (*Kannadi*Clones.csv.gz)
text: Gzip CSV with columns: Timestamp,VRIndex,CloneIndex,CloneName,PositionX,PositionY,PositionZ,RotationX,RotationY,RotationZ,NumberOfRings,hexRadius,skyboxId,skyboxSampleUtc,experimentPhase Each row is one visible-model root per frame. VRIndex is the configured numeric rig identifier (historically 1–4); CloneIndex is zero-based and can change when a grid is rebuilt. Positions are world cm, rotations are Euler degrees, hexRadius is world cm, NumberOfRings is an integer. A clone root can contain a whole mirrored band; it is not necessarily a single mesh/animal. Numeric clone values use invariant decimal points.

title: Swarm and band logs
text: Historical Swarm gzip CSV uses nine row columns: Timestamp,Name,Layer,X,Y,Z,skyboxId,skyboxSampleUtc,experimentPhase. Its header then appends NumberOfLocusts:..., SpawnAreaSize:..., Mu:..., Kappa:..., LocustSpeed:... as header metadata, not per-row columns. New 0.3 files append RotationX,RotationY,RotationZ after experimentPhase, yielding twelve data columns while retaining the old nine-column prefix. Parse column names and the appended metadata separately; older files have six, eight or nine data columns. Units: X/Y/Z and area size in scene world units (cm in walking scenes, m on terrain), mu in degrees, kappa dimensionless, speed in world units/s. Pre-0.3 logs contain positions without heading columns; their missing headings cannot be recovered as measurements. Current logs append recorded Euler rotations in degrees. New headers additionally include LocustSpeedStdDev in world units/s, DirectionDistribution and KappaElevation; the existing data-column prefix is unchanged. LocustSpeed is the generated population mean, not each individual's sampled speed. The archived experiment specifies the distribution; successive recorded positions give the realized motion. Periodic crossings jump across the cube and must be unwrapped before estimating speed. Embedded Choice populations create a new per-rig file when a phase rebuilds them. See night-sky.md for the Skyboxes/ image/manifest files, usage.jsonl activation audit, and loads.csv load history. Each load records the previous/new IDs, panorama filename, actual load time and represented sky time in UTC and observer-local time with an explicit offset. These are included in the normal run directory/ZIP. The sky ID identifies a scene stimulus, including when scene geometry occludes it; it does not identify a camera screenshot. Band gzip CSV has twelve row columns: Timestamp,Name,Layer,X,Y,Z,RotationX,RotationY,RotationZ,Speed,VisibilityPhase,experimentPhase, followed by extra Key:Value header metadata for spawn/boundary/grid parameters. Speed is cm/s; VisibilityPhase is elapsed phase in seconds modulo the total on+off cycle, not a normalized fraction. Read twelve data columns, then parse header metadata separately (older files have eleven). Layer indicates the rig-specific stimulus population, not a physical display number. Band logging follows the spawner's owned instances, including unlocked agents without a transform parent (these previously produced empty band logs). Kannadi, Swarm and Band rows use the same experimentPhase values as rig rows. VisibilityPhase remains the band blinking timer; it is not the experiment phase.

title: Optomotor and metadata
text: OptomotorDataLogger extends the rig/base schema with StimulusIndex (zero-based), Frequency (cycles/revolution), Contrast and DutyCycle (0–1), Speed (degrees/s), RotationAxis, ClockwiseRotation, ClosedLoopOrientation, ClosedLoopPosition. An instance on the drum records the drum transform; do not interpret it as animal pose. The world-pose logs on rig objects describe animal motion. The compact ColorDriftLogger CSV now has a matching five-column header: Current Time,CylinderName,CurrentBlue,TargetMean,experimentPhase. Its first four data values retain their previous meaning; the old mismatched rig-style header is corrected. Current animal metadata JSON stores ExperimentName, ExperimenterName, Comments, UsedAnimalIDs and Animals, whose entries include VR, SpeciesName, AgeDays, StarvedSinceHours, Sex, Comments and AnimalID. Transitional UsedFlyIDs, Flies and FlyID aliases remain for old analysis; canonical values win when both occur. Historical files use those legacy names. See compatibility. Age and starvation are text fields supplied through the UI; validate them in analysis instead of assuming a numeric JSON type.

title: Native tracker provenance
text: Current source writes companion_provenance.json at run startup and embeds the same tracker descriptors in config_manifest.json as companionProvenance. Each configured rig records whether an explicitly launched tracker process was found and its identity verified, the requested demo/strict-camera policy, release tag, executable SHA-256, PID/start time and configuration path when available. actualInputSource: "unverified" deliberately distinguishes process ownership from observed camera/animal provenance. Only a verified owned process matching the selected rig's backend, local endpoint and requested demo mode authorizes a native calibration snapshot. Its exact on-disk TOML/TXT/JSON bytes enter the normal SHA-256 archive with role tracker-calibration; configSnapshotPath and configSha256 locate and verify them. The primary system JSON remains unchanged. External/unmanaged inputs, stale/mismatched launches and missing configurations are explicitly marked unavailable or unverified. Missing optional native evidence does not invalidate otherwise complete experiment configuration snapshots. This captures the native configuration file on disk when the Unity run starts. It cannot establish unsaved native in-memory edits, physical tracking accuracy or actual source type from a legacy wire packet. Referenced background images, videos, executables and arbitrary sidecars are not recursively copied. Keep those native application files separately when needed for acquisition reproducibility. Saved animal poses and stimulus evidence remain authoritative for visual replay.

title: Analysis and replay cautions
text: Unwrap yaw before angular-velocity calculations. Use wall-clock differences for elapsed time while checking duplicates/jumps; a future monotonic timestamp would be preferable for sub-millisecond synchronization. Periodic X/Z wrapping and R resets cause coordinate discontinuities: use arena size and experiment boundaries when reconstructing path lengths. The fading overview trail is an operator display, not an analysis record. Current source writes rig numbers with invariant culture and round-trip float precision, quotes strings with CSV delimiters, and supports quoted multiline fields on replay. This prevents decimal-comma Mac locales or comma-containing step/config names from shifting pose columns. Rig timestamps retain seven fractional digits; unityFrame identifies the rendered frame. Regular rig capture runs in LateUpdate at order 1200, after movement/terrain adjustment and before telemetry. Immediate onset/swap event rows remain additional evidence. Archived versions used machine numeric culture and unquoted strings. A legacy row with a different field count is now rejected with an explicit warning rather than silently interpreting shifted numbers as a pose. Such corrupted rows cannot be recovered unambiguously. Kannadi/Swarm numeric writers already used invariant culture. Population gzip logs are loaded separately from animal trajectories. New Band rows additionally record Visible and UnityFrame; the visibility flag describes the actual renderer state. Older VisibilityPhase values used global time while rendering used an agent-local timer, so they cannot by themselves establish exact historical blinking. Replay marks that limitation instead of inventing visibility. Replay settings are inspector/UI fields: sessionFolder (newest when empty), absoluteSessionPath (optional override), playbackSpeed=1 seconds/second, loop=true, smallStepSeconds=1, largeStepSeconds=10, pauseOnSeek=true, autoResumeAfterSeek=true, createRigCameras=true, targetHorizontalFov=110 degrees. Replay split-screen cameras are analysis views, not LED panel viewport calibration. Keep the saved dynamic design/prefab catalog if reconstructing the stimulus environment.

title: Live monitoring and heading-onset records
text: The dedicated matrex.telemetry.v2 PUB stream (schema version 2) provides all rigs on port 9880, separately from tracking inputs. Heading-relative presentations append per-rig onset context to heading_reference.jsonl. See the versioned telemetry and onset schema for clocks, coordinate units, raw/consumed inputs, gains, sample freshness, circular mean and resultant length. For named cross-block heading references, heading_reference.jsonl additionally records savedAs and measureDuringPresentation. In the current Selwyn cycle, measurements are independent per rig, saved as milky-way-baseline each 240-second Milky Way block, and the following two swarm headers record the resolved world Mu. Sequence CurrentTrial increments when the repeated block group restarts; the setup prefix occurs only in the first pass.

title: Run configuration snapshots
text: Every new run folder saves its configuration during MasterDataLogger.Awake, before scene data loggers start. MainController creates a logger if one is absent. Saving no longer depends on which component happened to wake first, and repeated config loads cannot overwrite an earlier version or fail because a destination already exists. RunData/<session>/ system_config.json initial system snapshot sequenceConfig.json initial sequence snapshot config_manifest.json sources, versions, roles, hashes and errors Configs/ Files/Examples/Swarm/...json readable first copies, preserving source paths Files/Archive/Legacy/...json resolved legacy config copies Files/SwarmData/...csv referenced trajectory inputs and metadata Files/External/<path hash>/... absolute files outside StreamingAssets Snapshots/<SHA-256>.<extension> immutable bytes of every captured version The timestamp/scene-prefixed sequence and system copies remain at the run root for existing tools. The readable copies and root canonical files retain the first captured version. If a file changes between loads, both versions remain under Snapshots; consult the manifest's consumed and loads fields to identify which version was actually read, when and in which scene. Nothing overwrites the earlier bytes. The sequence graph is captured recursively: every configFile and design, nested/phased references, trajectoryFile plus an available metadata sidecar, and explicit skyboxPath images. Duplicate references are deduplicated; identical basenames in different directories remain distinct. Archive/Legacy fallback uses the resolved source location. Resource names for scene prefabs/materials are not file references; generated night-sky images and their provenance retain the existing Skyboxes archive. The shared reader snapshots the exact bytes returned to system, sequence, Choice, Swarm, Kannadi, Dynamic Choice and Optomotor loaders. It also captures loaded trajectory/sky files. Recorded CSV data is cached by content instead of only file timestamp/length, so a different input cannot silently reuse a previously parsed trajectory. Archive IO and hashing happen at configuration/input-load boundaries, not every rendered frame. config_manifest.json includes schemaVersion, Unity version, complete, each source path/reference, SHA-256, byte length, readable/snapshot paths, role and actual-load timestamps. Missing required files, failed writes or a missing/corrupt saved snapshot make the archive incomplete. Sequence start and experiment/phase application check it and report the failure through the existing error panel. A missing reference in a disabled phase, or a sky file overridden by uniformSkyColor, is recorded as unavailable optional input and does not block presentation.

title: Audit existing runs
text: python3 tools/audit_run_config_snapshots.py Assets/RunData --recent-since 2026-10-01 --report /tmp/run-config-audit.json The audit searches nested legacy copies and verifies hashes for new manifest snapshots. It accepts the comments/trailing commas supported by Json.NET without changing the original files. The report lists each session's missing sequence/system copies, missing referenced experiment files, nested copies and snapshot-integrity failures. The October 12 audit covered 474 existing folders. All 60 October folders had sequence/system copies; 59 had their referenced experiment configs. One run, 20261011_152342, referenced Examples/heading-aligned.example.json without a saved copy. Across the full older collection, 118 folders lacked at least one referenced config and four lacked a saved sequence. Many older folders predate system config, so absence there does not establish a contemporary system-saving regression. See historical audit. The audit is read-only. It never fills an old folder with today's config: that would mislabel current settings as the original experiment. An exact missing historical version can only be recovered from independent evidence such as a contemporaneous backup or known matching source revision. New snapshot behavior requires restarting Play to create a new session; existing folders remain unchanged.

title: Verification
text: RunConfigArchiveValidation.Run in a disposable Unity project checks startup copies, nested references, duplicate basenames, absolute/legacy references, optional files, repeat reloads, changed versions, missing files, cyclic references, custom system filenames and snapshot corruption. It also starts the current ControlScene experiment, checks saved hashes and confirms that a missing snapshot prevents sequence start. The existing five-scene phase suite and swarm trajectory/rendering suite check compatibility. Validation results records the actual results.

title: Heading-relative stimulus presentation and live telemetry
Experiment configuration
text: Use pre-stimulus / stimulus / post-stimulus in one experimental file. Heading measurement belongs to preStimulus.headingReference, with enabled (default false), startOffsetSeconds (default 0) and windowSeconds (default 180). The configured pre-stimulus world remains visible and controllable while each rig measures its circular mean and resultant length. An overlong observation is shortened to fit pre-stimulus, with a small GUI warning; the configured window remains saved. Each spawner separately opts into the frozen zero with useHeadingReference: true; computing the reference alone changes no stimulus direction. Old flat experiments still work. Heading observation shares the sequence timer and is capped to the remaining scene duration; it never extends the configured block. Their configured objects remain visible during observation. The default pose reset switches are true; set both false for continuity between conditions. The phase reference documents supported spawners, angle conventions, independent reset switches, examples and audit fields. The mean is atan2(mean(sin(yaw)), mean(cos(yaw))); resultant length is sqrt(mean(sin(yaw))² + mean(cos(yaw))²). One current virtual yaw sample is taken per rendered frame during the requested window. Samples are equally weighted, with no invented catch-up samples. There is no stability threshold; circling animals still get a finite angle with low resultant length. Kinefly input is control input, not the heading being averaged. Zero is +Z, +90° is right, and −90° is left of the frozen mean when opted in. Subsequent turns do not move that reference. heading_reference.jsonl records per-rig measurement completion; experiment_phases.jsonl records actual phase onsets and the references used then. Telemetry repeats the frozen results for late subscribers. The preserved Selwyn cycle runs one-time trimming, then repeating Milky Way-only, Milky Way/swarm and swarm-only blocks. Its named cross-block references are recorded in heading_reference.jsonl and resolved into each swarm log header. The earlier leftward swarm recipe remains a separate phased example.

title: Dedicated outbound ZMQ channel
text: Unity binds one PUB socket for all rigs. Tracking input remains on its existing per-rig SUB endpoints. Default output is tcp://127.0.0.1:9880, at 20 snapshots/second. Configure the hardware/network connection at the top level of system_config.json: "telemetry": { "enabled": true, "bindAddress": "127.0.0.1", "port": 9880, "rateHz": 20, "topic": "matrex.telemetry.v2" }, "statusOverlay": { "visible": true, "targetDisplay": 0 } Use bindAddress: "*" to accept connections from other machines; subscribers connect to the Unity computer's address. The port must differ from all configured tracking input ports. enabled: false disables output. rateHz must be in (0,240] and cannot exceed the actual render-frame rate. Output continues in Control and across scene changes. Bind/send errors are shown in the operator HUD; they do not prevent the experiment running. Reloading system config retries the publisher. Each outbound telemetry message is two UTF-8 frames: topic, then one JSON object. This requirement does not apply to tracking input: the existing Kinefly single-frame JSON protocol is accepted unchanged, as are topic/JSON messages. This follows NetMQ PUB/SUB framing. It is live monitoring, not a lossless recording: the PUB queue is bounded to two messages per subscriber, slow subscribers may miss snapshots, and no subscriber can block the render loop. The socket is created, used and disposed on one thread. Tracking SUB sockets now also own their entire lifecycle on their receive thread. Unity captures the immutable snapshot on the frame thread; JSON serialization and PUB socket operations run on a dedicated worker. Its pending queue retains only the latest snapshot, replacing and counting an older pending snapshot if encoding falls behind. Capture timestamps and frame numbers describe the sampled frame, not the later send time. Disabling, re-enabling or reloading configuration closes and recreates the worker and its socket. See the diagnostics performance measurements. python3 -m pip install pyzmq python3 tools/listen_telemetry.py --pretty python3 tools/listen_telemetry.py --endpoint tcp://UNITY_HOST:9880 > live.jsonl

title: Version 2 payload
text: Field Meaning schemaVersion, sequence Version 2; increasing publisher snapshot number, useful for detecting gaps. timestampUtc, realtimeSeconds, experimentSeconds, frame UTC timestamp; Unity unscaled uptime, scaled experiment time and frame. system Running flag; one-based trial and scene-sequence numbers; actual scene name/build index; remaining cycle and phase time; phase (preStimulus, stimulus, postStimulus); publisher state and local dropped-send count. Scene number is 0 while idle. Trial counts passes through the sequence, matching MainController. frameTiming Latest 2 Hz frame summary: timestamp/window, FPS, mean/peak frame milliseconds, configured target/VSync, software-cap budget, graphics API and timing sample count. cpuMainMs, cpuRenderMs, gpuMs, presentWaitMs are window means of available Unity frame timings; unsupported/missing values are null. GPU zero is treated as unavailable. Main/render work times already exclude Unity's presentation/target waits; waits are reported separately and can also reflect GPU pressure. Timing samples arrive about four frames later. The object is null until the first half-second summary. rigs All configured/registered VR IDs. A rig absent from the current scene has active: false, without fabricated pose/input. rigs[].pose x,y,z,pitch,yaw,roll: Unity world coordinates and Euler degrees. Heading is yaw; +Z is zero, +X is +90°. Units are the scene's authored world units (current walking scenes use cm). input.source, interpretation, endpoint Configured tracker type, active calculation path and tracking endpoint. input.motionMode, input.state, input.wireFormat Effective motion (flight, walking, force/torque), listener reception state and detected framing. input.endpoint is the endpoint used by the running listener. input.latest Atomic latest sensor packet: six values plus receive sequence/UTC timestamp, age and freshness. Angular pitch/yaw/roll are signed degrees; Kinefly wire radians are converted only for telemetry. Kinefly x/y wing angles are also degrees, while z stays tracker-native; other position fields remain tracker-native. positionUnits and angularUnits identify these. In force/torque mode the rotation channels represent torque and stay tracker-native rather than being mislabeled as angles. Missing fields retain existing zero defaults. input.consumed The exact atomic packet most recently read by closed-loop processing. May be older than latest. Repeated render frames can consume the same packet. closedLoop Actual position/orientation gain, yaw gain, yawDCOffsetDegrees, gain-scaled yawDCCompensationDegPerSecond and yawOutputDegPerSecond, force/torque gain, P/O enabled flags and whether tracking was applied in this frame. Applied position/yaw deltas describe that frame's tracking contribution, excluding later manual/autopilot movement. Yaw delta is wrapped to ±180°; it is not an integrated turn count. autoTrim Per-rig flag/state, independent measured flight and gate, degree² variance/threshold and degree standard deviations; mean/median/uncertainty in deg/s; selected statistic, measurement duration/progress, pass count and last adjustment in degrees with its actual gain-scaled rate change. headingReference disabled, observing, presented or error; remaining assessment time; frozen circular result after onset. errors Up to eight recent errors/assertions/exceptions with UTC time, message and stack trace; each text field bounded to 8192 characters. Full details remain in the session trace. Schema 2 deliberately changes angular units and field names from schema 1. Update subscribers to the default matrex.telemetry.v2 topic. Existing system configs using the built-in matrex.telemetry.v1 default upgrade to v2 in memory; configured custom topics are still honored. The CLI accepts schema 1 with an explicit old --topic matrex.telemetry.v1, but does not reinterpret old fields as degrees. Internal motion and historical raw CSV columns retain their original units. fresh means received within one second. A missing sample uses available: false, receivedUtc: null, ageSeconds: null; its zero numeric placeholders are not measurements. Telemetry snapshots are sampled monitoring records, not every sensor pulse. Receive sequence counters reveal packets skipped between snapshots. Tracker-generated timestamps or pulses not present in the existing six-number input protocol cannot be recovered. Legacy Kinefly retains held-input integration, while walking still freezes on stale input. Telemetry does not change those calculations.

title: On-screen diagnostics
text: The bottom-right panel appears by default on display 0, including in standalone builds. Tab toggles it throughout a running experiment, including if metadata retained input focus. Hiding deactivates the panel's graphics and skips its formatting/layout refresh; the independent FPS/timing readout and telemetry remain active. While idle, visible focused metadata fields retain Tab navigation and suppress experiment hotkeys. Hidden canvases, inactive or non-interactable input fields cannot block operator keys. A manual visibility choice persists through configuration refresh and scene changes; only a new error forces the panel open. Only one dashboard instance is allowed. statusOverlay.targetDisplay can move it to another connected display. The panel shows trial, sequence scene number/name, assessment/presentation state, per-rig gains, DC offsets and effective input mode (for example, Kinefly / flight). Each Input SUB line shows the actual tracking endpoint and reception state. Telemetry PUB (output) labels the separate outbound monitoring port. It persists across scene changes independently of the overview camera. Any new Unity error, assertion or exception, including errors logged on a background tracking thread, automatically reopens the panel and shows the latest message. Full recent error details are in telemetry and runtime_trace.log. Debugger errors are no longer suppressed at log level zero. Capturing an error reports it; it does not imply that the failing operation recovered. A presentation callback failure holds the sequence timer and reports the error.

title: Validation
text: Run the static validators, then HeadingTelemetryValidation.Run using Unity 6000.3.16f1 on a disposable copy with KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY in its root. It exercises circular wraparound/low-r/window eviction, opt-in and sequence precedence, generic/Choice adapters, actual Swarm scenes with distinct rigs, onset and repeated-trial continuity, real ZMQ input/output, signed raw data and error-driven HUD recovery. BogongGainValidation.Run and KannadiValidation.Run retain the historical Kinefly and walking arithmetic regression coverage. Physical tracking and LED timing require a bench run. The saved validation report records the current feature checks, 73,746 historical Kinefly checks, 1,008 walking/template checks, and a separate Python subscriber receiving real Unity snapshots.

title: Live browser monitoring
text: This chapter describes source updates after the immutable 0.3.0 release. The existing OS downloads remain unchanged. A browser dashboard needs a running bridge on the acquisition/server computer; GitHub Pages supplies static documentation, not a raw ZMQ connection.

title: Two kinds of telemetry message
text: The lightweight frame stream retains schemaVersion 2 on the configured topic (default matrex.telemetry.v2). Current source adds an experimentContext identity/reference describing the session/config/design/units context needed to interpret the snapshot without embedding a large configuration graph in every frame. The separate context heartbeat uses: Item Contract Topic <telemetry.topic>.context, normally matrex.telemetry.v2.context Payload schemaVersion 1 for the context-message schema; this is separate from frame schema 2 Payload kind matrex.context Interval setting telemetry.contextIntervalSeconds Default interval 2 seconds Valid interval range 0.25–60 seconds A subscriber joining mid-run can receive the periodically repeated context and associate it with lightweight frame snapshots. This does not turn the bounded monitoring channel into a durable record of every tracker frame. Keep the session archive for analysis and replay.

title: Browser bridge direction
text: Unity PUB: frames + context | v local/server ZMQ subscriber | v same-origin server-sent events (SSE) | v read-only browser view at /live/ The server subscribes to ZMQ; the browser receives the server's SSE response. The browser never opens a raw ZMQ socket. Context and frame versions are parsed according to their own contracts rather than treating every JSON message as an interchangeable pose.

title: Local and remote viewing
text: The trajectory-dashboard source adds /live/ for this monitoring view. Connecting/changing the upstream subscription is permitted only from loopback controls. Remote viewers observe the read-only stream through the running server. For a server intended only for live monitoring, --live-only disables the filesystem-analysis APIs rather than exposing the normal offline file workflow to LAN viewers. A LAN deployment still requires an explicitly running/bound server; opening this GitHub Pages manual does not start acquisition services. See Daari Deepa / trajectory-dashboard for the current launcher, packaging and server options. Integrations distinguishes tracker inputs, monitoring and saved-run analysis.

title: Run the bridge
text: From a checkout of Daari Deepa containing the live-monitor changes, install its native requirements and start the bridge: python -m pip install -r requirements-native.txt python native_app.py --telemetry tcp://127.0.0.1:9880 --open-browser The server defaults to 127.0.0.1:8060; open http://127.0.0.1:8060/live/ for the monitor. --telemetry-topic changes the default matrex.telemetry.v2 subscription. Use the endpoint actually enabled in Unity's telemetry settings. A bridge cannot discover a different rig's input port or enable telemetry inside an already running Unity player. For a deliberately shared read-only monitor on a trusted lab network: python native_app.py --telemetry tcp://127.0.0.1:9880 --host 0.0.0.0 --live-only --no-browser Then viewers use http://BRIDGE-HOST:8060/live/. The bridge's ZMQ connection remains to the configured publisher; binding its web server to a LAN interface does not require changing the Unity PUB address when both processes run on the same machine. Connection-setting controls remain loopback-only.

title: Standalone bridge packaging
text: The dashboard download hub serves complete ZIPs for Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS arm64 and macOS x64, with source revisions and SHA-256 checksums. Downloads are static and require neither sign-in nor Python. Passing main-branch builds update this hub without creating release tags. GitHub Actions also retains sign-in-only build artifacts for 14 days. Each package is built on its target OS and tested with an actual PUB → packaged receiver → HTTP/SSE connection, late-joining context, static browser assets, and a recorded-data fixture whose duration must remain exactly two seconds. The dashboard build workflow records the platform results. These checks exercise software and synthetic data; they do not measure a physical camera, tracking apparatus or LED display. The source has 158 dashboard regression tests. pandas is constrained to the validated 2.x series because pandas 3 changes datetime integer units and writable-array semantics used by the numerical reference. Unsupported pandas 3 environments fail explicitly, rather than silently changing durations. The source integration PR records this independently of the unchanged 0.3 Unity downloads. Snapshot and heartbeat ages are separate. Repeated idle/context events refresh visible tracker age without appending duplicate trajectory points. When a newer heartbeat advances the scene/trial before the next low-rate pose snapshot, the viewer clears the previous trajectory and waits for matching pose evidence; it does not combine an old pose with the new scene's units or config. An older heartbeat cannot relabel a newer frame.

title: Saved-run metadata discovery
text: The related dashboard loader accepts canonical animal metadata filenames (AnimalMetaData.json and the runtime's AnimalMetadata.json) alongside historical FlyMetaData.json. Canonical Animals and AnimalID take precedence over Flies / FlyID; an explicit empty Animals list remains authoritative. SpeciesName is retained, and FlyID remains a compatibility alias for historical analysis. Segment identity continues to combine SourceFile, normalized trial and step, so equal block names in two files do not collapse into one segment. These loader updates concern saved-run analysis, not the live transport. Retain the complete run directory and source revision for interpretation.

title: Interpretation
text: Use the frame's scene, phase, rig identity, tracking interpretation and freshness along with the matching experiment context. A visible trace is a sampled monitor, not proof that every input packet was received or that LED output happened at a measured physical latency. The default heartbeat makes late subscription practical; it is not a synchronization pulse. Frame timestamps describe the captured frame. A server/browser/network delay does not change the original acquisition time or repair an absent historical sample.

title: Stable reference
text: The 0.3 telemetry reference documents frame schema 2, its units and PUB queue behavior. This chapter describes the additional current-source context/browser path. Cite the actual source revision when using those changes; no new Unity release is implied.

title: Replay a recorded experiment
text: The saved-run replay path loads evidence from a saved run folder: animal poses, saved sequence/system/experiment files, archived sky images and recorded population poses. It opens with the God's-eye view so the whole experiment is visible. It does not substitute today's installed config for an absent historical file.

title: Open a run
text: Keep the complete session directory, including config_manifest.json, Configs, Skyboxes, rig CSVs, population CSV/gzip logs and any media directory. Extract a session ZIP before opening it. The folder is the portable unit; copying only a CSV loses the saved environment and optional video evidence. The 0.4 release target adds the recording library, tracker video controls and linked recorded trajectories described below; release publication and limits identify the actual available packages. These additions are not part of the frozen 0.3.1 download, whose existing replay still opens a saved folder with Browse, a path or the launch argument. In 0.4, choose Replay recordings from the setup sidebar. The library automatically lists recordings under this installation's RunData directory, newest first. By default this is MATREX VR RunData beside the app or executable. Protected installation directories use a stable per-installation folder in application support; the exact path is always shown above the list. --data-dir overrides it. Earlier builds' shared application-support recordings remain available through Browse. It shows the recorded span, observed rigs, animal metadata, tracker backend, sequence cycles and per-rig condition presentations. These are derived from saved rows; planned steps are not counted as completed trials. Setup-only folders and duplicate ZIP snapshots are not presented as experiment recordings. Select a recording to inspect Recorded files and Saved evidence & limitations, then choose Replay selected. This saves the current setup draft before opening the saved run. A finishing recording remains unavailable until its data writers have closed; other recordings can still be opened. Use Refresh to rescan or search by name, animal, backend or recorded scene. Browse… and Open an external folder path → Inspect folder open a recording on another drive or computer without moving it into the local library. You can also launch a player with: "./MATREX VR.x86_64" --replay-session "/path/to/RunData/session-folder" On macOS: open "/path/to/MATREX VR.app" --args --replay-session "/path/to/session-folder" This loads ReplayScene. Choose Open run…, then Browse… or paste the path into the run-folder field and choose Open run folder. The Editor and Windows/macOS use native system folder dialogs; Linux uses zenity or kdialog when installed, with manual path entry as the fallback. In the Unity Editor, dropping a folder into the replay UI is supported. Native operating-system folder drag/drop into a standalone player is not implemented; use Browse, the folder field or launch argument. Source integrations can call ReplayController.OpenSession(path).

title: Timeline and views
text: Space plays/pauses. Scrub the timeline forward or backward. Left/Right seek one second; hold Shift for ten seconds. N/M jump to the previous/next recorded step marker. Choose a playback speed from 0.1× to 4×. The God's-eye view is the default. Fit frames the recorded trajectory and returns to the overview. In 0.4, right-drag or I/J/K/L turns the overview; middle-drag pans; the wheel zooms. W/A/S/D moves horizontally and Q/E moves down/up; hold Shift to move faster. Perspective / Top-down view changes the overview projection. These controls are inactive while editing a path or media form. Click God's-eye view / Animal VR… to cycle the main view. The Cameras panel can show the saved front-camera reconstruction beside the tracker video while the main image stays overhead. Hide collapses that panel; − / + resize both previews together while keeping their original aspect ratios and the transport clear. Media tools… reveals import, collection, refresh and offset controls. In the God’s-eye view, each rig has a stable color, visible marker and heading arrow. The bright tail shows its last five recorded seconds; the faint path belongs to the current recorded condition. A wire cone indicates the front-camera field of view. VR labels and edge arrows help locate rigs outside the current view. These are analysis annotations, excluded from the saved animal-camera reconstruction. Adaptive clipping improves close inspection; Fit restores the full track view. Where saved camera data is available, the animal reconstruction preserves its projection and panel aspect with letterboxing. This is an analysis view of saved evidence; it does not establish physical LED scanout or pixel-for-pixel historical output. All animal timestamps use a common session origin so independent rigs do not each start at their first row. A backward seek updates animals, recorded populations and applicable saved stimulus context together. Replay controls operate on recorded time; they never restart live tracking or the acquisition sequence.

title: Record and replay tracker video
text: These controls belong to the 0.4 release target. Video is optional: pose recording and replay work without it. Acknowledged per-experiment recording Start/Stop, manual override and recorder-state reconciliation are not implemented. One independent tracker recording can span preflight and multiple experiment runs; stopping a VR experiment does not stop that recorder. Before starting, review Save tracker video for the relevant rig. 0.4 enables it by default for supported bundled Rekkefly/HejjéTrac launches; explicit tracker.saveVideo:false remains an opt-out. This requests native MJPEG AVI plus frame/configuration logs. A tracker already running with another recording option must be closed explicitly before changing it; calibration stays in its shared native configuration. The legacy Kinefly/FicTrac backend names can also select those bundled successors. An independently running external legacy tracker supplies camera footage only if that application actually records it; its tracking transport alone contains no camera pixels. Use Initialize tracking for input/calibration preflight, then start the experiment or labeled demo. Preflight creates no experiment pose recording, but a tracker launched with video enabled may already record. The tracker remains an independent application. For real experiments, inspect its camera, calibration and tracking quality before presenting stimuli. Demonstration input is simulated or prerecorded, not a new animal measurement. End the experiment with Back to setup / Esc, or let its configured sequence finish. Wait for Finishing recording… to clear before opening that run. Data writers are drained and the saved context and recording summary are finalized in the background. Close the native tracker normally when its video recording is finished. Unity never stops it as part of archival. If it closes cleanly while Unity is still running, the app can acknowledge the completed recorder. If the tracker is still open when the experiment finalizes, camera media stays pending while the poses remain replayable. Open the run and choose Media tools… → Collect media to gather completed app-launched footage. Refresh reloads media already present in the run. The original tracker recording stays at its source; copied media and sidecars are preserved under the run's media directory with integrity hashes. A linked clip follows the same replay clock as the trajectory, including pause, playback speed and forward/backward scrubbing. Software consumed-input frame association means a saved pose used the tracker input frame matched to that video frame; it is not an exposure or display synchronization measurement. Gaps or unavailable coverage remain visible rather than being filled with guessed frames. The video panel selects footage belonging to the chosen animal and the segment covering the replay time. A rig with no saved footage does not inherit a different animal's camera. The panel explains whether footage was switched off, is still pending, or must be imported from an external tracker. Enabling recording now cannot recover video that an earlier run never saved. The 27 October local-run audit records the concrete missing-video finding in the preview runs. For another finished tracker recording, choose Media tools… → Import footage…, select its folder and confirm The tracker has finished saving this recording. Leave the optional offset blank to preserve unknown timing. To align it approximately, enter an explicit offset using replay time = video time + offset; a positive offset means the video began later. Set offset… changes that alignment metadata without rewriting raw footage. Importing old video does not recover frame associations that were never recorded. Unsupported media may be archived without a playable or synchronized native preview. Collecting media or changing an offset updates the run folder. A ZIP created earlier remains its original snapshot and is not silently replaced. Transfer the complete updated folder when sharing a run with newly collected footage. See the recorded-media contract for clocks, manifests, import checks and synchronization limits.

title: Linked recorded trajectories
text: In 0.4, Trajectory plots opens the independent Daari Deepa recorded viewer. Unity remains the replay clock: the plots receive its time, speed and paused state, while seek/play/pause requests from the viewer return to Unity. The recorded viewer uses loopback port 8061; acquisition Live plots remains separate on 8060. Closing a replay session disconnects its controls without terminating the independent viewer. The linked native viewer is included only in the reviewed macOS Apple Silicon bundle, pinned to Daari Deepa 1486b81e. Older pinned Intel macOS, Windows and Linux dashboard archives lack the required replay API/assets; an explicit capability message is shown instead of spawning repeated copies. Unity’s internal pose/video replay does not depend on that external viewer and remains part of every platform build. An ordinary standalone analysis view can still inspect the saved data independently.

title: What is restored
text: The saved manifest resolves immutable configuration snapshots and verifies their hashes. Old recordings without a manifest can use the config copies actually present in that session; a fidelity warning identifies the missing provenance. Recorded scene/config/phase fields identify the stimulus context. Archived Skyboxes/<skyboxId>.png supplies the actual texture displayed at that point. Where the named scene is included in the build, replay loads its geometry additively and freezes live acquisition scripts. Saved Choice/Dynamic Choice content and disk-indexed population poses restore supported experiment elements. Large population CSV/gzip recordings are indexed for seeking instead of loading every agent pose into memory at once. The fidelity panel identifies missing configs, built geometry, sky images, population data and other unavailable evidence. It also distinguishes recordings that lack agent orientation/animation information. A recording cannot establish pixels, random states, wall-clock corrections or stimulus details that were never saved. Replay is an evidence-based reconstruction, not a guarantee of historical pixel equivalence. Do not fill an old recording with today's similarly named JSON. If a reference has multiple archived versions and the correct version cannot be selected from the saved acquisition context, replay reports the ambiguity rather than choosing silently.

title: Historical formats
text: Versions 0.1/0.2 contain the older rig-trajectory viewer, with inspector fields and the same basic keyboard seek controls. Their replay does not automatically restore every generated sky or population. Keep their exact source/configs when comparing archival behavior. 0.3 Swarm position logs append RotationX, RotationY, RotationZ after the existing experimentPhase column. The old nine-column prefix remains, and old recordings remain readable, but headings that were not recorded cannot be recovered as measurements. Data formats documents the schemas and clocks. The lifecycle/replay report records actual ReplayScene loading, archived sky/geometry/population, scrubbing and overview tests. See release verification for the tested scope.

title: 0.4 recording/replay verification
text: The round-trip validation records two actual scenes and reopens the resulting folder in ReplayScene. It compares the saved frame poses and rendered animal-camera images before/after a dynamic color swap, then seeks backward across the swap and scene boundary. The measured mean RGB error is at most 0.0158% in the six tested 256 px views. Inputs are explicitly synthetic, sent through a real native-format PUB; this does not claim physical camera or LED validation. Current source starts replay at the first experiment row instead of leaving the playhead in a long initial ControlScene wait. Saved camera projection/panel aspect is preserved where available, with letterboxing rather than stretching; God's-eye markers and paths are excluded from the animal camera. Replay preview lights are suspended while the imported scene supplies its original lighting. Logged dynamic swap and adaptive black/gray onset decisions are restored without rerunning random choices. Legacy timestamp/scene-prefixed configuration copies are resolved by suffix only when their saved content is unambiguous. Missing or conflicting evidence remains an explicit fidelity warning. New Band records preserve actual visible/hidden state; older phase-only records cannot prove exact blinking. The 27 October local review records native keyboard/rendering acceptance and current UI checks. The 48 focused resize/header assertions use actual production IMGUI events and Full HD/Retina framebuffers; the 82 camera assertions cover markers, clipping, resets and preserved animal-view pixels. Latest standalone pointer/drag acceptance remains incomplete because native automation returned noWindowsAvailable. Windows/Linux builds have no native execution walkthrough, and evenly paced 60 FPS remains unresolved. These software checks do not establish physical camera/LED timing.

title: Extend the source
text: Use the existing JSON controls when the experiment differs only in parameters. Add or modify Unity scenes/assets/controllers when the environment or behavior itself changes. MATREX VR intentionally does not provide a general level editor.

title: Add a recipe first
text: Copy a complete compatible experiment and sequence example, retain its subdirectories, and point a block's configFile or design to the new file. Set explicit tracking/reset/units choices. The studio can create an independent variation of a shared experiment without relinking every block. Use the configuration reference to distinguish omitted defaults from template example values. Do not infer support merely because the lossless editor retains a new extension key: a production parser must consume it to affect rendering.

title: Add an ordinary parameter
text: Add the field/property to the runtime configuration type used by the owning parser, with a clear default, units and finite/range validation. Apply it in the owning controller at the appropriate initialization/phase boundary. Regenerate configuration schemas using ConfigurationSchemaBuilder. Add help/conditional UI annotations when they clarify behavior. Add a complete recipe demonstrating the field and check its saved/telemetry/replay implications. Verify that old omitted values preserve the intended behavior and that an actual edit is reversible in the shared document model. Unknown fields survive editor round trips, but known fields must fit their runtime type before Start. Preserve an explicit compatibility alias only with a documented precedence rule; do not silently rewrite old acquisition files.

title: Add a scene
text: Start from a compatible authored environment and preserve the rig/component pattern. Register the scene's controller in the orchestration path, associate its schema/parser in ConfigSchema where necessary, and enable the scene in the build settings. A config naming an unbuilt scene cannot make its geometry appear in the standalone player. For efficient repeated conditions, implement IInSceneSequencer.AdvanceStep where supported. That method must fully reapply/reset the condition and release replaced populations/materials; skipping a Unity scene load is not permission to accumulate trial resources.

title: Add prefabs, materials and agents
text: Use the owning scene/catalog's registered assets. Kannadi prefabs belong in the KannadiPrefabCatalog; Choice/dynamic content uses its own registered resources. Keep authored physical scale, pivots, culling layers and per-rig visibility explicit. A new real species is metadata. It does not automatically select a virtual model, locomotion interpretation or tracker calibration. A new virtual agent visual is an asset/config choice. Preserve that distinction in UI labels and recordings.

title: Add a tracker or adapter
text: Implement the input contract, including wire shape, units, cumulative versus incremental/rate meaning and stale behavior. An adapter can normalize an external stream without making ZmqListener guess units from species names. Validate complete samples and keep socket ownership on the receive worker. Do not reuse the outbound telemetry topic as a tracking input contract. If extending versioned telemetry, preserve semantic versioning of payload meaning and document angular conversions.

title: Make recording and replay part of the change
text: Record original consumed files and the minimal dynamic state needed to interpret the experiment. Append compatible columns where possible; retain source identity/version and units. If the new stimulus cannot be reconstructed from current recordings, surface a fidelity warning in replay rather than substituting today's defaults. For large populations, use bounded worker queues and seekable indexed playback. Preserve discontinuities and use a shared acquisition timeline across animals.

title: Validate on a disposable copy
text: Many Unity validators intentionally replace test configs and create synthetic sessions. They require KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY at the disposable project's root. Do not run them against a live authoring/acquisition configuration. Run the relevant static template/asset checks, production JSON/replay contract checks and native scene/UI/resource tests for the changed path. A test that synthesizes input or shortens trials does not replace a physical apparatus bench check. See release evidence and lifecycle.

title: Build and distribute
text: Use the pinned Unity version and required desktop modules. The source build helper prepares a revision, public hardware defaults, manifests, hashes and complete archives; it does not publish them. Custom-source builds should retain a distinct version/source identity so recordings can identify their renderer. This documentation can be rebuilt with the manual builder described in the documentation source. Static HTML is committed for GitHub Pages; readers do not need Unity, Pandoc or a server-side renderer.

title: Experiment Workflow
text: This project runs experiments by chaining Unity scenes and, within some scenes, chaining in‑scene sequence steps. Use this doc as a quick reference when adding or running experiments.

title: Scene sequencing (sequenceConfig.json)
text: Location: RuntimePaths.ConfigRoot/sequenceConfig.json (Editor: Assets/StreamingAssets; current standalone: writable profile Config). Fields: randomise: shuffle the order of the listed scenes when true. loop: restart from the first scene when the list ends. sequences: array of scene entries. Each entry has sceneName, duration (seconds to run that scene before advancing), optional parameters (passed to the scene controller), and reloadScene (set false to stay in the same scene and let it advance internally). On startup MainController reads this file, copies it into the logging folder, and then walks through the list according to timers and looping rules.

title: In‑scene sequencing (e.g., Choice_desync)
text: Some scenes implement IInSceneSequencer (e.g., Choice_desync via DynamicSequenceController). When sequenceConfig.json sets reloadScene: false for a step, MainController calls AdvanceStep(parameters) instead of reloading the scene. For Choice_desync, parameters.design points to a sequence design JSON in Assets/StreamingAssets/ (generated by the editor scripts). DynamicSequenceController loads that design and advances through its internal steps based on time or triggers defined per step.

title: Generating sequence designs
text: Editor menu items under Tools/… generate design JSON files into Assets/StreamingAssets/. Examples: Gray shade angle sweep with mid-trial color swap: Tools/Generate Gray Shade Choice AngleSweep Swap SequenceDesign.json (Assets/Scripts/BuildGrayShadeAngleSweepSwapDesign.cs). Other generators follow the same pattern (e.g., BuildGrayShadeChoiceDesign, BuildStaticDecisionDesign). After generating a design, reference its filename in sequenceConfig.json (e.g., set "design": "sequenceDesign_grayShades_angleSweep_swap.json" for a Choice_desync entry).

title: Adding a new experiment
text: Create or modify a generator script under Assets/Scripts to emit the desired design JSON into Assets/StreamingAssets/. Add/update a sequences entry in sequenceConfig.json with the target sceneName, duration, and any parameters the scene expects (e.g., design). Ensure the scene controller implements IInSceneSequencer if you plan to stay in-scene (reloadScene: false), or leave reloadScene at true to force a reload between steps. Play the scene; MainController will load the config, copy it to the log folder, and step through scenes/steps according to your settings.

title: Continuous heading assessment
text: For Swarm or ordinary Choice, enable headingReference in the individual experiment config. The rig continues tracking through assessment and stimulus onset, with no onset reset. Heading observation shares the configured scene/phase timer and is capped to the remaining duration; it does not add time to a condition. See heading-relative presentation for a reusable component API and the required stimulus adapter when adding new controllers.

title: Repeated resets and scene lifecycle
text: The historical workaround avoids scene reloads by advancing an experiment within its existing scene. That path remains useful: same-scene blocks with reloadScene: false use IInSceneSequencer.AdvanceStep, including Dynamic Choice/Choice_desync, Swarm, Kannadi and the terrain lab. Changing to another scene, or explicitly setting reloadScene: true, still loads a scene normally. Asynchronous scene loading alone does not release objects or native handles retained by a previous trial. The 0.3 work addresses concrete resource ownership problems found while auditing repeated transitions: Generated material instances now have an owner that destroys them when their trial object is destroyed, including in-place resets. Optomotor's generated mesh, material and texture are released on destruction. Asynchronous swarm writers dispose their wake-up handle after draining. Submission/completion synchronize with disposal so a late callback cannot signal an already disposed handle. Tracking listeners stop when disabled as well as destroyed, and restart on re-enable. A worker still stopping remains owned rather than being replaced by another live socket/thread. The workers still own their sockets and file writers on their own threads. Clean shutdown drains recorded frames before archiving. The runtime exposes active worker/writer/material/resource counters for targeted stress validation; these counters identify owned resources rather than total Unity process memory. There was no original Unity crash dump establishing a single root cause. These changes fix identified leaks and lifecycle races; they do not establish that every crash after 50–100 reloads has been eliminated. Physical GPU/driver behavior, acquisition timing, different scenes and long sessions require testing on the actual workstation. The Unity report passed 1,293 checks, including 150 actual MainController Choice↔︎Swarm scene loads at accelerated 0.1-second block duration with four local SUB listeners and two generated agents, plus 150 native ColorDrift/material/grating/socket teardown cycles. Its scene-load samples record the tracked owned-resource counters after teardown. These are accelerated real scene loads, not a 30-second hardware acquisition soak. For reproducible acquisition, use explicit same-scene reset settings and save the sequence/config graph with each run. Compare regular scene reloads and in-place transitions under the same workload, record resource counters/process memory, and retain Unity's Player log and any crash dump. A shortened synthetic transition test is useful evidence of cleanup; it cannot substitute for a full-duration hardware run. See release verification, experiment workflow and saved-run replay.

title: Flight diagnostics performance
text: Profiling found two avoidable sources of frame pressure: repeated full-window sorts in auto trim, and repeated whole-row string copying in the four rig CSV loggers. Telemetry also serialized and sent its JSON on the Unity frame thread. The fixes preserve sampling, units, logged columns and calibration behavior. Auto trim retains its sample/value workspace and selects the exact median by partitioning, with a bounded fallback for difficult inputs. Both the long precision window and short recovery window retain their existing statistics. CSV formatting reuses a StringBuilder; every column no longer copies the growing row. Telemetry captures Unity values on the frame thread and serializes/publishes on one worker. Its pending slot retains the latest snapshot and counts overwritten snapshots. Socket creation, use and disposal remain on that worker, including configuration reload and disable/re-enable. The dashboard still updates at 2 Hz. Numeric changes no longer trigger an additional preferred-height text layout when its rows and error history are unchanged.

title: Measurements
text: The saved report includes source hashes, independent correctness checks and the benchmark conditions. These are Apple M2 Pro Unity Editor measurements, not LED workstation FPS. Work Before After Four trim ticks, p99 CPU time, full 120-second windows 2.36 ms 0.35 ms Four trim ticks, observed maximum CPU time 8.42 ms 0.50 ms CSV allocation overhead per frame, four rigs, above the no-diagnostics baseline 121,882 bytes approximately 30,476 bytes Dashboard full layout versus cached panel layout, paired final-run median 0.96 ms 0.67 ms Telemetry JSON serialization/socket sending on frame thread every publish worker The live Selwyn MW sky fixture uses four rigs and six 128px cameras per rig. Camera rendering takes approximately 2.54–2.60 ms of CPU submission time, while game callbacks take approximately 0.16 ms without diagnostics and 0.33 ms with all diagnostics. CSV formatting is the largest steady diagnostic cost; trim produces occasional evaluation work. Camera submission is the larger steady workload in this fixture. This measures CPU submission, not completed GPU time, display synchronization or the operator HUD's GPU fill cost. Batch Editor mode does not automatically render a Game view. The final scene benchmark explicitly renders all 24 cameras and records their CPU time separately from PlayerLoop. The earlier callback-only baseline is retained only for callback and allocation comparisons; its very short frame intervals must not be interpreted as thousands of displayed frames per second. The old publisher did not restart after component re-enable, so its affected baseline cases are excluded. The optimized publisher is explicitly configured and its restart is checked with real received snapshots. Historical VR1 data from 20261011_035104 has median frame intervals of 17 ms in star setup and 22 ms during swarm stimulus, with p99 intervals of 20 and 33 ms. That recording predates the current auto trim, so it shows scene-related slowdown without identifying today's controller cost. It does not prove a GPU bottleneck on the LED computer.

title: Workstation frame pacing
text: The reported LED setting is target 60, VSync off, with 58–60 FPS even in a simple scene. This uses Unity's software timer, which Unity documents as susceptible to microstutter. It does not by itself measure remaining CPU/GPU capacity. For a 60 Hz output, use top-level "targetFrameRate":60, "vSyncCount":1. The 60 Hz four-rig Kinefly example includes these settings; preserve the workstation's actual tracker addresses, panel placement and target display. /1 follows the actual refresh rate; on a 120 Hz output use /2 for 60 FPS. Explicit existing pacing settings remain authoritative. The FPS HUD now samples a fixed one-element FrameTiming workspace, refreshes text at 2 Hz, and reports frame mean/peak, CPU main/render work, GPU and presentation/target-FPS wait milliseconds. These summaries also appear in outbound telemetry. Unity's CPU work times already exclude its synchronization waits; do not subtract the wait again. A large wait can come from the cap/VSync or the GPU, so inspect the work timings together. Release builds enable Frame Timing Stats. Unsupported timings appear as a dash/null: Linux OpenGL does not provide GPU frame time; Linux Vulkan does. This instrumentation does not classify a machine as GPU-bound when GPU data is absent. Tab now works throughout a running sequence even with lingering metadata focus. Hidden/inactive/non-interactable legacy and TMP text fields no longer suppress operator keys. Hiding deactivates dashboard graphics and stops its format/layout refresh; configuration refresh does not reopen it. The small timing readout remains available for comparing the same scene with the dashboard shown/hidden. New errors still open the panel. The regression fixture failed on the previous implementation at hidden-canvas focus, then passed on the fix. The updated live validator also checks configuration visibility persistence, running versus idle metadata handling, duplicate removal/error capture, actual graphics deactivation, wire timing fields and timing-label layout. The saved frame dashboard report records the source hashes and results. CPU/GPU numbers from batch Editor mode are not workstation measurements.

title: Verification and reproduction
text: All 74 Gaussian cases match the preceding estimator's results exactly, including actual Unity heading integration and the five-pass convergence checks. The median selector matches independent full-sort truth in 80 cases, including ordered/reversed input, duplicate values, extreme values, odd/even counts and unused workspace capacity. Live flight/bypass/persistence/recording checks pass with 64 agents per rig. Telemetry checks pass with actual PUB/SUB packets, degree fields, dashboard controls, scene transitions and worker disable/re-enable. Use a disposable Unity project containing the repository's Assets, Packages and ProjectSettings, plus a KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY marker in its root. These validators refuse to run without that marker; the scene benchmark replaces only the disposable project's local system/sequence configs. Run Unity 6000.3.16f1 with -batchmode -projectPath COPY -executeMethod METHOD -logFile LOG: DiagnosticsPerformanceValidation.Run: warmed CPU callbacks, allocation-event recording, median truth checks and dashboard layout comparison. DiagnosticsFrameValidation.Run: real Selwyn sky scene, features isolated in sequence, explicit 24-camera submission, game callback timing and per-frame allocation bytes. KineflyGaussianValidation.Run: hidden-mean convergence and actual heading integration. KineflyAutoTrimValidation.Run: flight gating, controls, persistence, CSV phase capture and swarm worker drain. HeadingTelemetryValidation.Run: real telemetry transport and restart. GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread() reports no usable allocation data in this Unity Mono runtime. The callback benchmark therefore counts Unity GC.Alloc events rather than mislabeling their timing as bytes. The scene benchmark uses the GC Allocated In Frame byte counter. Callback timings exclude cold startup, but occasional garbage-collection or OS scheduling outliers remain visible in the report.

title: Scene reload investigation
text: This investigation uses two-second experiments with a full Unity scene reload for every experiment. The asynchronous in-scene reset path is not used by the reload soak. Testing was performed on 25 October 2026 with Unity 6000.3.16f1, macOS, Apple Silicon and Metal rendering. The original historical native Unity crash has not been reproduced. A concrete failure in the original tracking listener has been reproduced and isolated: shutting down a socket on the main thread while its worker is blocked in a receive leaves workers and socket resources behind. One run also recorded a NetMQ I/O thread exception followed by loss of tracking input. A separate material ownership regression was found and corrected. These findings must not be described as a captured native crash or proof that every historical crash has the same cause.

title: What the test exercises
text: Assets/Editor/SceneReloadDiagnostics.cs writes a sequence with duration: 2 and reloadScene: true on every row, disables randomisation and looping, and checks that every loaded experiment receives a new scene handle. The normal profile alternates Choice_desync and Swarm: two changing visual objects per animal in Choice, and 64 generated Bogong moth agents per animal in Swarm. All four animal rigs run throughout. An external process publishes real, finite tracking packets on four local ZeroMQ PUB sockets at 120 Hz. The test samples after Start, approximately 0.55 and 1.55 seconds into each experiment. Each active sample checks that all four receivers have recent packets, and the second sample verifies that each receiver advanced. sceneLoaded observations are explicitly marked as occurring before Start; zero counters at that point are not used as evidence of resource cleanup. Graphics are enabled. The authored animal cameras render normally, and each enabled panel camera is also rendered into a 128 × 128 offscreen target every Unity frame. These diagnostic targets are counted separately and destroyed on unload. Choice authors 20 panel cameras and Swarm authors 24. The test checks the actual authored count rather than assuming that every scene has six faces per rig. It does not duplicate a laboratory LED wall, its full resolution, drivers or physical tracker. Every active sample records managed memory, Unity allocated/reserved memory, native Material/Mesh/Texture/RenderTexture counts and bytes, GameObjects, open descriptors, tracking workers, writer workers and writer backlog. A separate supervisor records process RSS, virtual size and actual operating-system thread counts. After the protocol it measures cleanup both before and after explicit garbage collection and Resources.UnloadUnusedAssets; neither is forced between experiments.

title: Original listener: matched comparison
text: The archival project was reconstructed from commit 779926a80b02190d6dd0410f260e52bba105a04e. All 2,484 tracked project files were present, and all 188 C# files matched that commit before adding the diagnostic runner. The matched comparison changes exactly one runtime file, ZmqListener.cs; the original NetMQ and AsyncIO DLLs and all other runtime source remain identical. The input interruption profile pauses the publishers 0.25 seconds before each experiment ends, then resumes them when the next scene loads. Both active sample points still have four recent, progressing inputs. This exposes a listener waiting for the next packet at destruction. Observation, 40 forced reloads Original listener Worker-owned socket + 100 ms reads Active samples with all four live inputs 80 / 80 80 / 80 Active open descriptors, first → last 113 → 183 109 → 109 Shutdown deadline warnings 37 0 Descriptors after complete scene teardown 167 93 OS threads near first → last active sample 120 → 149 127 → 123 Native Unity process crash None captured None captured The original run has two shutdown timeouts while leaving the initial Control scene and another 35 during experiment reloads. Active descriptors grow by 70, or two per failed experiment-worker shutdown. After complete teardown, the original retains 74 more descriptors than the treatment, matching two per each of the 37 timeouts. This is strong evidence of a resource growth mechanism in the old listener. The comparison does not measure how many reloads would exhaust resources on a different system. The old implementation creates the socket on the main thread, blocks on ReceiveFrameString on a worker, then disposes the same socket on the main thread during destruction. It waits 500 ms for the worker and discards the thread reference even if the worker remains alive. The treatment creates, receives from and disposes the socket on the worker, and uses bounded 100 ms receives so the stop flag can be observed without another packet. It does not invoke global NetMQ cleanup between scenes. This agrees with NetMQ's documented socket threading restrictions and socket cleanup lifecycle. An earlier original-listener attempt recorded this actual exception on the second reload: NullReferenceException NetMQ.Core.Pipe.ProcessPipeTermAck NetMQ.Core.ZObject.ProcessCommand NetMQ.Core.IOThread.Ready NetMQ.Core.IOThreadMailbox.RaiseEvent NetMQ.Core.Utils.Proactor.Loop Subsequent experiment receivers stopped receiving, and descriptors rose from 116 to 229 by load 17 while the publishers continued. That attempt was then terminated by the diagnostic supervisor, after its timestamp parser rejected a five-digit fractional timestamp. Its exit was SIGTERM, not an observed native Unity crash. The parser was corrected before the complete 40-load comparison above. No macOS crash report was produced by that attempt.

title: Material ownership regression
text: DynamicSequenceController installed an owned material for each object, but the later colour swap accessed Renderer.material. That access created another instance and detached it from the owner. The swap now changes the already-owned sharedMaterial. The focused native probe rebuilds eight visual objects 40 times and exercises both colour-swap paths, with no garbage collection or asset unload between cycles. With the previous swap implementation, destroying all objects leaves 320 native materials while the ownership counter incorrectly reads zero. With the correction, the rendered material stays identical to the owned material, the live count stays at nine (eight objects plus their source), and destruction leaves zero probe materials.
