This is a regression in the later ownership implementation, distinct from the older full-scene reload failure.

title: Completed reload evidence
text: The first modern run and the matched pre-modernisation c13d33dd run each completed 200 full two-second reloads with 400 active samples, all four inputs progressing, all authored cameras rendered, and no native process crash. Their per-scene live native resource counts stayed flat. Both exposed two null-sky UI summary exceptions on the final return to Control; these are preserved in their results, and were corrected before the final current-source rerun. The final current-source run passed all 200 reloads: 400 active samples, no stale or nonprogressing input, no runtime exceptions, no shutdown timeouts, and all 20/24 authored panel cameras rendered. Actual scene intervals ranged from 2.002 to 2.301 seconds (median 2.215), including transition work. Before forced garbage collection, teardown left zero tracking workers, writer workers, owned trial materials and diagnostic render targets; these stayed zero after collection. Live native counts stayed constant within each scene. One Unity Editor search-index startup exception was preserved and classified separately from runtime errors. Detailed current-source results and the separate terrain/night-sky profile are recorded in the machine-readable results. Source and plugin fingerprints identify the exact tested working tree, since several fixes are newer than the base commit. The terrain profile also passed 40 full two-second reloads, with the publishers paused before every unload. All 80 active samples verified two terrain components, a recorded 4,096 × 2,048 astronomical sky and four progressing animal inputs. All 24 panel cameras rendered; live counts remained 188 materials, one mesh, 100 textures and 32 render textures. There were no runtime errors or worker shutdown timeouts. Scene intervals were 2.014–2.990 seconds, including terrain/sky setup; teardown left zero tracking workers and owned trial materials. The terrain scene emits five existing missing-script warnings per load: three InfinityCode.RealWorldTerrain.RealWorldTerrainItem and two RealWorldTerrainContainer importer metadata components refer to absent scripts. Native Unity Terrain and the recorded sky are present and rendered, but these 200 warnings are retained in the results. They are not classified as a resource leak. The probe's initial idle-sky inspection also required a shader-property guard; that intentionally interrupted attempt is recorded separately from the clean 40-load repeat.

title: Reproduce on the diagnostic host
text: Use a disposable project copy with KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY at its root. Never use the original working project: the runner temporarily replaces its copy's system and sequence configurations, restores them on normal completion, and saves the originals in the output folder. If the process is interrupted, restore those two files from original-configs before running another test. python3 tools/run_scene_reload_diagnostics.py \ --project /absolute/path/to/disposable-project \ --output /absolute/path/to/new-output-folder \ --count 200 --duration 2 --scenes Choice_desync,Swarm python3 tools/analyze_scene_reload_diagnostics.py \ /absolute/path/to/new-output-folder For the interrupted-input comparison add --pause-before-reload 0.25 --scenes Choice_desync --count 40. For terrain and automatic sky use --profile terrain-night-sky --scenes Choice_Selwyn --count 40. Override --unity and --libzmq for the installed host paths. This supervisor currently uses macOS process tools; it is not a Windows/Linux soak result. Raw JSONL observations, complete Unity logs, publisher progress, source hashes and any newly generated native crash reports remain in the ignored diagnostic output directory. The supervisor captures native stacks and a memory-map summary if main-thread progress stops, then terminates only its own child. A supervisor termination is explicitly distinguished from a crash. Historical mono_crash.mem.*.blob files present in the repository contain only zero bytes and supplied no usable stack evidence. Full reloads now have a repeatable regression path, but an eight-minute accelerated Editor soak does not certify multi-hour experiments, Windows/Linux graphics, laboratory hardware, arbitrary custom scenes or every resource limit. Keep both the full-reload path and the in-scene transition option available, and repeat the test with the exact experiment configuration and hardware if the historical crash recurs.

title: Six camera directions
text: The shared Assets/Prefabs/Camera Prefabs/VR.prefab now contains Front, Back, Left, Right, Up and Down. Standard VR1–VR4, Swarm and Kannadi variants inherit these faces. The older Cube variants inherit Down instead of adding a duplicate. ControlScene's historical removal overrides for Up have been removed. ViewportSetter activates exactly the directions listed in the system config. All enabled faces use a 90° vertical field of view. Up/Down use Front's camera origin, near/far clip planes and culling mask, including Kannadi's eye-height offset and each rig's population layers. They keep their ±90° pitch. Four-face RBLF configurations still work and leave Up/Down disabled.

title: Enable all six
text: Copy Assets/StreamingAssets/Examples/System/fictrac-six-cameras.example.json to Assets/StreamingAssets/system_config.json, then set tracker addresses and ports for the rig. The template uses display 0 and four rows of six 128×128 panels: 768×512 output pixels. The order is Down, Right, Back, Left, Front, Up (DRBLFU). The local hardware config is ignored by Git; the template is versioned. For an existing config, set each required rig's displayOrder to DRBLFU and allocate six panel slots without overlap. The template uses startCol: 0, startRow: 0/1/2/3, and horizontal: true. Face letters select rendering; they do not change experiment movement or sensor logging. Face Rig-local viewing direction Rotation relative to Front F +Z Identity B −Z Yaw 180° R +X Yaw +90° L −X Yaw −90° U +Y Pitch −90° D −Y Pitch +90° North is +Z for the astronomical sky when northYawDegrees is zero. The night-sky horizon mask makes the lower celestial hemisphere black; the scene's ground can still appear in Down.

title: Validation
text: Use Unity 6000.3.16f1 with graphics enabled on a disposable project copy containing KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY: Unity -batchmode -projectPath <copy> -executeMethod SixCameraValidation.Run -logFile <log> The check loads the base rig and fourteen variants, verifies unique faces, renders a direction marker through each standard camera, checks origins and layer masks, and tests six-to-four-face reconfiguration. It also covers the actual ControlScene, Choice, Swarm and Kannadi scene instances. KannadiValidation.Run covers the broader sequence and runtime behavior; NightSkyValidation.RunControlPreview verifies the live sky and Bogong preview with the local system layout.

title: Kannadi / Swarm modernization
text: The integration branch is codex/kannadi-modernize. It starts from origin/currentlocustvr (60a7121, 2025-11-18) and incorporates the full history of origin/JuliusTree (1205fe3, 2026-09-09). A merge keeps both histories rather than duplicating their shared ancestors with hundreds of cherry-picks. JuliusTree supplies shared infrastructure and unrelated experiments; locust assets and behavior come from currentlocustvr. The existing NatureStarterKit2 importer fix (db13b13) is cherry-picked separately.

title: What is retained and integrated
text: Restored the historical Grey_505050 material and its original GUID, fixing missing material references that prevented JuliusTree's two-tree Choice controller from starting. JuliusTree's system configuration, ZMQ fresh-pose checks, replay, Choice/DynamicSequence experiments, and data logging, carried forward with the user's Unity 6000.3.16f1 upgrade and package changes. Locust models, swarm and band prefabs, Kannadi scene, per-rig initial poses, numeric tracking gains, self/peer viewing, and mouse-controlled overhead overview. Unity 6 TextMesh Pro essential resources are upgraded from the installed uGUI package while preserving asset GUIDs. Settings and fonts match the new importer version, so opening TMP text no longer asks for the old resource import. A single FPS counter persists at the top right across scenes and remains visible when the overview is hidden. It measures frame rate without changing VSync or frame limits. Kannadi is the sole mirror scene. The separate Matrix scene, wrapper, and prefab variants have been removed. Swarm and Kannadi are enabled in build settings. The branch's default sequence runs Swarm for 20 seconds, then Kannadi for 1000 seconds. Entrainment uses 256 locusts per rig over a 200 × 200 cm area, mu: 0, kappa: 100000, and speed 2 cm/s. This doubles the earlier population while keeping the arena size. At this kappa the existing spawner uses the exact requested heading. The former JuliusTree default is saved as Assets/StreamingAssets/Kannadi/sequenceConfig_JuliusTree.json. Old locust JSON and generation scripts are preserved in Assets/StreamingAssets/Archive/LegacyLocustInputs. They are historical inputs, not validated modern Choice configurations. Their paths and schemas may need migration before reuse.

title: Hardware configuration and startup
text: Open your MATREX VR checkout as a Unity project and start Assets/Scenes/ControlScene.unity as usual. Use Unity 6000.3.16f1, matching the upgraded project version. Copy Assets/StreamingAssets/Kannadi/system_config.example.json to the ignored local Assets/StreamingAssets/system_config.json, or retain your existing hardware file and add its overheadCamera section. Set the actual sphere diameters in centimeters, FicTrac addresses/ports, LED panel pixel dimensions, panel rows/columns, and display order for VR1–VR4. The example uses a 5 cm sphere and ports 9872–9875 as editable starting values, not a calibration. The hardware file is applied to the existing ViewportSetter, ZmqListener, and ClosedLoop components on all four swarm/mirror rigs. Scene parameters determine the experiment, not the hardware calibration. In the original Kannadi setup, the user-selected system_config_VR1.json (now archived) was copied to the ignored system_config.json: four rigs, RBLF, 2.6 cm spheres, and display 0. The prior primary-checkout changes were saved in the Git stash named Before switching primary checkout to Kannadi integration 2026-09-28 before switching branches.

title: Camera allow-list
text: displayOrder is authoritative in every scene using ViewportSetter, including Swarm, Kannadi, Choice, and DynamicSequence. RBLF enables only those four cameras, in that order; Up and Down remain disabled even when serialized as enabled. Listed inactive cameras are activated. The shared VR prefab now includes Down, all variants expose six faces, and Up/Down match Front's origin, clipping and visibility mask. Examples/System/fictrac-six-cameras.example.json is the six-face layout. Empty, missing, or null orders disable all cameras on that rig. A missing rig entry also disables its cameras; it never borrows VR1's settings. Unavailable target displays disable stimulus cameras rather than routing them elsewhere. Panel size, row, column, horizontal/vertical direction, and target display come from system config. Layouts refresh on config reload and window resize. Invalid and duplicate letters are ignored without consuming panel slots. Camera visibility masks remain the experiment's responsibility; they do not override the hardware allow-list. The operator overview is separate from the stimulus cameras.

title: Experiment parameters
text: Assets/StreamingAssets/Kannadi/multiplayer.json is the runnable example. Sequence parameters can be inline or specify configFile; inline values override file values, and an inline vrConfigs array replaces the file's array. Field Behavior numberOfRings Positive: 1 + 3r(r+1) replicas per tracked animal. Zero: center only. Negative: no replicas. Self-view omits its own center. hexRadius Positive radius in world centimeters. Legacy spacing is accepted when hexRadius is absent. Kannadi grid spacing is retained. kannadiTilePrefab Name in Assets/Resources/KannadiPrefabCatalog.asset; supports individual locusts, bands, and registered choice shapes. The catalog has explicit references for standalone builds. boundaryLengthX, boundaryLengthZ Independent rectangular periodic dimensions, centered at world origin. Wrapping preserves overshoot. periodicBoundary Default true; set false for unbounded movement. closedLoopPosition Boolean or nonnegative numeric gain; translation is scaled by this and the calibrated sphere radius. closedLoopOrientation Boolean or nonnegative angular gain. Default 1 maps each sensor yaw delta 1:1 to world yaw; zero disables turning. Explicit 0.5 or 2 scales the measured angle. The previous turn-speed convergence behavior has been removed. vrConfigs Entries with vrIndex 1–4, optional initialPosition, initialRotation in degrees, watchIndex, and per-rig gain overrides. watchIndex Omitted: see the other tracked animals' layers. 1–4: see only that animal's replicas, while retaining the shared floor/background. Own index: see own replicas except the center. animateOnMove Boolean animation gate, enabled in the supplied Swarm and Kannadi configs. false restores continuous animation. animationSpeedThreshold Default 0.5 world units/second (cm/s). Walking animation runs only above the threshold. Measures planar translation of the root, not animated bones; rotation in place does not count. Legacy animationNoiseThreshold is accepted when the new field is absent. Both Swarm and Kannadi support reloadScene: false sequence steps. Reconfiguration replaces old agents instead of accumulating populations. Bands mirror the tracked rig; their members do not continue autonomous walking. Clone height comes from the selected prefab rather than a hard-coded offset. For animation gating, Kannadi replicas and band members follow the tracked rig's translation; autonomous Swarm locusts use their own translation. Periodic wrapping is accounted for so crossing an arena boundary does not create a false speed spike. You can set either field inline in a sequence step or in its referenced experiment file: "animateOnMove": true, "animationSpeedThreshold": 0.5 Both locust scenes use the existing grass_05 dry green/brown grass texture through a dedicated unlit ground material. Its current tile spans 100 world units (100 cm; 200 repeats across the 20000-unit plane), providing ground optic flow independently of light placement. The earlier 20-cm setting changed in commit 8597c35.

title: Operator overview
text: The overview sees all tracked animals and all virtual animal layers. Each active scene rig with a ClosedLoop component and a VR<number> name gets a colored heading arrow and just its number (1, 2, etc.). Marker discovery runs twice per second and supports IDs beyond four; it never creates placeholder animals. Arrows are drawn in the operator UI, remain 14 pixels long as the camera zooms, and cannot appear in stimulus cameras. Arrows stay at the exact projected positions of the real VR game objects. Overlapping animals keep overlapping arrows and labels; there is no collision avoidance, displacement, or connecting leader line. This also applies in Swarm, where virtual locusts remain part of the scene image rather than receiving extra tracked-animal arrows. A thin, faint trail shows the most recent 60 seconds and fades continuously with age. Set trailDurationSeconds to 30 for a shorter history, or 0 to hide trails. Hiding the overview disables both of its cameras and the tracking/mesh component, and releases the render texture. The header button and FPS readout remain available. Showing it recreates the render target and starts fresh history, avoiding a false line across an unobserved interval. Large jumps (over trailBreakDistance world centimeters between samples) break the path instead of drawing across a periodic wrap. History starts afresh when changing scenes. The overview, markers, and history are destroyed with the scene. In system_config.json, overheadCamera supports: "overheadCamera": { "enabled": true, "targetDisplay": -1, "x": 0.58, "y": 0.02, "width": 0.4, "height": 0.4, "resolution": 512, "markerSizePixels": 14, "trailDurationSeconds": 60, "trailSampleInterval": 0.1, "trailWidthPixels": 1.5, "trailBreakDistance": 50 } Coordinates are normalized with the origin at the bottom left; the default places a panel covering 40% of the screen width and height in the bottom-right area (about 78% more area than the previous 30% panel). targetDisplay: -1 follows the system display; a nonnegative value selects an operator display. Adjust this rectangle to the unused area of your actual LED layout. The overview never changes the LED camera viewports. Within the image, right-drag orbits, middle-drag pans, and the wheel zooms. Reset view restores the overhead framing; Show / hide toggles the image. Gestures started outside the image do not control this camera. The orbit transition from straight down is continuous.

title: Logging
text: Kannadi writes one compressed clone CSV per rig, including positions, orientations, ring count, and radius. Filenames distinguish rapid scene reloads, and floating-point data uses invariant decimal formatting. Swarm retains its population logger. Referenced experiment JSON files in subdirectories are copied into the run log along with modern system/sequence records.

title: Validation
text: Run the dependency/build-registration check with: python3 tools/validate_kannadi_assets.py Assets/Editor/KannadiValidation.cs is a Unity batch regression runner. Use a disposable project copy with KANNADI_VALIDATION_COPY at its root, Examples/System/fictrac-four-cameras.example.json copied to system_config.json, and the branch's default sequence. It creates synthetic session data and disables live ZMQ input. Invoke Unity with -batchmode -projectPath <copy> -executeMethod KannadiValidation.Run -logFile <log>; do not pass -quit, because the runner exits after asynchronous Play Mode checks. It covers heading orientation, constant arrow size across tenfold zoom-out, numeric labels, exact overlapping marker positions, hidden rendering and render-target release, persistent FPS, TMP resource compatibility, translation-only animation thresholds and periodic wrapping, dry-grass material references, dynamic discovery including a fifth rig numbered 12, history expiration and fading, discontinuity handling, the 20-second aligned Swarm configuration, strict camera inclusion, omitted/null orders, missing rigs, horizontal/vertical pixel placement, runtime configuration reloads, inactive cameras, missing displays, in-scene sequence changes, system settings on four rigs, Swarm → Kannadi → Choice → JuliusTree two-tree → dynamic sequence transitions, fresh/missing/stale tracking behavior, numeric translation, visibility masks, zero/negative rings, rectangular wrapping, prefab materials, band following, camera orbit, CSV creation, and overview cleanup. Results are written to kannadi-validation.json, with a rendered overview in kannadi-overview.png. The recorded run passed 768 runtime assertions with zero runtime failures. The static check passed all 84 Swarm/Kannadi scene/catalog dependency files. See kannadi-validation-results.json and kannadi-overview.png alongside this document. Validation uses a disposable Unity 6000.3.16f1 copy with the upgraded project's package files. Unity's unrelated editor search-cache exception is recorded separately in the test report. The overview screenshot includes synthetic trajectories to demonstrate the markers and fading; it is not experimental data. Physical LED/FicTrac calibration, network timing, and actual monitor mapping remain untested.

title: Reset controls (Unity 6)
text: The rig prefabs have both ClosedLoop and Keyboard enabled. R resets position and heading to the current experiment's initial pose, including when FicTrac is absent or stale. P toggles tracked translation and O toggles tracked orientation; these are toggles, not separate resets. Resuming orientation uses the current visible heading as its baseline. Escape stops the sequence and returns to Control; Escape from Control quits the player. MainController owns Escape so rig components cannot quit during a scene transition. Validation: 773 checks passed with synthetic tracking, including missing/stale reset and sequence exit; physical keys and tracking hardware still need a bench check.

title: Unity 6 input and configuration reference
text: The Unity 6 Input System migration uses package 1.20.0, a shared editable action map, gamepad movement/reset, and InputSystemUIInputModule for active UI. Active Input Handling remains Both to accommodate bundled third-party demo scripts; project-owned runtime controls use the new backend. Restart an already open Editor after pulling this change. The final regression run passed 876 checks with zero runtime failures. This includes simulated keyboard/mouse/gamepad events, actual rig movement, reset without a live pose, scene camera allow-lists, overview lifecycle, Optomotor, the full dynamic template, Choice bands and per-rig band visibility, strict configuration deserialization, and migration wind/AGL transitions. The report separately records Unity Editor's pre-existing SearchDatabase cache exception. Physical LED/FicTrac timing and controller hardware were not exercised. Sixteen JSON templates/examples and full manuals now live under Assets/StreamingAssets/Templates and docs/configuration-reference.md, docs/unity6-controls.md, docs/data-formats.md. Bogong/SmrMah wind and AGL settings now work in Choice; exact historical inputs and source commit IDs are retained in docs/config-history. Dynamic Choice respects both tracking flags false, saved runs include referenced dynamic design files, and the Choice scene registers the band example's prefab.

title: Walking gains and frame timing
text: Walking yaw now uses the same incremental angle model as JuliusTree, with a true dimensionless gain. Default translation and orientation gain are both 1; explicit numeric Swarm/Kannadi values override them. The former gain×360 degrees/second convergence cap depended on render timing and could continue turning on repeated packets. It has been removed. Signed yaw differences handle 0/360 crossings, and the ZMQ handoff copies each complete pose under a lock so components cannot be mixed between packets. Top-level system config fields targetFrameRate (default 120; -1 uncapped) and vSyncCount (default 0) own frame pacing. ViewportSetter no longer forces VSync on. The FPS HUD shows measured rate and target or VSync mode. The local hardware file is set to 120 FPS and VSync 0. Validation: 918 checks passed, including exact 0/0.5/1/2 gains, a 90-degree input without a frame-dependent cap, wrapped yaw/reversals, repeated render frames, concurrent pose publication, and FPS persistence across scenes. These establish the software behavior; they do not replace a live-stream comparison against the user's stable older build.

title: Releases and compatibility
text: GitHub Releases is the publication record. A local build or source change is not a published binary. The website discovers real uploaded ZIPs; it never constructs a download URL for an absent asset.

title: 0.4 — terrain, recording and replay
text: Release target: v0.4.0. Publication is established by the uploaded GitHub Release assets, not by this source document or a local build. The release manifests identify the exact source revision and packaged companions. Earlier 0.3 release descriptions below retain their historical scope. Four TerrainChoice spatial layouts share one environment prefab and two equidistant placeholder trees. Four ready-to-load treatment sequences independently select visible and navigation surfaces across all four layouts, covering sixteen scene/treatment combinations without sixteen scene copies. The shared centimeter recipe uses 1 cm eye clearance and texture scale 4; both-flat conditions deliberately look identical. Configured LED panel geometry and camera routing remain authoritative. See terrain recipes. Initialize tracking opens the independent tracker for calibration/input checks before the experiment. The setup and JSON retain the same values and inherited defaults. Choice configurations expose Available objects & materials, with exact-name Type/Material controls. Recordings default to MATREX VR RunData beside each player; protected installations use Application.persistentDataPath/Installations/<installation-id>/RunData. Configuration remains in Application.persistentDataPath/Config. Explicit --data-dir and --config-dir overrides remain supported. The recording library shows its root, discovers completed runs and opens external folders without moving them. Replay combines saved poses, trial context, supported scene reconstruction and available tracker video on one seekable clock. A compact transport, media card, disclosed media tools, bounded preview resizing and refined dialogs accompany colored rig markers, recent recorded trails, heading arrows, front-camera cones and offscreen labels. The God’s-eye camera supports orbit, pan, translation, projection changes and adaptive clipping. Animal-camera evidence retains its saved projection/aspect. The reviewed Mac arm64 Daari Deepa 1486b81e payload adds linked recorded-trajectory plots and replay control. Older pinned Intel Mac, Windows and Linux dashboard archives lack that API/assets and report the capability limit. Unity’s internal pose/video replay is independent of the external viewer. The compact build enables 14 scenes: ControlScene, Choice, Choice_desync, Choice_Selwyn, Swarm, Kannadi, Optomotor, TerrainCueLab, Rugosity_RS, ReplayScene, TerrainChoice_RoughLeft_SmoothRight, TerrainChoice_SmoothLeft_RoughRight, TerrainChoice_BothSmooth and TerrainChoice_BothRough. Existing scene GUIDs remain compatible. Other forest/two-tree source examples still require enabling their scenes and rebuilding.

title: 0.4 verification and known limits
text: The local Mac review records actual native rendering and keyboard checks. Terrain/video verification includes fresh native recordings and Unity import/decode/seek checks using generated or attributed prerecorded input. Camera checks passed 82 assertions; preview resize/header checks passed 48 assertions at Full HD and supplied Retina scale, with actual production IMGUI events. They are distinct from native window input acceptance. Evenly paced 60 FPS remains unresolved. High uncapped throughput does not establish uniform presentation intervals. The pacing investigation reproduces engine/platform effects in minimal controls and records additional tails under the four-recorder workload. FPS measurement fixes retain real delayed frames and peaks; they do not certify LED presentation timing. Acknowledged per-experiment tracker recording Start/Stop, state reconciliation and manual override are not implemented. Save tracker video requests recording when an eligible bundled tracker is launched. Recorders remain independent and may span multiple experiment runs; finish them normally, then collect completed media. A VR experiment stopping does not by itself stop its video recorder. See video workflow. Latest standalone pointer/drag acceptance is incomplete: native automation returned noWindowsAvailable, including after unlock. Native keyboard/rendering checks and injected Unity GUI-event tests passed within their separate scopes. The earlier 0.3.1 walkthrough does not establish acceptance of every changed 0.4 mouse interaction. Windows/Linux archives are cross-built on Mac and have not received native execution walkthroughs. Mac packages are universal, ad hoc signed and not notarized. Only the reviewed Mac arm64 Rekkefly correction supports the strict camera path; older pinned packages on other architectures remain blocked for that path. Bundled Linux HejjéTrac requires glibc 2.39 or newer. Physical tracker calibration, LED scanout/exposure synchronization, representative long-run acquisition and hardware-specific behavior remain apparatus checks. Build the pinned release source with both reviewed Mac payload options: python3 tools/build_release.py --ref v0.4.0 --version 0.4.0 --platform all \ --local-native-camera-fix \ --local-dashboard-archive .integration/local-dashboard/DaariDeepa-macos-arm64.zip The helper emits three complete OS ZIPs, per-archive SHA-256 files and embedded build/release manifests. It never uploads them. Hosted CI currently deploys only the static website; Unity desktop archives are built locally with the installed target modules. A published stable release is discovered by the website only after its actual ZIP assets exist. When reusing a previously reviewed unsigned native executable instead of rebuilding it with Cargo, also pass the paired --verified-native-binary /path/to/rekkefly and --native-binary-provenance /path/to/MATREX-NATIVE-PROVENANCE.json options. The builder verifies the binary and receipt against the pinned source/patch before Unity starts; these options require --local-native-camera-fix and do not skip provenance checks. See companion build provenance.

title: 0.1 — archived main
text: Source: 779926a80b02190d6dd0410f260e52bba105a04e, release tag v0.1.0. Preserves the main runtime before the configuration studio and telemetry integration. Includes its historical Control metadata form, Choice, Swarm, Kannadi, Optomotor, replay and night-sky behavior. Packaging adds a public hardware starting template, build tooling and START-HERE.txt; runtime experiment scripts and JSON retain the archived revision. The actual shipped sequence is manual-start Choice_Selwyn, 86,400 seconds per block, looping with reloadScene: false, using Kannadi/selwyn-night-sky.json. Its forward autopilot is 7 m/s, tracked orientation enabled, generated Selwyn sky at startup's current instant with fixed UTC+11 and 30-minute updates. The old revision's README described an earlier Swarm→Kannadi default; the JSON establishes actual startup. The release keeps old metadata names, application-relative files and older replay/reset limitations. It does not include the later Tab dashboard or outbound experiment telemetry. Archived 0.1 shortcuts and launch guide.

title: 0.2 — integrated Config UI Test baseline
text: Source: c13d33dd, release tag v0.2.0. Preserves the already integrated Config UI Test branch: modern Kannadi, Bogong stars and moth/swarm behavior, generated/recorded swarms, configuration studio, live diagnostics/telemetry, recursive run snapshots and the updated terrain cue experiments. The branch already contains the Kannadi modernization, heading telemetry and Bogong night-sky histories; these are not additional disconnected feature copies. Startup retains autoStart: true with seven 30-second TerrainCueLab conditions, looping and advancing in place. Escape returns to setup; -configure bypasses auto-start. The earlier Selwyn sequence remains Examples/Sequences/selwyn-before-rugosity.json. The studio already preserves unknown JSON, exact untouched numbers, omissions/nulls and original bytes on unchanged saves. It retains historical metadata/speed spelling and engine scene rigs authored as VR1–VR4. It still edits bundled StreamingAssets and records under the application's data directory. Archived 0.2 shortcuts and launch guide.

title: 0.3 — holistic improvements
text: Release tag: v0.3.0. The source revision and platform build manifests are recorded with the release. This version brings reversible configuration, writable profiles, configurable animals, saved-run replay and explicit lifecycle cleanup together. A fresh profile opens the setup studio (autoStart: false); existing user sequence flags are preserved. Editable configs and recordings use a writable profile (Config and RunData under Application.persistentDataPath), with --config-dir and --data-dir overrides. Editor defaults remain unchanged. Initial seeding copies missing files only and never replaces existing user edits. Real subjects are animals; simulated/replayed individuals are agents. Session metadata adds species and animal IDs, and the system file stores per-rig speciesName. agentSpeed and agentSpeedStdDev describe simulated motion, retaining existing aliases. Canonical animal metadata retains old aliases for analysis during transition. Runtime rig provisioning follows configured VR IDs within available rendering-layer capacity. Scene lifecycle gives trial materials, generated Optomotor assets, writer handles and tracking workers explicit cleanup. Saved-run replay adds folder/config discovery, a common timeline, archived skies/populations and a default God’s-eye view. See release-specific verification before relying on a behavior for acquisition. Replay includes a native Browse… folder picker (Windows/macOS, Editor, and Linux when zenity/kdialog is installed), folder-path input and --replay-session. Editor folder drag/drop works; standalone OS-level folder-drop is not implemented. The compact build contains ten scenes: ControlScene, Choice, Choice_desync, Choice_Selwyn, Swarm, Kannadi, Optomotor, TerrainCueLab, Rugosity_RS and ReplayScene. Forest/two-tree examples marked sourceBuildOnly need their scenes enabled in a custom source build. Custom level authoring belongs in Unity source, not in the configuration studio.

title: JSON and naming migration
text: New/current field Accepted older field Rule agentCount numberOfLocusts Canonical non-null count takes precedence; a population of zero remains valid. agentSpeed locustSpeed, locoSpeed First non-null value wins in that order; units remain the scene's world units per second. agentSpeedStdDev locustSpeedStdDev New field takes precedence; existing distribution meaning is retained. Animals Flies Canonical metadata wins when both are present, regardless of property order. AnimalID FlyID Canonical animal ID wins. Hardware VR remains a routing key. UsedAnimalIDs UsedFlyIDs Canonical list wins. Per-rig system speciesName — Saved as SpeciesName in animal metadata. Loading or viewing a configuration does not mass-rewrite legacy fields. See animal/agent compatibility for the complete mapping. The lossless editor preserves unknown extensions, untouched exact numeric text and missing values. If you explicitly set a canonical alias, it takes precedence; remove it to restore a legacy value's influence. Existing species-specific prefab names, Unity asset GUIDs, serialized component fields and historical CSV headers are preserved where renaming would break recordings or scenes. The operator UI uses animal/agent terminology.

title: Platform packaging and verification
text: Release archives target Windows x86-64, macOS universal (Apple silicon and Intel), and Linux x86-64. Packages carry complete Unity players, public starter config and version-specific START-HERE instructions. macOS packages are ad hoc signed and are not notarized. Cross-building a target on macOS establishes the build result; Windows/Linux runtime behavior still needs a check on those operating systems and physical acquisition hardware. Keep the whole extracted player directory together. Versions 0.1/0.2 require a writable extraction/app bundle because their historical code writes there. 0.3 uses a writable profile instead. See getting started for exact paths and migration. Each version is pinned separately so archive, integrated baseline and new improvements can be compared without moving an older tag. Build status, actual uploaded assets, hashes and runtime test evidence belong to the release itself. Tests using synthetic tracker data do not establish physical LED scanout timing or animal-tracking calibration.

title: 0.3.1 — native desktop workflow
text: Release tag: v0.3.1. This freezes the desktop workflow accepted in the manual Mac test, before the subsequent recording-library and synchronized video work. The player opens fullscreen at native resolution with Retina-aware controls. A fresh apparatus profile offers Start demo and Configure; daily sequence and animal/session editing remain separate from hardware setup. Gain sliders span 0–50 with unrestricted numeric entry. The replay toolbar supports bidirectional timeline dragging, view switching, and an app-owned Mac folder picker that remains visible over fullscreen. Bundled trackers and Daari Deepa launch independently, with stable per-user installations. Apple Silicon includes the reviewed Rekkefly source correction (f9a9ba71 plus the checked-in patch) and Daari Deepa f122518a. Their exact source revisions, patches and executable hashes accompany the packages. Other architectures retain pinned upstream companions; the strict live-camera Rekkefly path requires the correction and is unavailable there. Demo input and manual/external tracker workflows remain available. No new upstream tracker release is implied. The manual Mac workflow report records Configure, Start, physical webcam input, live plots, acquisition, replay and 43 two-second scene transitions. An earlier build passed 300 full two-second reloads; the original historical native crash was not reproduced, and these results do not establish its sole cause or eliminate every hardware-specific failure. Windows/Linux are cross-built and not manually tested on those operating systems. For this release's tested Apple Silicon payloads, build with: python3 tools/build_release.py --ref v0.3.1 --version 0.3.1 --platform all \ --local-native-camera-fix \ --local-dashboard-archive .integration/local-dashboard/DaariDeepa-macos-arm64.zip See local companion build provenance for reproducing the reviewed dashboard archive. Omit those flags only for an explicit upstream-companion build; it does not reproduce the tested Apple Silicon package. Run the archived 0.3.1 command from its matching checkout, including its companion locks and quickstart. Current-source locks and the 0.4 quickstart describe different payloads; they must not be substituted into a claimed reproduction of 0.3.1.

title: Software verification
text: Evidence Result and scope Unity lifecycle/replay report 1,293 checks passed: 150 accelerated native ColorDrift/material/grating/socket teardown cycles; 150 actual MainController Choice↔︎Swarm full scene loads at 0.1-second configured duration, with four local tracking SUB listeners and two generated agents; six-animal asynchronous layer/camera/reference checks; real ReplayScene folder, saved geometry/sky/population, timeline and default overview checks. Offline replay checks 630 checks passed against the production archive/cache/writer code. JSON compatibility report 43 contracts passed for lossless documents, animal aliases/species, canonical agent count/speed precedence and validation. Unity-only collaborators are stubs in these contract checks. Rig readiness report 71 checks passed: configured rig creation, omitted-rig disabling, sparse VR10 IDs, isolated layers and camera masks, including additional asynchronous cameras excluding authored private rigs. 0.3 GUI report / capture manifest 2,946 checks passed with graphics-enabled Unity runtime panels and fresh Full HD captures: animal/species edits, field geometry, raw JSON Apply/Discard visibility, replay launcher and actual UI callbacks, using synthetic metadata. Website download tests 15 assertions passed: actual uploaded OS ZIP selection, incomplete/missing assets, universal macOS preference, version sorting and fallback. These accelerated software regressions establish cleanup and replay behavior under their recorded fixtures. They do not reproduce a 30-second, 100-reset physical acquisition run, certify LED timing or prove the sole cause of the historical Unity crash. Windows/Linux archives are cross-built; runtime checks on those operating systems and the actual apparatus remain separate.

title: Rebuild the desktop archives
text: Use an activated Unity 6000.3.16f1 Editor with macOS, Windows Mono and Linux Mono support. The repository has no Unity license credentials configured for hosted CI. GitHub Actions can build Unity through GameCI when a suitable license is supplied; the published archives here were built locally. python3 tools/build_release.py --ref v0.4.0 --version 0.4.0 --platform all \ --local-native-camera-fix \ --local-dashboard-archive .integration/local-dashboard/DaariDeepa-macos-arm64.zip Supply --unity /absolute/path/to/Unity on another workstation. The helper creates a fresh ignored .release-work/release-0.4.0/ folder, prepares tracked files from the requested Git revision, injects the release builder, supplies the public hardware template, and emits ZIPs, source manifests and SHA-256 files. It refuses to reuse an existing output folder. It never uploads releases. Archival tags can be rebuilt with a matching --quickstart text file containing their historical controls and storage locations; exact companion reproduction also requires the corresponding locks and reviewed payloads. On macOS, copy-on-write project/cache copies keep disk use manageable; other platforms need room for a complete source checkout.

title: Hardware and calibration
text: The system configuration maps software rigs to tracker endpoints and display rectangles. It does not calibrate a camera, measure ball diameter, infer an LED wiring order or certify scanout timing.

title: What the software needs
text: Item Configuration / responsibility Real animal label/species Session Animal ID and per-rig speciesName; does not choose a tracker mode automatically Tracker source Address, port, effective motion mode and documented input units Ball calibration Actual sphere diameter and publisher convention for cumulative displacement Display output Physical target display, pixel resolution, panel dimensions and offsets Camera-face arrangement Valid displayOrder matching the real surrounding panel order Scene scale Centimetres for walking/rugosity, metres for supported Selwyn/migration terrain Timing Workstation frame pacing, tracker acquisition timestamps and physical LED scanout measurements Storage Writable recording root with capacity for population/sky/config evidence

title: Before animal collection
text: Confirm rig identities individually so one animal cannot receive another's tracking or virtual population. Verify face order, panel location and camera orientation using an identifiable test stimulus on the real output. Check Up/Down faces when using a six-face layout. Compare one known measured displacement/yaw against the rendered world with explicit gain and reset settings. Test missing/stale inputs and operator overrides under the same mode that will be used for acquisition. Record the physical north alignment for astronomical experiments. Frame-rate targets and frame-time dashboards report software timing. They cannot alone establish LED scanout phase, camera-to-display latency, stimulus luminance or projector/panel calibration. Retain physical synchronization/calibration records with the experiment.

title: Multi-rig planning
text: The number of configured software animals is bounded by available independent stimulus layers and workstation rendering/recording capacity. More configured rigs do not create tracker fanout or physical video outputs. External tracker fanout, display driving and network topology must be set explicitly. The integration guide links the tracker projects. Viewports gives the exact pixel mapping. Use a representative population/sky load when checking performance; a blank Choice scene is not a substitute for a dense moth/terrain experiment.

title: Hardware documentation scope
text: This manual documents the current software contract and the apparatus-dependent checks that follow from it. Rig-specific wiring drawings, parts lists, measured scanout/latency results and physical calibration procedures must come from the actual apparatus. They are not inferred from an example system_config.json. Those hardware records can be added alongside this manual as they are measured.

title: Trackers and analysis
text: The toolchain separates visual experiment control from tracking and analysis. MATREX VR owns Unity stimuli, rig motion, recordings and replay; an external tracker supplies the measured input. Analysis tools operate on saved evidence or a deliberately bridged monitoring feed.

title: Verified related projects
text: Project Role Repository Rekkefly Modern Rust flight/Kinefly tracking path; use its documented Unity-compatible ZMQ fanout pvnkmrksk/rekkefly HejjéTrac Native Rust walking tracker; packaged hejjetrac desktop / hejjetrac-cli, with source binary names distinguished below pvnkmrksk/hejjetrak Daari Deepa Browser-native trajectory views using WebGL/Canvas with Python preprocessing/serving pvnkmrksk/trajectory-dashboard These are separate repositories and release/installation flows. Their names do not establish that every available output socket already matches MATREX VR. Use the adapter/launch contract appropriate to the selected tracker and software revision.

title: Verified tracker launch surfaces
text: Rekkefly accepts a configuration, rig label and per-process output port: rekkefly --config "/path/to/tracker-config" --label VR1 --zmq-port 9871 --headless An optional --device DEVICE selects the camera. Its supervised shutdown flag is intended for an owning launcher: stdin newline/EOF requests a graceful stop and disables fallback behavior. Keep that ownership separate from attaching to an already running tracker. HejjéTrac uses its configuration's zmq_port; there is no command-line port override in the audited launcher: hejjetrac --config "/path/to/tracker-config" --windows 1 This example uses the packaged desktop executable. The audited source checkout names its Cargo binaries fictrac-desktop and fictrac; the packaging script supplies the hejjetrac / hejjetrac-cli names and hejjetrak aliases. Match the executable to the installed version rather than renaming a CLI binary by assumption. The config port must match the Unity rig. Its native FT row is not the old JSON pose object. See the exact input contract.

title: Release and transport boundary
text: The stable 0.3 player retains the established JSON tracker contract. Current source adds modern tracker names and native FT decoding. The native integration guide and 791-frame native report document 300 actual HejjéTrac FT rows, 100 mixed legacy JSON frames and 391 actual Rekkefly messages (391 of 400 synthetic source frames, also observed by an independent subscriber after PUB startup) with the updated NetMQ bundle, and separate transport evidence from decoding-only tests. These source changes do not move or replace the 0.3 release tag.

title: Optional owned tracker launch
text: Current source can show explicit Launch/Stop buttons for configured local installed trackers. It does not download, discover or automatically launch executables, and never stops unrelated processes. Installed executable/calibration paths, direct argv handling, local-only limits and supervision behavior are documented in native tracker integration. Stable 0.3 does not gain these source additions retroactively.

title: Direction matters
text: tracker / adapter PUB --> MATREX VR per-rig SUB input MATREX VR PUB telemetry --> external subscriber / browser bridge saved run folder --> replay or offline trajectory analysis Tracker input has the six-channel pose contract. Outbound monitoring has the versioned telemetry schema. Saved population/animal CSV and config manifests have their own data formats. They are not interchangeable just because all are JSON, CSV or ZMQ.

title: Flight and walking
text: Rekkefly is the modern flight source. Select its Unity-compatible fanout and the source Rekkefly backend (or the established Kinefly-compatible path for stable 0.3), then verify signed yaw/DC/gain behavior. HejjéTrac supplies the walking acquisition path: current source decodes native FT rows with the Hejjetrac backend; stable 0.3 uses the established JSON adapter. Verify cumulative angular displacement and yaw conventions before applying sphere-radius conversion. A physical tracker connection is not required to browse setup or inspect an existing run. Manual/autopilot movement is a simulation control, not a replacement measurement of the animal.

title: Browser monitoring
text: An ordinary static web page cannot open a raw ZMQ socket. A live browser dashboard requires a running bridge/subscriber on an authorized workstation/server, with an explicit browser transport and access configuration. GitHub Pages serves the documentation and downloads; it is not an acquisition server. Current source provides the live browser monitoring contract, including the context heartbeat and same-origin SSE bridge. The trajectory-dashboard project documents its browser/processing environment. Keep live monitoring separate from the durable run archive: bounded telemetry may omit snapshots and is not the full tracker stream.

title: Icons and project identity
text: The documentation uses locally bundled Lucide icons with the retained ISC license, following the icon library used in the HejjéTrac project. Rekkefly has its own custom application icon/native controls; this manual does not imply that its existing UI uses Lucide.

title: Source of truth
text: Use the linked repositories for their current builds and platform-specific dependencies. MATREX VR's accepted fields/units remain defined by ZmqListener and ClosedLoop. When a new integration changes a wire contract, record the exact revisions with the experiment and validate a known motion before collecting data.

title: Tracker backends and optional app launch
text: Current source connects Rekkefly flight tracking and HejjéTrac walking tracking to the existing per-rig ZMQ input. The live telemetry output goes to Daari Deepa. Tracker measurement ports and the MATREX telemetry output port are separate. A dashboard subscribes to telemetry; it does not feed movement back into Unity. The setup screen shows modern backend names. Rekkefly (enum 4) and Hejjetrac (enum 3) are explicit new config choices. Kinefly (1), FicTrac (0), and Tirbala (2) remain accepted; opening a file does not rewrite them. HejjéTrac and historical hejjetrak spelling are accepted input aliases. Real subject metadata uses AnimalID and SpeciesName; generated or replayed individuals remain agents.

title: Measurement wire contract
text: Rekkefly: one UTF-8 JSON frame, compatible with Kinefly. x is left wing angle, y is right wing angle, yaw is left minus right, all radians. Unity retains the raw radian signal for flight gains/auto trim. Additional tracker timestamp/frame fields are allowed. HejjéTrac: one UTF-8 frame beginning FT, followed by exactly 25 numeric CSV columns. Numeric columns 15/16 contain world forward/east position in sphere radians; 17 contains heading radians. Unity maps east to X and forward to Z, scales displacement by sphere radius in centimetres, and converts heading to quaternion degrees. Full upstream data remains in tracker recordings. Existing single JSON, two-frame topic+JSON, and separate legacy topic/JSON messages remain accepted. A topic-only message is ignored. Nonfinite/malformed measurements are rejected without publishing a partial pose. Explicit Hejjetrac mode uses walking interpretation. A native FT row also selects walking under the legacy FicTrac name. Historical FicTrac-named Bogong JSON retains its previous gain behavior. A walking FT row is rejected on a flight backend rather than being mistaken for wing angles. MATREX bundles NetMQ 4.0.1.13, AsyncIO 0.1.69 and NaCl.Net 0.1.13. This fixes the old 4.0.0.1 client's handshake with the native HejjéTrac publisher. Exact DLL hashes/frameworks and official package sources are in the transport manifest; licenses are in TrackerTransport. No tracker output algorithm or calibration is changed.

title: Optional native app buttons
text: In System details, expand a rig's Tracker field and choose Set value. Provide the absolute installed executable and an existing calibration/config file. MATREX never discovers/downloads executables and never launches them automatically. On macOS, use the binary inside the app's Contents/MacOS folder. Launch/Stop buttons appear for configured rigs in setup. An external tracker started by the operator continues to work normally. Example optional per-rig fields (merge into a complete existing system config): { "vrId": "VR1", "speciesName": "Drosophila melanogaster", "closedLoopMode": "Rekkefly", "zmqAddress": "127.0.0.1", "zmqPort": 9871, "tracker": { "executablePath": "/absolute/path/to/rekkefly", "configFile": "Trackers/VR1.toml", "device": "", "headless": false } } The launcher uses the audited Rekkefly 0.6.2 (2df99c3) supervision interface and HejjéTrac 94404c64 stdio interface. Older installed trackers can be started manually if they lack those launch flags. The launcher passes argv directly, without a shell. Relative tracker config paths resolve under the MATREX config root. Rekkefly receives --config FILE --label VRn --zmq-port PORT --supervised, with optional --device/--headless. Supervision disables fallback and supports stdin shutdown. HejjéTrac receives --config FILE --windows 1 --control-stdio, then a typed session 1 start request. Installed HejjéTrac packages name the desktop executable hejjetrac and the CLI hejjetrac-cli; a Cargo source build produces fictrac-desktop and fictrac. Its calibration config must set zmq_port to the same rig port and zmq_host to loopback; there is no port CLI override and MATREX never rewrites the calibration file. Device/source selection for HejjéTrac stays in that file. Only locally bound trackers can be launched by these optional buttons. Save calibration edits in the native tracker before Stop: MATREX asks its owned process to close, then terminates it if it does not exit promptly. Unrelated processes, including another instance of the same executable, are never stopped. Owned trackers persist across experiment scene transitions and stop when MATREX quits. Stop remains available if you clear an owned tracker’s optional launch fields. Applying a system configuration that removes or renames a rig stops only the process MATREX owned for that rig; changing the selected backend does not relabel a running process.

title: Native verification
text: The machine-readable native report records the exact measured scope. On macOS arm64/Unity 6000.3.16f1, real HejjéTrac processed 300 sample-video frames and Unity received all 300, alongside 100 legacy JSON frames. Current Rekkefly 0.6.2 processed 400 synthetic frames with simultaneous Unity and libzmq subscribers: both received 391 identical stream samples, with 9 frames missed during subscription startup and 0 publisher queue drops. This demonstrates live fanout, with normal PUB startup loss rather than a recording/replay guarantee. 150 listener shutdown cycles returned the worker count to 0 and kept OS thread count bounded. The telemetry probe also tests an external libzmq subscriber, Unicode metadata, schema 2 frames, and schema 1 context heartbeats at a faster independent cadence. This is not physical camera validation or a Windows/Linux execution claim. python3 tools/test_tracker_contracts.py passes 66 offline backend/decoder and native owned-process checks, including removal/rename, cleared launch fields, argument quoting and leaving unrelated processes running. tools/test_native_tracker_interop.py --help describes the optional real Unity/HejjéTrac probe; optional --rekkefly-bin/--rekkefly-config arguments add current Rekkefly fanout; it creates a separate tiny project and leaves the source checkout and tracker calibration files untouched. Python/pyzmq are development test dependencies, not requirements for running MATREX or the native trackers.

title: Cite the software
text: The repository provides a CITATION.cff file with verified software metadata. It identifies MATREX VR, Pavan Kumar Kaushik as named in the Git history, the repository and release version. No DOI or root license is invented.

title: Suggested software citation
text: Pavan Kumar Kaushik. MATREX VR, version 0.3.0. Software. https://github.com/pvnkmrksk/matrexVR Include the exact release tag or source commit used for acquisition, and retain that identity with the run. A source-modified renderer should cite its commit as well as the project. The software citation is distinct from any publication describing an experiment.

title: Stimulus and dependency credits
text: Generated astronomical sky stimuli use NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio's Deep Star Maps 2020, Ernie Wright (USRA), with Gaia DR2: ESA/Gaia/DPAC. The bundled Astronomy Engine source carries its MIT notice and pinned revision. Individual sky manifests record provenance and the represented UTC instant. Unity, NetMQ and bundled third-party assets retain their own terms and notices. The historical README identified MIT licensing, but the repository has no root LICENSE establishing a project-wide grant. This manual does not infer one from dependency licenses. Documentation icons are from Lucide, with the ISC license retained beside the local assets. Native gallery images carry their capture provenance. See sky preview provenance and the gallery.
